title: GSAP on Elementor 4.x sites without losing the score
summary: GSAP 3.15.0 (13 Apr 2026) is 100% free for commercial use, including every former Club plugin (ScrollTrigger, SplitText, MorphSVG, ScrollSmoother, Flip, DrawSVG, Draggable...), installable from public npm/jsDelivr/cdnjs under the "Standard no-charge" license. Measured gzip: core 28.3 KB + ScrollTrigger 18.0 KB + SplitText 3.7 KB = 50 KB; the all-in-one all.js is 184 KB gz and must never ship. Bytes are not the score problem; execution is: the agency's own platonos pays 1.78 s bootup / 358 ms TBT by running gsap+ScrollTrigger+SplitText at load. The pattern that keeps 95-100 is: self-host in the child theme, one tiny `type="module"` loader (WP 6.5 `wp_enqueue_script_module`) that dynamic-`import()`s GSAP only after the first scroll/pointer event or when the first `[data-anim]` element approaches, animates only below-the-fold elements that are visible by default (no CSS opacity:0, no `elementor-invisible`), uses transform/opacity-only tweens with `once:true`/`batch()`, wraps everything in `gsap.matchMedia()` with a `prefers-reduced-motion` condition, and keeps the loader out of every Delay-JS/combine layer (`type="module"` is skipped by LiteSpeed and Perfmatters, but WP Rocket delays it unless `nowprocket`, FlyingPress unless keyword-excluded). Lighthouse never scrolls and emulates reduced-motion=false, so below-fold scroll animations cost 0 in the lab; they still must be cheap for field INP. Avoid on these sites: ScrollSmoother/Lenis (scroll-jacking, wrapper DOM breaks Elementor sticky/popups/CMP, no gain on touch), pinning inside Elementor's flex containers without `pinSpacing:true`, pins under Motion-Effects transforms, GSAP on the same element as an Elementor entrance animation or Pro Interaction, SplitText on the LCP heading, and GSAP add-on packs. Elementor Pro Interactions (motion.min.js 42 KB gz, enqueued only on pages that use one) cover simple fade/slide/scale reveals without any custom code; GSAP is for orchestrated timelines, SplitText, SVG and pins. No published 90+ GSAP case study could be opened (GSAP forums offline, PSI quota exhausted); the real data points are the agency's own measurements.
critic_notes: Method: WebFetch had no DNS in this container (ENOTFOUND for every host), so every source was opened with curl through the proxy and converted to text locally; GSAP files were downloaded from jsDelivr and gzip -9 measured; Elementor/Pro runtime facts come from the published bundles on limnoupolis.gr (Elementor 4.3.5, Pro 4.3.1) and raw.githubusercontent.com. Not reachable: gsap.com/standard-license (302 to /offline/, forums still down), web.archive.org (connection reset), plugins.svn.wordpress.org (403; used api.wordpress.org instead), gh api for elementor/elementor (403, raw files worked), the ScrollTrigger normalizeScroll page (not re-opened; its scroll-jacking quote is taken from the researcher). Open questions updated: Q1 resolved at runtime level (per-interaction `breakpoints.excluded` honoured by interactions.min.js; panel UI unchecked); Q2 resolved (`elementor/popup/show|hide` as jQuery + window CustomEvent); Q4 still open (license text); Q7 mostly resolved (jQuery sticky with spacer and classes). New open item: whether Pro Interactions ignore prefers-reduced-motion (runtime shows no check; needs one Playwright run). Highest-impact changes for the plugin: remove the IntersectionObserver and pointer/click triggers from the loader, and never ship the npm-root ESM files. Skipped: no Lighthouse/Puppeteer run was executed in this phase (research-only), and no Novamira call was made; the risk the user must know is that the finding-3 loader as drafted can run GSAP inside the lab trace on pages whose first animated block sits in the second screen.

findings.claim: GSAP is free for all commercial use since 3.13 (29 Apr 2025), including every former Club plugin; current release is 3.15.0 (13 Apr 2026); install from public npm/jsDelivr/cdnjs, never from the retired private registry.
findings.detail: gsap.com/pricing: "GSAP is now 100% free for all users, thanks to Webflow's support". 3.13 release post: "100% FREE including ALL of the bonus plugins like SplitText, MorphSVG, and all the others that were exclusively available to Club GSAP members ... even for commercial use"; "Please move off the private repository by June 1, 2025". npm registry `gsap@latest` = 3.15.0, license field: "Standard 'no charge' license: https://gsap.com/standard-license". Release dates from registry: 3.13.0 2025-04-30, 3.14.0 2025-12-08 (MorphSVG `smooth`, `curveMode`), 3.15.0 2026-04-13 (`easeReverse`, deprecates `yoyoEase`). Free plugin set now in the public package: ScrollTrigger, ScrollSmoother, ScrollTo, SplitText, ScrambleText, Text, Flip, Draggable, Inertia, Observer, MorphSVG, DrawSVG, MotionPath, MotionPathHelper, Physics2D, PhysicsProps, CustomEase/Bounce/Wiggle, GSDevTools, EaselPlugin, PixiPlugin. The gsap.com/standard-license page currently redirects to the forums, which are offline (PHP vulnerability notice), so the license text itself could not be read today; the npm metadata and pricing page are the opened sources.
findings.breaks_when: A build still points `.npmrc` at npm.greensock.com (installs fail) or ships a pre-3.13 Club build whose license text forbids redistribution in a theme; or a site uses an old gsap.min.js 3.12 that lacks the free SplitText rewrite and `easeReverse`.
findings.how_to_apply: Pin `gsap@3.15.0` in the child theme (download dist/*.min.js from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.15.0/dist/ or `npm i gsap@3.15.0`), commit the files under `wp-content/themes/CHILD/js/vendor/gsap/`, remove any `@gsap:registry` lines from .npmrc. Document the license as the GSAP Standard no-charge license.
findings.how_to_verify: `curl -s https://registry.npmjs.org/gsap/latest | jq '.version,.license'` returns 3.15.0 and the Standard license string; in the browser console `gsap.version` prints "3.15.0" and `gsap.plugins.ScrollTrigger`/`SplitText` are defined after registerPlugin.

findings.claim: Byte budget per module (3.15.0, measured gzip -9): core 28.3 KB, ScrollTrigger 18.0 KB, SplitText 3.7 KB, ScrollSmoother 5.5 KB, Flip 9.7 KB, MorphSVG 9.6 KB, DrawSVG 2.2 KB; the all-in-one `all.js` is 184 KB gz and must never be shipped; self-host the files you use, do not load from a CDN.
findings.detail: Downloaded from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.15.0/dist/: gsap.min.js 72,927 B raw / 28,268 gz; ScrollTrigger.min.js 44,575 / 17,998 (bundles Observer); SplitText.min.js 7,732 / 3,658; ScrollSmoother.min.js 13,373 / 5,545; Flip.min.js 25,534 / 9,706; MorphSVGPlugin.min.js 21,195 / 9,553; DrawSVGPlugin.min.js 4,351 / 2,211; Observer.min.js 10,014 / 4,320; ScrollToPlugin.min.js 4,059 / 1,962; MotionPathPlugin.min.js 22,002 / 9,706; TextPlugin.min.js 10,570 / 3,561; CustomEase.min.js 7,143 / 3,673; Draggable.min.js 35,762 / 13,490; InertiaPlugin.min.js 7,335 / 3,260; all.js 808,273 / 183,709. Typical reveal stack core+ScrollTrigger = 46.3 KB gz; with SplitText 49.9 KB. jsDelivr serves `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and brotli (29,312 B for core), cdnjs and unpkg host the same 3.15.0 files. But Chrome partitions the HTTP cache by top-level site since Chrome 86 ("cached resources will be keyed using a new Network Isolation Key ... composed of the top-level site and the current-frame site"), so a CDN copy is never 'already cached' from another site, and a CDN origin is a third party in Lighthouse's third-parties audit, eating the plugin's 150 KB third-party budget (sites-in-the-wild rule 6) and costing an extra DNS+TLS connection. The npm package is ESM with `"sideEffects": false`, `"module": "index.js"`; for bundler builds import `gsap` and `gsap/ScrollTrigger` only and call `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger)` so tree-shaking does not drop the plugin (Installation FAQ).
findings.breaks_when: `all.js`/`all.min.js` or the UMD bundle of every plugin is loaded (184 KB gz, 800 KB parse); GSAP is pulled from jsdelivr/cdnjs (third-party budget, extra connection, no cross-site cache); a plugin is imported but not registered in a bundler build (production build silently drops it).
findings.how_to_apply: Child theme: `js/vendor/gsap/gsap.min.js`, `ScrollTrigger.min.js`, optional `SplitText.min.js`; or build an ESM entry `js/motion.js` with `import gsap from 'gsap'; import { ScrollTrigger } from 'gsap/ScrollTrigger'; gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger);`. Load only on pages that have animated elements (finding 3). Never add Flip/Draggable/MotionPath unless a component uses them.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse `network-requests`: only first-party `/wp-content/themes/CHILD/js/...gsap*` entries, each under the sizes above, and none before LCP; `third-parties-insight` lists no cdn.jsdelivr.net/cdnjs/unpkg; `bootup-time` has no gsap entry over 100 ms on the mobile run.
findings.correction: Budget line: core+ScrollTrigger 46.3 KB gz holds only for dist/*.min.js (UMD) or an esbuild-bundled ESM build; never copy the npm root *.js ESM files into the theme. Replace '184 KB all.js' with 'all.min.js 124 KB gz / 334 KB parse'.

findings.claim: The score-safe loading pattern: GSAP is never in the load path. One ~400 B `type="module"` loader (WP 6.5 `wp_enqueue_script_module`) dynamic-`import()`s GSAP only after the first scroll/pointer event or when the first `[data-anim]` element is within 300 px; animated elements are visible by default and only below the fold, so the lab run (which never scrolls) executes zero GSAP and real users get it before they reach it.
findings.breaks_when: A `from()` target is inside the first viewport at load (it would snap to its start state when GSAP arrives mid-scroll: visible jump; skip-if-on-screen guard above prevents it); a stylesheet pre-hides animated elements (content invisible when JS is delayed or fails; LCP element can vanish); the loader is combined/delayed by a cache plugin (finding 10); GSAP is enqueued classic-style on `load` (TBT, platonos pattern); the module is printed in `<head>` without `type=module` (blocks parsing).
findings.how_to_apply: Child theme only (never an HTML widget script per design-to-elementor.md); add `[data-anim]` to at most 20 below-fold elements per page (rule 13); Novamira: set the attribute in the element's `attributes` (v4) or `_attributes` (v3) when writing the tree; purge cache; shoot at 390 px.
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse median of 3: `network-requests` has no `gsap` or `motion.js` entry (loader only, <1 KB); `bootup-time`/`long-tasks` unchanged vs. the static build; LCP element unchanged, Render Delay < 300 ms. Then a Puppeteer timespan that scrolls to the bottom: gsap files load after the first scroll, no long task > 50 ms, no console errors; `document.querySelectorAll('[data-anim]')` elements end at `opacity:1`. Playwright with `reducedMotion:'reduce'` shows the same final layout.
findings.correction: Loader: drop the IntersectionObserver; start only on scroll/wheel/touchmove/keydown (`{once:true, passive:true}`); the on-screen guard in motion.js already handles deep links and short pages. motion.js: either build it once with `npx esbuild src/motion.js --bundle --minify --format=esm --outfile=js/motion.js` (tree-shaken core+ScrollTrigger about 46 KB gz) or, with no build step, `await import('./vendor/gsap/gsap.min.js'); await import('./vendor/gsap/ScrollTrigger.min.js'); const {gsap, ScrollTrigger} = window;` — the 3.15.0 UMD wrapper is `(t=t||self).window=t.window||{}` so it attaches to window even when evaluated as a module. Resolve the import path with `new URL('./motion.js?v=1', import.meta.url)` instead of a hard-coded theme path.

findings.claim: Keep ScrollTrigger cheap: transform/opacity only, `once:true` for reveals, `ScrollTrigger.batch()` for grids, `limitCallbacks`/`ignoreMobileResize` config, function-based start/end with `invalidateOnRefresh`, no `markers` in production, create triggers in DOM order; never animate height/width/top/left/filter or set `will-change` on pinned ancestors.
findings.detail: web.dev animations guide: 'Avoid any property that triggers layout or paint unless it's absolutely necessary'; use `transform` (translate/scale/rotate) and `opacity`; `will-change` 'only if you notice graphics issues', and 'remove the property when the change has stopped'. Lighthouse flags non-composited animations ('Avoid non-composited animations' audit reads Chrome's compositor failure reasons per DOM node; composited animations are excluded from CLS). ScrollTrigger docs: it 'does NOT constantly watch every element ... It ONLY watches the scroll position', debounces scroll to rAF, waits for a 200 ms gap before refreshing on resize; `once: true` kills the trigger at end, 'eligible for garbage collection', sets toggleActions to 'play none none none'; `ScrollTrigger.batch(".card", { interval: 0.1, batchMax: 3, once: true, onEnter: b => gsap.to(b, { autoAlpha: 1, y: 0, stagger: 0.15, overwrite: true }) })` replaces N IntersectionObservers; `ScrollTrigger.config({ limitCallbacks: true, ignoreMobileResize: true })` (ignoreMobileResize skips refresh on the 25 % vertical resize of the mobile address bar, 'avoiding the jumps'); `end: () => '+=' + el.offsetHeight` plus `invalidateOnRefresh: true` so resize keeps values right; 'always create things in the order they'll happen on the page' (pinned triggers shift later ones) or use `refreshPriority`; `fastScrollEnd`/`preventOverlaps` for fast flicks; GSAP's `force3D: "auto"` already promotes to a layer during the tween and drops back to 2D afterwards. GSAP CSS plugin: use `x`, `y`, `xPercent`, `scale` aliases (direct matrix writes) rather than `transform:` strings (parsed every tick). GSAP's ticker auto-sleeps after 120 idle frames (`autoSleep: 120` in gsap-core.js), so an idle GSAP page has no rAF loop, unlike Lenis/custom rAF loops (INP risk per rule 13). Scrub: `scrub: 0.5–1` (one second catch-up) is smoother than `true` on a 4x CPU; `start: 'clamp(top bottom)'` prevents partially-scrubbed states for elements near page top.
findings.breaks_when: Tweens on `height`, `width`, `top`, `left`, `margin`, `filter: blur()` or `background-position` (layout/paint per frame, Lighthouse non-composited audit fails, janky on moto g class phones); `will-change: transform` left on a pinned element's ancestor (breaks `position: fixed` pinning: 'browsers treat it just like having a transform applied'); hundreds of individual ScrollTriggers with onEnter callbacks instead of `batch()`; `markers: true` shipped to production; hard-coded pixel `end` values on responsive layouts.
findings.how_to_apply: Lint motion.js: allowed tween props `x,y,xPercent,yPercent,scale,rotation,opacity,autoAlpha,clipPath` (clip-path is paint but cheap for masks) and nothing else; every reveal uses `once: true` or `batch({once:true})`; one `ScrollTrigger.config()` at the top; `gsap.defaults({ ease: 'power2.out', duration: 0.8 })`; a build flag strips `markers`.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse `non-composited-animations` audit passes (0 nodes); DevTools Performance recording while scrolling a mobile emulation: Rendering/Painting near zero during tweens, no frame > 16.7 ms attributed to Recalculate Style/Layout; Rendering tab FPS meter > 95 % frames; `ScrollTrigger.getAll().length` falls as `once` triggers complete.

findings.claim: Target Elementor markup through stable hooks you own: Pro Custom Attributes (`data-anim|fade-up`) on v3 elements, the General-tab Attribute section (`attributes` prop) on v4 atomic elements, and v4 Global Classes; never GSAP-select by `elementor-element-{id}`/`data-id`, generic `.e-con`, or widget internals; run after Elementor's `frontend/element_ready/global` hook for dynamic content and skip the editor.
findings.detail: element-base.php renders every v3 element wrapper with `class="elementor-element elementor-element-{id}" data-id="{id}" data-element_type=... data-e-type=...` (+`data-settings` JSON and `elementor-invisible` when `_animation`/`animation` is set); the 8-char id changes when a template is imported or a section is duplicated, so selectors by id rot. div-block.php (v4) renders `class="e-con e-atomic-element {base-style-class} ...settings.classes"` where `classes` are the Global Classes and `attributes` (Attributes_Prop_Type) are the custom attributes; Elementor help (25 Sep 2026): v3 'Advanced > Attributes ... key|value, e.g. data-spots|round' and v4 'General tab > Attribute section > + ... Name / Value (dynamic tags are supported)'. So: `data-anim="fade-up"`, `data-anim-delay="0.1"` are set by the designer or by Novamira in `settings.attributes`, and GSAP selects `[data-anim]`. v4 Global Classes are the second stable hook (`.card-feature` → batch reveal). For AJAX-loaded content (Loop Grid pagination, popups) Elementor fires `elementorFrontend.hooks.doAction('frontend/element_ready/global', $scope, $)` for every element and `frontend/element_ready/{widgetType}` (elements-handlers-manager.js) — register `elementorFrontend.hooks.addAction('frontend/element_ready/global', ($scope) => { ctx.add(() => initReveals($scope[0])); ScrollTrigger.refresh(); })` after `window.addEventListener('elementor/frontend/init', ...)` (frontend.js dispatches it). `elementorFrontend.isEditMode()` (frontend.js) / `body.elementor-editor-active` guards keep GSAP out of the editor preview where it would fight live edits.
findings.breaks_when: Selectors hard-coded to `.elementor-element-7a3f9c1` break on import/duplicate; `.e-con` selectors animate every container including the hero; GSAP inits once on `DOMContentLoaded` and misses Loop Grid 'load more' items or popup content (unanimated or stuck at `autoAlpha:0` if pre-set); GSAP runs inside the editor iframe and leaves inline transforms on elements the designer is styling.
findings.how_to_apply: Design-to-Elementor lint: every animated node has `data-anim` (whitelist of preset names) and no `_animation`/`interactions`; motion.js reads presets from attributes: `{ 'fade-up': { y: 32, autoAlpha: 0 }, 'fade': { autoAlpha: 0 }, 'scale-in': { scale: 0.96, autoAlpha: 0 }, 'stagger-children': ... }`; Novamira: write `attributes` on the atomic element; v3 `_attributes: "data-anim|fade-up"`.
findings.how_to_verify: `document.querySelectorAll('[data-anim]').length` equals the plan (≤ 20); none of them is inside the first top-level container; after clicking Loop Grid 'Load more' the new items animate and `ScrollTrigger.getAll()` grew; in the editor (`?elementor`) no inline `transform`/`opacity` styles appear on the preview elements.

findings.claim: Never put GSAP and an Elementor entrance animation, Motion Effect or Pro Interaction on the same element, and never animate an element whose ancestor has a Motion Effect transform; GSAP targets also need `transition: none` for the properties GSAP drives.
findings.detail: element-base.php adds `elementor-invisible` (visibility:hidden) to any element with `_animation`/`animation` set; Elementor's own JS removes it on viewport entry, so a GSAP `from({autoAlpha:0})` on the same node either never shows (if Elementor JS is delayed) or double-animates. Help 'Entrance animations' lists 37 CSS keyframe animations and says reduced-motion disables them; breakage-checklist.md notes reduced motion 'never removes elementor-invisible'. Motion Effects 'Scrolling Effects' (Vertical/Horizontal Scroll, Transparency, Blur, Rotate, Scale) are JS-driven transforms/filters on the element; ScrollTrigger docs: a 'transform or will-change on an ancestor element ... breaks position: fixed behavior', so a pin inside a Motion-Effects container shifts and 'moves with the scroll' (`pinReparent: true` is the expensive bail-out). GSAP common mistakes: 'definitely avoid having CSS transitions applied to elements that you're animating with GSAP ... the browser would constantly be interrupting things' and a 1 s tween under a 1 s transition finishes after two seconds. Elementor widget styles ship transitions (e.g. button/image hover `transition`), so pinned or tweened Elementor elements need `transition: none` on the GSAP-driven properties. Plugin rule 13 already requires zero animation above the fold; with GSAP that means zero `[data-anim]`, zero `_animation`, zero `interactions` in the first top-level container and header.
findings.breaks_when: Element has both `_animation: fadeIn` and `data-anim` (stays `visibility:hidden` under Delay-JS; cretaforums/voreniahorizon render-delay pattern); pin target lives inside a container with Scrolling Effects (pin jumps); a tweened Elementor button has `transition: all .3s` (tween duration doubles, stutters); SplitText/GSAP applied to the LCP h1 (Render Delay).
findings.how_to_apply: Lint per element: exactly one of {`_animation`/`animation` != none, non-empty `interactions`, `data-anim`}; none in the first section/header; motion CSS: `[data-anim], [data-pin] * { transition: none !important; }` scoped to transform/opacity (`transition-property: color, background-color, border-color`) so hover colour transitions survive; pin only containers with no Motion Effects on any ancestor (`motion_fx_motion_fx_scrolling` unset).
findings.how_to_verify: At load, `document.querySelectorAll('.elementor-invisible[data-anim]').length === 0`; `getComputedStyle(el).transitionProperty` on every `[data-anim]` excludes transform/opacity; pinned element's ancestors have `transform: none` and no `will-change`; LCP node in Lighthouse has no `elementor-invisible`, no `data-anim`.

findings.claim: Wrap all GSAP setup in `gsap.matchMedia()` with a `prefers-reduced-motion` condition and a pointer/width condition, and in `gsap.context()` for cleanup; under reduced motion set the end state (`duration: 0`) rather than skipping, because Lighthouse emulates reduced-motion=false and real users with the preference must still see content.
findings.detail: gsap.matchMedia() docs: `mm.add({ isDesktop: '(min-width: 800px)', isMobile: '(max-width: 799px)', reduceMotion: '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)' }, (context) => { let { isDesktop, reduceMotion } = context.conditions; gsap.to('.box', { rotation: isDesktop ? 360 : 180, duration: reduceMotion ? 0 : 2 }); return () => {/* custom cleanup */} })` — 'when it no longer matches, all the GSAP animations and ScrollTriggers created during that function's execution get reverted automatically'; the handler re-runs on every toggle, and `mm.revert()` reverts everything. gsap.context(): 'Collects all GSAP animations and ScrollTriggers ... so that you can easily revert() or kill() ALL of them at once', optional scope element so selector text only matches descendants, `ctx.add(() => ...)` to register later animations (AJAX content, popups). Lighthouse's emulation has reduced-motion and Save-Data false (levers.md 7.1, citing Lighthouse constants.js), so the mobile branch of your matchMedia runs in the lab: keep it empty or cheap, and gate heavy effects (pins, SplitText chars, parallax) on `(pointer: fine) and (min-width: 1025px)` rather than on reduced motion. SplitText 'Integrates seamlessly with GSAP's context(), matchMedia()'.
findings.breaks_when: Reduced-motion branch does nothing and targets are pre-hidden (invisible content for those users); desktop pin/parallax runs in the 412 px Lighthouse run because it was gated only on `prefers-reduced-motion`; ScrollTriggers are not reverted when a popup closes or a resize crosses the breakpoint (duplicate triggers, wrong start/end).
findings.how_to_apply: motion.js skeleton: `const mm = gsap.matchMedia(); mm.add({ fine: '(pointer: fine) and (min-width: 1025px)', reduce: '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)' }, ctx => { const { fine, reduce } = ctx.conditions; const d = reduce ? 0 : 1; /* reveals for all */ if (fine) { /* pins, parallax, SplitText chars */ } });` Popups: `jQuery(document).on('elementor/popup/show', (e, id, popup) => ctx.add(() => initReveals(popup.$element[0])))` (Pro event name taken from the agency's existing code; verify against the installed Pro version) and `ScrollTrigger.refresh()` on hide.
findings.how_to_verify: Playwright project with `reducedMotion: 'reduce'`: all `[data-anim]` end at `opacity: 1`, screenshot equals the static baseline; resize the viewport across 1024/1025 px: `ScrollTrigger.getAll().length` is stable (no doubling); Lighthouse mobile run shows no `pin-spacer` elements in the DOM snapshot.

findings.claim: Cache-plugin Delay-JS and combine layers must skip the module loader and GSAP files: LiteSpeed and Perfmatters leave `type="module"` alone by design, WP Rocket delays it unless `nowprocket`, FlyingPress unless keyword-excluded; never let GSAP be combined or delayed twice.
findings.detail: LiteSpeed optimize.cls.php `_parse_js`: `if (!empty($attrs['type']) && $attrs['type'] != 'text/javascript') { continue; }` (modules and JSON untouched), also skips `nomodule`, `data-no-optimize` (non-empty), `data-cfasync="false"`, and in Delayed+Combine mode `data-no-defer` or anything matching 'JS Deferred/Delayed Excludes'; delayed classic scripts are rewritten to `type="litespeed/javascript" data-src=...` and run on user activity ('Delayed runs the JS only after detecting user activity'); docs: `data-no-defer="1"` or filter `litespeed_optm_gm_js_exc` for Guest Mode; 'JS Delayed Includes' deprecated in 7.9.2. WP Rocket: 'On all JavaScript, either with a src attribute or not, a type="text/rocketlazyloadscript" attribute will be added ... If a script already has a type value, it will be copied in a data-rocket-type attribute' → a `type="module"` loader IS delayed; exclusion by keyword list or 'adding the nowprocket attribute'; triggers: keydown, mousemove, touchstart, wheel, click, scroll...; combine is disabled when Delay is on. Perfmatters: Delay 'should work with a script tag with either the type='javascript' or no type' (module scripts untouched); 'Delay all scripts' + 'Excluded from delay' keyword list (match on src URL or any inline string); common Elementor exclusions listed. FlyingPress: 'All scripts are delayed unless excluded', partial case-insensitive keyword on the whole `<script>` tag (`motion-loader`, `/themes/CHILD/`); its 'Load after interaction' mode is 'not suitable if your site has sliders, animations, menus ... above-the-fold'. Why exclude rather than rely on Delay-JS: the loader already gates itself; a second gate means GSAP arrives mid-scroll after the first `[data-anim]` is on screen, and Delay-JS 'forced execution' is what the plugin's rule 2 measures. Combining a module into a classic bundle breaks `import('./vendor/...')` relative resolution.
findings.breaks_when: WP Rocket Delay without `nowprocket` on the loader (GSAP never loads for a user who only scrolls with the keyboard? — scroll is a trigger, so mostly late, not never; but LiteSpeed Delayed + Combine without `data-no-defer` bundles the ESM entry into a classic file: SyntaxError on `import`); FlyingPress keyword list missing the theme path; Perfmatters 'Delay all' with Elementor without the documented Elementor exclusions (`frontend.min.js`, `webpack.runtime.min.js`, `elementorFrontendConfig`...) so `elementorFrontend` is undefined when motion.js registers `frontend/element_ready` hooks.
findings.how_to_apply: Print loader with `nowprocket data-no-optimize="1" data-no-defer="1"` (filter `wp_script_attributes`/`wp_inline_script_attributes`); add keyword `motion-loader` and `/js/vendor/gsap/` to FlyingPress 'Exclude' and Perfmatters 'Excluded from Delay' and WP Rocket 'Excluded JavaScript Files'; LiteSpeed: 'JS Deferred/Delayed Excludes' += `motion-loader.js`, keep JS Combine OFF (plugin baseline).
findings.how_to_verify: View source of a cached page: the loader tag still reads `<script type="module" src=".../motion-loader.js">` (no `text/rocketlazyloadscript`, `litespeed/javascript`, `data-src`, `data-rocket-src`); after a cold load with no gesture, no gsap request; after one wheel event, `motion.js` + gsap files load with 200 and no console SyntaxError; `elementorFrontend.hooks` exists before motion.js runs.
findings.correction: Remove the unverified LiteSpeed 7.9.2 deprecation note; state FlyingPress module handling as 'undocumented — always exclude by keyword'. Everything else stands.

findings.claim: Pinning in Elementor needs care: Elementor containers are display:flex so ScrollTrigger sets `pinSpacing:false` by default (content scrolls under the pin), pins use `position: fixed` which any ancestor transform breaks, and the Pro sticky header must sit outside the pinned tree; keep pins desktop-only and scrub ≥ 0.5.
findings.detail: ScrollTrigger docs: 'if the container is display: flex, pinSpacing is set to false by default'; 'Warning don't animate the pinned element itself ... animate only elements INSIDE the pinned element'; 'you probably have a transform or will-change on an ancestor element which breaks position: fixed behavior ... pinReparent: true can bail you out ... reparenting can be expensive'; `pinType: 'fixed'` default for body scroller — 'position: fixed seemed to deliver better performance overall'; `anticipatePin: 1` to avoid the one-frame flash of unpinned content on fast scroll; nested pins need `pinnedContainer`; pins change the page height, so 'always create things in the order they'll happen' or use `refreshPriority`. Elementor's `.e-con` is a flex container and Motion Effects add transforms (finding 6), and Pro Sticky adds a fixed header — a header inside a pinned ancestor stops sticking. On touch, pinning plus the address-bar resize causes jumps unless `ScrollTrigger.config({ ignoreMobileResize: true })`. Cost: each scrubbed pin runs a tween per frame while active and a layout recalculation on every refresh; on a 4x-throttled moto g this is the budget killer, and Lighthouse (no scroll) will not show it — field INP will.
findings.breaks_when: `pin: true` on an `.e-con` without `pinSpacing: true` (following sections slide under the pinned one); pinned section nested in a container with Scrolling Effects or `will-change` (jitter/jump); sticky header inside the pinned subtree; pins enabled on phones (address-bar refresh jumps, long frames); pin created after a later trigger (wrong start/end for everything below).
findings.how_to_apply: Only inside `mm.add('(pointer: fine) and (min-width: 1025px)')`; wrap the pinned block in a plain `<div class="pin-wrap">` (v4 e-div-block with `display:block` style) and pin that; `ScrollTrigger.create({ trigger: '.pin-wrap', pin: true, pinSpacing: true, anticipatePin: 1, start: 'top top', end: '+=150%', scrub: 0.8 })`; one pin per page; verify no Motion Effects on ancestors; header remains a Theme Builder header outside `main`.
findings.how_to_verify: Desktop: scroll through the pinned range — no jump at pin start/end, next section begins exactly after unpin (`.pin-spacer` height correct); header stays sticky; mobile emulation: no `.pin-spacer` present; DevTools Performance during the pinned range: no Layout events per frame.

findings.claim: Do not use ScrollSmoother or Lenis on these sites: both require a page-wide wrapper that breaks `position: fixed` elements (Elementor sticky header, popups, WhatsApp/CMP banners), neither smooths touch by default so phones pay the setup for no effect, `normalizeScroll` is 'a hybrid form of scroll-jacking', and the plugin already classifies smooth-scroll before LCP as a blocker (rule 13).
findings.detail: ScrollSmoother docs: content must live in `#smooth-wrapper > #smooth-content`, and 'position: fixed should be outside the wrapper — since the content has a CSS transform applied, browsers create a new containing block and that means position: fixed elements will be fixed to the content rather than the viewport'; Elementor prints header, footer and popups inside the body content, so they would have to be moved out of the wrapper by JS. 'by default, ScrollSmoother will NOT apply scroll smoothing on touch-only devices (like phones)' (`smoothTouch` opt-in); `normalizeScroll: true` 'forces scrolling to be done on the JavaScript thread' and 'doesn't prevent the address bar from hiding/showing on iOS phones in portrait'; normalizeScroll docs call it 'experimental' and 'a hybrid form of scroll-jacking'. Lenis README: integrates via `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update); gsap.ticker.add(t => lenis.raf(t*1000)); gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)` — a permanent rAF loop; `allowNestedScroll` 'checks the DOM tree on every scroll event' (perf warning), `naiveDimensions` 'has a performance impact'; `respectReducedMotion` default true. Corpus: andreas-stricker.at runs `smooth-scrolling-with-lenis` and scored 39-68 with Lenis named a TBT contributor; rule 13: 'Lenis/smooth-scroll before LCP are blockers'. GSAP's `scrollerProxy()` exists for third-party smoothers but 'We don't support other libraries'.
findings.breaks_when: Any smooth-scroll library is active on mobile (rAF loop + transform of the whole content = TBT/INP, address-bar jumps, pinch-zoom conflicts); Elementor sticky header/popup/CMP inside the smoothed wrapper (they scroll away or are unclickable); `scroll-behavior: smooth` in CSS alongside ScrollTrigger (start/end markers drift on resize per st-mistakes).
findings.how_to_apply: Policy: no ScrollSmoother/Lenis/Locomotive in the build skill; if a brief insists on 'smooth' feel, use `scrub: 1` on scroll-linked tweens (the 'catch-up' feel without scroll-jacking) and `data-speed`-style parallax via a transform tween on inner images desktop-only. Add `html { scroll-behavior: auto }` when a theme sets smooth.
findings.how_to_verify: No `#smooth-wrapper`, `lenis`, `locomotive`, `ScrollSmoother` strings in the HTML/network log; `document.documentElement.classList` has no `lenis` classes; no continuous rAF task in a 5-second idle Performance recording; CrUX INP p75 under 200 ms after 28 days.

findings.claim: SplitText 3.13+ is the right tool for text reveals below the fold: 3.7 KB gz, `autoSplit:true` + `onSplit` re-splits when fonts load, `mask:'lines'`, automatic aria; but never on the LCP heading, only `lines, words` (not chars) on phones, and only after `document.fonts.ready`.
findings.detail:
3.13 rewrite: '50% smaller, 14 new features'; docs: 'to maximize performance you should really only split what you need'; `autoSplit: true` 're-split whenever the fonts finish loading or when ... the width of the split element(s) changes and lines are split' and 'SplitText will even console.warn() you if you try splitting before the fonts finish loading and you didn't set autoSplit: true'; 'make sure to create any animations in an onSplit() callback ... If you return the animation in the onSplit(), SplitText will automatically clean up and synchronize'; `mask: "lines"` wraps lines in a clipping element; `aria: "auto"` adds aria-label to the split element and aria-hidden to pieces (links inside lose semantics → use `aria:'hidden'` + visually hidden copy). Splitting rewrites innerHTML into many spans (DOM nodes count against rule 15's 1,500-node budget) and re-splits on font load; on the hero `h1` that shifts the LCP candidate and adds render delay (platonos's 1.78 s bootup includes SplitText at load). Pattern:
```js
if (fine) document.fonts.ready.then(() => document.querySelectorAll('[data-anim="lines"]').forEach(el => SplitText.create(el, { type: 'lines, words', mask: 'lines', autoSplit: true, onSplit: s => gsap.from(s.words, { yPercent: 110, duration: 0.9, stagger: 0.03, ease: 'power3.out', scrollTrigger: { trigger: el, start: 'top 85%', once: true } }) })));
```
Greek text splits correctly (improved 'foreign character support'); `prepareText()` exists for languages without spaces.
findings.breaks_when: SplitText on the hero h1/p (LCP element rewritten, Render Delay, FOUC on font swap); `type: 'chars'` on long Greek paragraphs on phones (hundreds of spans, long task); splitting before fonts load without autoSplit (wrong line breaks); animating `s.lines` created before a re-split (orphaned tweens) instead of returning the tween from `onSplit`.
findings.how_to_apply: Allow `data-anim="lines"` only on h2/h3 below the fold, ≤ 3 per page, desktop-only (`fine`) or `lines`-only on phones; load `SplitText.min.js` inside the same dynamic import chunk; keep `font-display: swap` + preloaded heading woff2 (rule 11) so `fonts.ready` resolves early.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse LCP element is unchanged and has no `aria-label` injected by SplitText; DOM node count delta after split < 150; console shows no SplitText font warning; resize across a breakpoint re-splits without duplicated words (`el.textContent` equals the original).
findings.correction: Add to how_to_verify: run the breakage-checklist scroll CLS gate (buffered layout-shift observer) on pages with data-anim="lines" and fail on any shift whose source is a split heading; keep `mask:'lines'` off on headings with 3+ lines on phones.

findings.claim: Elementor Pro Interactions (Editor V4) cost 42 KB gz of motion.min.js + handler only on pages that have at least one interaction, offer Fade/Slide/Scale with Page-load / Scroll-into-view / While-scrolling / Hover / Click triggers, and are the right tool for simple reveals; GSAP is for everything they cannot do — but never both libraries for the same job on one page.
findings.detail: modules/interactions/module.php registers `motion-js` (`assets/lib/motion/motion.min.js`, version 11.13.5 — the Motion library) and `elementor-interactions` on `elementor/frontend/after_register_scripts`; interactions-frontend-handler.php collects interactions through `elementor/frontend/builder_content_data` (header, footer, post content, cached in postmeta) and in `wp_footer` priority 1 calls `enqueue_interactions_assets()` only `if (!empty($elements_with_interactions))`, then prints `<script type="application/json" id="elementor-interactions-data">`; measured on limnoupolis.gr: motion.min.js 128,346 B raw / 42,160 B gzip — comparable to GSAP core + ScrollTrigger (46.3 KB). Help (19 Jun 2026): triggers 'Page load, Scroll into view, While scrolling (start and end point), On hover, On click'; effects 'Fade, Slide, Scale', In/Out, duration/delay; and 'Interactions apply to all devices, you cannot customize interactions for different screen sizes' — whereas the 4.0 developers update (19 Mar 2026) promised 'dedicated breakpoint controls, allowing you to simplify or disable complex motion for mobile users' and module.php ships `breakpoints` in its config, so per-device behaviour must be verified on the installed 4.3.x. Interactions are JS-driven and fire on load for 'Page load' triggers, so design-to-elementor.md's rule stands: none in the first screen, ≤ 2 per page. Novamira has `elementor-add-interaction` for them. Decision rule for the build skill: single-element fade/slide/scale reveal → Interaction (no custom code, editor-visible, cached postmeta); staggered groups, timelines, SplitText, pins, SVG draw/morph, Flip layout changes, scroll-linked parallax with easing → GSAP; a page should load motion.min.js or GSAP, not both (≈ 88 KB gz and two animation engines fighting on shared elements).
findings.breaks_when: A 'Page load' interaction sits on an above-the-fold element (JS-dependent paint, same class of problem as `elementor-invisible`); interactions and `data-anim` on one element; both motion.min.js and GSAP loaded on a page for a handful of reveals; relying on per-breakpoint interactions that the help says do not exist.
findings.how_to_apply: Lint: `interactions` arrays non-empty only below the first section and ≤ 2 per page; if any element has `data-anim`, the page uses GSAP for all its reveals (set no interactions); if the page's motion is ≤ 2 simple reveals, use interactions and skip the GSAP loader (`[data-anim]` absent → loader does nothing).
findings.how_to_verify: Pages without interactions: no `motion.min.js` or `interactions.min.js` in the network log and no `#elementor-interactions-data` script; pages with them: both load deferred/in footer and the first-screen elements have no interaction entries; check whether the installed Pro 4.3 panel offers breakpoint toggles for an interaction and record the answer in the reference.
findings.correction: Replace 'per-device behaviour must be verified' with: each interaction item carries `breakpoints.excluded` (array of breakpoint labels) honoured by interactions.min.js on 4.3.5; the build skill may exclude 'mobile'/'mobile_extra' per interaction, and the lint should treat a page-load interaction without mobile excluded as a mobile-affecting animation.

findings.claim: Per-page delivery: prefer the child-theme loader that no-ops when the page has no `[data-anim]`; Elementor Pro Custom Code (location `<body> – End`, priority 1-10, Display Conditions) is the no-code fallback for printing the same `<script type="module">` on selected pages, not a place for animation code.
findings.detail: Elementor help 'Add custom code' (14 Jan 2024): HTML/JS/CSS snippets, 'Custom code does not support PHP'; Location options `<head>`, `<body> – Start`, `<body> – End`; Priority 1-10, 'Lower numbers indicate higher priority'; Conditions via Publish > Conditions > Edit, 'the same way as display conditions for global templates' (entire site, singular, archive, specific pages); built-in linter. Custom Code is Pro-only, stored as a CPT and printed into the HTML like any other inline script, so cache plugins process it (finding 10 exclusions apply) and inline JS there cannot be a module with relative imports unless written as `<script type="module" src="/wp-content/themes/CHILD/js/motion-loader.js" nowprocket data-no-optimize="1"></script>`. design-to-elementor.md already bans `<script>` in HTML widgets (per-document CSS/JS, uncached, in the DOM). The attribute-presence check in the loader (`document.querySelector('[data-anim]')`) scopes GSAP to exactly the pages that use it with zero per-page configuration and works across Polylang/WPML translations (conditions would need both languages' pages).
findings.breaks_when: Animation code lives in Custom Code set to Entire Site with `<head>` location (runs before Elementor's frontend, blocks parsing, not versioned); Custom Code conditions list only the Greek page and the English translation animates nothing or errors; inline Custom Code is delayed by WP Rocket (no `nowprocket` possible on inline? — it is possible on inline tags too per WP Rocket docs) and executes mid-scroll.
findings.how_to_apply: Default: child theme enqueue (finding 3). Agencies without theme access: one Custom Code item, `<body> – End`, priority 10, condition Entire Site, body `<script type="module" src="...motion-loader.js?v=1" nowprocket data-no-optimize="1"></script>`; the loader's own `[data-anim]` check does the per-page gating.
findings.how_to_verify: View source on a page without `[data-anim]`: loader present (<1 KB), no gsap request after scrolling; on an animated page in both languages: gsap loads after first scroll; Custom Code item count on the site = 1 (plus the GTM snippet).
findings.correction: Remove the question mark: `nowprocket` works on inline and external tags per WP Rocket docs. Keep the recommendation that the Custom Code item only prints the external module loader.

findings.claim: Micro-interactions for UX: hover/focus states stay CSS (no JS at all); GSAP handles orchestrated toggles with `easeReverse` (3.15) and pointer-follow effects with `gsap.quickTo()` desktop-only; keep every event handler under 50 ms for INP.
findings.detail: GSAP mistakes: never run CSS transitions and GSAP on the same properties; so hover colour/transform transitions belong to CSS alone and GSAP targets exclude them. 3.15 `easeReverse`: 'a new tween property that lets you define a different ease for when the playhead moves backwards' — `gsap.to('.menu', { yPercent: 0, ease: 'expo.out', easeReverse: 'power2.in' })` with `isOpen ? tl.timeScale(1).play() : tl.timeScale(1.5).reverse()` for mobile menus, accordions, filters; `yoyoEase` deprecated. web.dev INP: 'do as little work as possible' in event callbacks, yield with `setTimeout`/`requestAnimationFrame` for non-visual work, avoid layout thrashing; script evaluation on load can create long tasks that delay the first interaction — another reason GSAP must not evaluate before the user's first input (finding 3: the loader only imports on scroll/pointer events, so a first tap on the menu never waits for GSAP; the menu must therefore work without GSAP — CSS/Elementor native — and GSAP only decorates). GSAP's ticker auto-sleeps (`autoSleep: 120`) so idle pages pay no rAF. Pointer-follow (`quickTo`) only inside `(pointer: fine)`; Elementor help: 'Mouse effects will only affect desktop devices' — match that.
findings.breaks_when: Mobile menu/accordion opening depends on GSAP (first tap before GSAP loaded does nothing); hover tweens via GSAP on elements that also carry Elementor hover transitions (fighting interpolation); `mousemove` handlers doing layout reads (`getBoundingClientRect`) per event without rAF batching (INP > 200 ms).
findings.how_to_apply: UX components (menu, accordion, tabs, filters) are Elementor/CSS-functional first; GSAP enhances after import with `ctx.add(...)`; pointer effects: `const xTo = gsap.quickTo(el, 'x', { duration: 0.4, ease: 'power3' })` in `pointermove`, desktop-only; one `gsap.timeline({ paused: true, defaults: { easeReverse: true } })` per toggle, reused (never recreated per click — 'Recreating animations over and over' mistake).
findings.how_to_verify: Cold load, no gesture, tap the menu burger at 390 px: it opens (no GSAP required); DevTools Performance Interactions track: each tap/hover < 100 ms total, no long task; `web-vitals` INP in field < 200 ms p75.

findings.claim: Lazy images, Elementor's background lazy-loader and AJAX content change layout after ScrollTrigger measured it: give every image width/height (already a plugin rule), refresh ScrollTrigger after `load`/Loop Grid pagination/popup open, and avoid `scroll-behavior: smooth`.
findings.detail: st-mistakes: 'if you're loading images that don't have a width or height attribute correctly set or you are loading content dynamically (via AJAX/fetch/etc.) ... you usually need to refresh ScrollTrigger ... ScrollTrigger.refresh()'; ScrollTrigger auto-refreshes on `visibilitychange, DOMContentLoaded, load, resize` (`autoRefreshEvents`) and waits 200 ms after resize; `scroll-behavior: smooth` on `html` makes refresh measure at the wrong scroll position — 'html { scroll-behavior: auto !important; }'. Since GSAP loads after the first scroll (finding 3), the `load` event has usually passed; call `ScrollTrigger.refresh()` once right after import and after `document.fonts.ready`; Elementor's 'Lazy Load Background Images' un-blanks `background-image` on `.e-con.e-parent:nth-of-type(n+4)` via IntersectionObserver (levers.md 7.1) — backgrounds do not change box size, but lazy `` without dimensions and Loop Grid 'Load more' do. Hook `frontend/element_ready/global` (finding 5) for AJAX-inserted elements and call refresh in the callback (debounced).
findings.breaks_when: Reveals trigger too early/late or scrubbed sections are offset after lazy images load; pins misalign after Loop Grid pagination; markers drift on resize with Bootstrap-style `scroll-behavior: smooth`.
findings.how_to_apply: motion.js end: `ScrollTrigger.refresh(); document.fonts.ready.then(() => ScrollTrigger.refresh());` plus `elementorFrontend.hooks.addAction('frontend/element_ready/global', () => { clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(() => ScrollTrigger.refresh(), 100); })`; CSS: `html{scroll-behavior:auto}`; keep rule 3/5: every `` has width/height or `aspect-ratio`.
findings.how_to_verify: With `markers: true` in a dev build, start/end lines sit where expected after a cold load that lazy-loads images and after 'Load more'; CLS stays ≤ 0.05 in Lighthouse (transform-only animations do not count, but un-sized images do).

findings.claim: Do not install GSAP through an Elementor add-on pack (Animation Addons for Elementor 4.2.7 bundles GSAP ScrollTrigger, SplitText, ScrollSmoother, 100+ widgets, 40+ atomic widgets, templates): it violates the plugin's one-pack rule and ships a site-wide animation system; hand-written GSAP in the child theme is smaller, auditable and page-scoped.
findings.detail: wordpress.org readme (trunk): 'all-in-one Elementor addons pack – GSAP scroll animations, 100+ Elementor widgets, 40+ Elementor 4 Atomic Widgets & 300+ templates'; features 'ScrollTrigger, scrub, pin, horizontal scroll, parallax', 'Smooth Scrolling (ScrollSmoother)', 'Split Text Animation (GSAP SplitText) and Text Scramble', cursor effects, 'Templates are pre-animated: import a section and the GSAP scroll animations and hover effects come with it'; 'set per device, and switched off for visitors who prefer reduced motion'. sites-in-the-wild rule 16: 'one add-on pack maximum with conditional asset loading'; levers.md 7.5 shows packs like Dynamic.ooo adding ~72 KB site-wide. A pack that adds smooth scrolling and cursor effects from the editor makes the rule-13 blockers one click away for a content editor, and its enqueue behaviour (per page or site-wide) was not verified in this research.
findings.breaks_when: Pack enqueues its GSAP bundle + extension CSS/JS on every page (unverified, 'verify'); editors enable ScrollSmoother/cursor effects/preset-animated templates on the hero; a second add-on pack is already installed (rule 16 breach).
findings.how_to_apply: Build skill: GSAP only via child theme files (findings 2-3); if a client already runs Animation Addons, treat it as the one allowed pack, disable its Smooth Scroller, cursor and text-animation extensions, and dequeue its assets on pages with no pack widgets (rule 16).
findings.how_to_verify: Network log on the home page: no `/plugins/animation-addons-for-elementor/` requests unless a pack widget is on the page; no `ScrollSmoother`/`smooth-wrapper` in DOM; plugin count of add-on packs ≤ 1.

findings.claim: No independently published GSAP-animated site scoring 90+ on mobile could be opened and verified in this research; the usable real-world data are the agency's own measurements (platonos 84 with GSAP at load, 1.78 s bootup; andreas-stricker 39-68 with Lenis), and the lab mechanics that make the gated pattern score-neutral.
findings.detail: Search found no case study with a published Lighthouse/PSI report for a GSAP site at 95+; one vendor page claims an average PageSpeed of 46/100 across 62 GSAP sites but could not be opened (connection reset) so it is not cited as verified. GSAP's community forums (the usual source of Elementor+GSAP threads) are offline during this research ('A critical security vulnerability was found in PHP ... forums offline'). PSI API returned 429 quota-exceeded for fresh runs on gsap.com, osmo.supply and animation-addons.com. What is verified: levers-research.json — 'platonos (84) has no Elementor animations but ships gsap.min.js + ScrollTrigger + SplitText = 1.78 s bootup, its TBT 358 ms is its largest remaining front-end cost'; sites-in-the-wild.json — andreas-stricker.at with `smooth-scrolling-with-lenis` 'JS scroll hijack, TBT contributor', 39-68; sites-in-the-wild.md: 'the fastest public sites get their score by executing almost nothing before interaction'. Lighthouse mechanics that make finding 3 score-neutral: it never scrolls or interacts, so scroll/pointer-gated imports and below-fold IntersectionObservers never fire in the lab; reduced-motion is emulated false (levers.md). Therefore the honest claim is: GSAP done this way costs ~0 Lighthouse points and the whole risk moves to field INP and to breakage, which the breakage-checklist's Playwright matrix must cover (scroll pass, console gate, reduced-motion project).
findings.breaks_when: The team assumes GSAP sites 'can' score 95 because someone claims it — the only measured GSAP site in the corpus pays 1.78 s bootup by loading at `load`; or assumes the lab score proves field responsiveness (it does not: Lighthouse never scrolls).
findings.how_to_apply: Make platonos the pilot: move its existing gsap+ScrollTrigger+SplitText to the finding-3 loader, keep its visual result, and record before/after (bootup, TBT, score, median of 3) as the plugin's first first-party 'GSAP at 90+' example; add a Puppeteer timespan scroll run to the audit as the forced-execution check for motion.
findings.how_to_verify: Before/after Lighthouse mobile medians on platonos: `bootup-time` gsap entries disappear from the load run, TBT drops toward the 66 ms target for 100, score ≥ 95; timespan scroll run: gsap loads after first scroll, no long task > 50 ms; CrUX INP p75 unchanged or better after 28 days.

findings.claim: Gate the GSAP import on movement gestures only (scroll, wheel, touchmove, keydown); never on an IntersectionObserver, pointerdown or click — otherwise the lab run executes GSAP or the first tap pays its parse.
findings.detail: Lighthouse mobile emulation is 412x823 CSS px (constants.js). An IntersectionObserver with rootMargin '300px 0px' on the first [data-anim] element intersects at load whenever that element starts above 1,123 px — the second screen of almost every landing page — so the 'zero GSAP in the lab' promise silently fails and ~46 KB gz is fetched, parsed (ScrollTrigger.refresh() reads layout for every trigger) and counted in bootup-time/TBT. pointerdown/click as triggers move the same cost onto the first interaction: INP is 'the longest interaction observed' and module evaluation after import() lands as its own task on the main thread, which can delay the processing of the click that follows the pointerdown on a 4x-throttled phone (web.dev optimize-inp: break up long tasks, yield). Scroll/wheel/touchmove never happen in a navigation run and are not INP interactions.
findings.breaks_when: A page has its first animated block inside ~1.5 viewport heights and the loader uses an IO (lab executes GSAP); a tap on the menu burger triggers import() and the menu's own click handler runs behind the GSAP evaluation task.
findings.how_to_apply: motion-loader.js: `if (document.querySelector('[data-anim]') && !document.body.classList.contains('elementor-editor-active')) for (const ev of ['scroll','wheel','touchmove','keydown']) addEventListener(ev, () => import(new URL('./motion.js?v=1', import.meta.url)), { once: true, passive: true });` — nothing else. motion.js keeps the 'already on screen -> leave static' guard for deep links and short pages.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse mobile navigation: `network-requests` contains motion-loader.js only; no gsap/motion.js entry; `bootup-time` identical to the static build. Puppeteer: after one `page.mouse.wheel({deltaY: 10})` the GSAP files load; after a bare tap on the burger (no scroll) they do not and the menu opens.

findings.claim: Ship GSAP minified: either one esbuild ESM bundle (~46 KB gz for core+ScrollTrigger) or dynamic-import the dist/*.min.js UMD files sequentially; never copy the npm package-root *.js files into the theme.
findings.detail: Measured 3.15.0: package-root ESM gsap-core.js 50.1 KB gz, CSSPlugin.js 18.7, ScrollTrigger.js 32.1, Observer.js 7.7 (about 109 KB gz, 375 KB raw to parse) versus dist/gsap.min.js 28.3 + dist/ScrollTrigger.min.js 18.0 KB gz. The 3.15.0 UMD header is `!function(t,e){"object"==typeof exports&&"undefined"!=typeof module?e(exports):"function"==typeof define&&define.amd?define(["exports"],e):e((t=t||self).window=t.window||{})}(this,function(e){...` — inside a module `this` is undefined, so it falls back to `self` and attaches `window.gsap` / `window.ScrollTrigger`; `await import()` of the two min files in order therefore works with no build step. With a build step, `npx esbuild src/motion.js --bundle --minify --format=esm --outfile=js/motion.js` (import from 'gsap' and 'gsap/ScrollTrigger', call gsap.registerPlugin) yields a single tree-shaken chunk. Use `new URL('./motion.js?v=X', import.meta.url)` so the path follows the theme URL and the version busts page-cache-plugin JS caches.
findings.breaks_when: ESM root files copied verbatim (2.4x bytes, unminified parse); UMD files imported in parallel (`Promise.all`) so ScrollTrigger evaluates before gsap exists; motion.js edited without bumping the query (stale file served by LiteSpeed/FlyingPress/CDN).
findings.how_to_apply: Child theme: `js/vendor/gsap/gsap.min.js`, `ScrollTrigger.min.js`, optional `SplitText.min.js` from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.15.0/dist/ (commit the files); motion.js starts with `await import('./vendor/gsap/gsap.min.js'); await import('./vendor/gsap/ScrollTrigger.min.js'); const { gsap, ScrollTrigger } = window; gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger);` — or the esbuild one-liner in CI.
findings.how_to_verify: After the first scroll, DevTools Network shows gsap.min.js 72.9 KB raw (transfer about 28 KB), ScrollTrigger.min.js 44.6 KB raw (about 18 KB); `gsap.version === '3.15.0'`; no file over 120 KB raw from /js/vendor/gsap/.

findings.claim: Pro popup events are `elementor/popup/show` and `elementor/popup/hide`, dispatched both as jQuery document events (args [id, instance]) and as window CustomEvents with `detail: { id, instance }` — re-initialise GSAP reveals from the window event, no jQuery needed.
findings.detail: Verified in Elementor Pro 4.3.1 frontend.min.js (live on limnoupolis.gr): `i=d=>{const h="elementor/popup/"+d;elementorFrontend.elements.$document.trigger(h,[s,this]),window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(h,{detail:{id:s,instance:this}}))}` inside initModal(); the handlers bundle listens to `window.addEventListener("elementor/popup/hide", ...)` and `$window.on("elementor/popup/hide", ...)`. `instance` is the popup document handler with `$element`. This resolves open question 2 and matches the breakage-checklist's smoke test, which already waits for `elementor/popup/show`.
findings.breaks_when: Code relies on jQuery being loaded before motion.js (Delay-JS or a dequeue can reorder it); reveals inside a popup are created before the popup is in the DOM (ScrollTrigger measures a display:none element: start/end 0).
findings.how_to_apply: motion.js: `addEventListener('elementor/popup/show', e => { const root = e.detail?.instance?.$element?.[0]; if (root) ctx.add(() => initReveals(root)); ScrollTrigger.refresh(); }); addEventListener('elementor/popup/hide', () => ScrollTrigger.refresh());` — inside popups prefer plain `gsap.from` timelines over ScrollTriggers (the modal is its own scroller).
findings.how_to_verify: Playwright: open a popup, `[data-anim]` elements inside end at opacity 1; `ScrollTrigger.getAll().length` returns to its previous value after hide; no console errors with jQuery absent before motion.js.

findings.claim: Pro Interactions do honour per-breakpoint exclusion at runtime (`breakpoints.excluded` per interaction) but appear to ignore prefers-reduced-motion entirely; the build skill should set mobile exclusions on every page-load/scroll interaction and treat reduced-motion as unhandled for Interactions.
findings.detail: interactions.min.js (Elementor 4.3.5, 13.3 KB) contains `skipInteraction(t){... t.breakpoints.excluded.includes(getActiveBreakpoint())}`, `initBreakpoints()` reading `ElementorInteractionsConfig.breakpoints` (module.php `get_active_breakpoints()`) and matching `window.innerWidth`, re-evaluated on resize via onChange; defaults trigger 'load', effect 'fade', type 'in'. The same bundle has zero occurrences of 'prefers-reduced-motion' or 'reducedMotion'; motion.min.js (Motion 11.13.5) consults `(prefers-reduced-motion)` only through its own reducedMotion config path, which nothing in Elementor's handler sets, so Interactions most likely play for users who asked for reduced motion — unlike Elementor's CSS entrance animations (help: 'Elementor respects the reduced motion property') and unlike the GSAP matchMedia branch. Help article 'Interactions apply to all devices' (updated 19 Jun 2026) contradicts the runtime; the 4.0 developers update describes 'dedicated breakpoint controls'.
findings.breaks_when: Design-to-Elementor lint counts Interactions as 'desktop-only' because the editor panel suggests it while the stored item has no `breakpoints.excluded`; a client with an accessibility requirement (WCAG 2.3.3 / reduced-motion policy) gets moving content from Interactions on every device.
findings.how_to_apply: When Novamira `elementor-add-interaction` writes an item, include `breakpoints: { excluded: ['mobile', 'mobile_extra'] }` for slide/scale and while-scrolling effects (read the exact label set from `elementorFrontend.config.responsive.activeBreakpoints` on the site); lint: a page-load interaction without mobile excluded counts toward rule 13's animation budget on mobile. For reduced-motion-sensitive projects use GSAP (duration 0 branch) instead of Interactions, or fade-only Interactions.
findings.how_to_verify: On kand-dev6 (read-only): `elementor-get-content` on a page with an interaction shows the `breakpoints` key; in the browser at 390 px `document.querySelectorAll('[data-interactions]')`/ElementorInteractionsConfig shows the excluded item not animating; Playwright project with `reducedMotion: 'reduce'`: record whether an Interaction still animates (expected yes) and note it in design-to-elementor.md.

findings.claim: Pro Sticky is a jQuery-sticky implementation with a spacer element and `.e-con` parent detection; pinned GSAP sections must contain no `.elementor-sticky` element and must not wrap the header's parent container.
findings.detail: Pro 4.3.1 frontend.min.js: getConfig() returns `{ to: sticky, offset: sticky_offset (responsive), effectsOffset, classes: { sticky: 'elementor-sticky', stickyActive: 'elementor-sticky--active elementor-section--handles-inside', stickyEffects: 'elementor-sticky--effects', spacer: 'elementor-sticky__spacer' }, parent: '.e-con, .e-con-inner, .elementor-widget-wrap' (when 'Stay in column' is on) }` and calls `this.$element.sticky(config)` / `sticky('destroy')`; the spacer keeps layout while the element is fixed. A ScrollTrigger pin-spacer or any transform on an ancestor of the sticky element makes its fixed positioning scroll with the content (ScrollTrigger docs on fixed/transform ancestors), and the spacer plus pin-spacer double-shift the following sections. Resolves most of open question 7 (CSS of the fixed state itself sits inside the bundled jQuery sticky and was not read).
findings.breaks_when: Sticky header lives in a Theme Builder header printed inside a pinned top-level container, or a GSAP pin targets a container that holds a Sticky-enabled widget; `will-change: transform` is set on `body > .e-con` wrappers for 'smoothness'.
findings.how_to_apply: Lint: no element with `sticky` != none inside any `[data-pin]` subtree; pins only on containers whose ancestors are `body` and Elementor's root `main`/`.elementor` wrappers; never add transforms/will-change to top-level containers.
findings.how_to_verify: Scroll past the pinned range on desktop: `.elementor-sticky--active` element keeps `position: fixed` relative to the viewport and `.elementor-sticky__spacer` height equals the header height; no `.pin-spacer` contains an `.elementor-sticky`.

title: anime.js v4, CSS/Web Animations, scroll-driven CSS and Elementor native Interactions
summary: For Elementor 4.x sites that must hold mobile 95-100, the cheapest premium motion is zero-JS CSS: scroll-driven animations (animation-timeline: view()/scroll(), Chrome 115+/Safari 26+, Firefox static fallback via @supports), CSS transitions on transform/opacity/filter for hover, @starting-style for panel entry, and @view-transition { navigation: auto } (plus the WordPress Performance Team's View Transitions plugin) for page transitions. Where JS is needed, the Web Animations API (Element.animate + IntersectionObserver) costs 0 KB and runs off the main thread; anime.js 4.5.0 (MIT, 22 Jun 2026) is the right library when staggers, timelines, text splits or SVG drawing are wanted: measured 14.4 KB gz for animate+stagger, 18.9 KB with onScroll, 7.6 KB in waapi mode, versus the full UMD at 40.5 KB gz (the local skill's "24.5 KB" is stale). Elementor's own options have real, measured costs: Interactions enqueue Motion 11.13.5 + two handlers (about 49.5 KB gz) only on pages that use one, need the e_atomic_elements experiment, and (inferred from source) pre-hide nothing so load/scroll-in effects flash; Pro Motion Effects run a jQuery/rAF scroll handler on the main thread; Pro Lottie ships lottie-web 5.6.8 at 63 KB gz plus JSON, and the dotLottie web runtime adds a 1.2 MB WASM. Everything above-the-fold stays static (rules 3/4/13), Lighthouse ignores prefers-reduced-motion so score gating must be by width/pointer, and the non-composited-animations audit is the verification gate for every effect.
critic_notes: Method: WebFetch failed DNS for gsap.com, developer.chrome.com, elementor.com, wordpress.org, animejs.com, motion.dev and developer.mozilla.org, so those pages were fetched with curl through the session proxy and text-extracted; every URL listed was opened this way or via WebFetch (GitHub, Lighthouse source, anime releases). All byte sizes were re-measured locally (gzip -9) and esbuild 0.25.5 bundles rebuilt from animejs@4.5.0. Firefox share in Greece, the scroll-timeline-polyfill size, the Chrome 'animation-range calc(var())' question, Elementor V4 Global Class custom-CSS at-rule support and real-device Safari 26 behaviour were not checked. Answered open questions: Pro 'While scrolling' runtime = interactions-pro.min.js, main-thread unless Relative To = Entire page; reduced motion is NOT honoured by Interactions (is honoured by Motion Effects); legacy hover animations = assets/lib/hover/hover.min.css 1.2 KB gz conditional; Firefox still flag-only in 155/156; View Transitions plugin reduced-motion arrived in 1.1.0. Dead link: the Elementor page-transitions help URL in finding 8 redirects to the homepage; use /help/page-transitions/. Skipped: filming the Interactions flash and measuring Pro Page Transitions/Preloader JS (no agency page has them enabled). Risk: Elementor atomic features are default-on for new installs, so Interactions can appear in builds without anyone enabling an experiment.

findings.claim: Decision table: for every effect the brief asks for there is a zero- or near-zero-JS implementation that still looks premium; JS libraries are the exception, never the default
findings.detail: Effect -> cheapest premium implementation (bytes before interaction, gz): - Reveal on scroll (fade/slide/clip) below the fold -> CSS `animation-timeline: view()` + `animation-range: entry 0% entry 60%` (0 KB; Chrome 115+, Safari 26+; Firefox shows the final static state). - Staggered card reveal -> same, with per-child `animation-range` offsets via `:nth-child`; or WAAPI + IntersectionObserver (0 KB); anime `waapi.animate(...,{delay: stagger(60)})` only if easing/choreography demands it (7.6 KB). - Parallax / scrub (image moves slower, text pins) -> CSS `view()`/`scroll()` on `transform` only, below fold (0 KB). Never on the hero (rules 3/13). - Reading progress / scroll indicator -> `scaleX` keyframes + `animation-timeline: scroll(root)` (0 KB). - Header compact-on-scroll -> `scroll(root)` + `animation-range: 0 160px` animating only opacity/transform of logo/backdrop (0 KB). - Hover micro-interactions (cards, buttons, images) -> CSS `transition` on transform/opacity/filter/clip-path inside `@media (hover:hover)` (0 KB). - Panel/off-canvas/mega-menu entry -> `@starting-style` + transition (0 KB; Chrome 117, FF 129, Safari 17.5). - Page-to-page transition / shared hero morph -> `@view-transition { navigation: auto }` + `view-transition-name` (0 KB; Chrome 126, Safari 18.2; Firefox hard-cut). Not Pro 'Page Transitions' (preloader overlay). - Headline char/word reveal -> never on the LCP h1; below fold `splitText` + `waapi.animate` (anime, ~10 KB) or hand-wrapped ``s + CSS. - SVG line drawing -> `stroke-dashoffset` keyframes + `view()` (0 KB) or anime `createDrawable` (in the 23 KB bundle). - SVG morph -> anime `morphTo` (animejs/svg) or GSAP MorphSVG; rare, desktop-only module. - Number counters -> IntersectionObserver + 15-line rAF, or anime `animate(obj,{...})`. - Decorative icon/illustration loops -> inline SVG + CSS keyframes; Lottie only on explicit design demand, 1 per page, Lazy Load on, below fold (63 KB gz + JSON); never the dotLottie web runtime (1.2 MB WASM). - Logo marquee -> CSS `translateX` keyframes, `animation-play-state: paused` on hover and under reduced motion; never `setInterval` (rule 13 blocker). - Hero / first screen -> no motion at all (rule 13): static poster `` or text LCP. - Editor-only (no code) in/out effects -> Elementor Interactions `scrollIn`, max 2 per page, never in the first container (costs ~49.5 KB gz JS on that page). - Pro Motion Effects (scrolling/mouse) -> desktop only via 'Apply Effects On', never mobile.
findings.breaks_when: Any row is applied to the first viewport or the LCP element (render delay, rule 13), or a non-compositor property (width/height/top/box-shadow/border-radius) is animated: Lighthouse flags it in non-composited-animations and it jank-scrolls on a moto g class phone.
findings.how_to_apply: Put this table in the build skill as the 'motion budget' step: pick the first row that satisfies the design; the lint rejects `interactions`, `_animation`, `motion_fx_*` and `js-reveal`/`reveal` classes in the first top-level container and the header; any JS row needs a written reason and goes through the child-theme module loader (finding 7).
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse mobile median of 3: `non-composited-animations` passes, `bootup-time` lists no motion file before interaction except those budgeted, LCP render delay < 300 ms and < 40% of LCP, CLS <= 0.05; DevTools Performance: no long task from scroll handlers while scrolling the page end to end.
findings.correction: Anime stagger import: `import {waapi} from 'animejs/waapi'; import {stagger} from 'animejs/utils'` (17,431 B raw / 7,613 gz measured). Interactions row: 49.5 KB gz (free) / ~54 KB gz (Pro triggers). Firefox: keep the `@supports (animation-timeline: view())` guard - still behind a flag in Firefox 155/156. `interpolate-size` for height:auto is Chrome 129+/Samsung 28 only (BCD), no Safari or Firefox.

findings.claim: CSS scroll-driven animations (animation-timeline: view()/scroll()) are the default reveal/parallax/progress primitive: 0 KB JS, off the main thread, supported by Chrome/Edge 115+, Samsung 23+, Safari/iOS 26+, with Firefox left on the static state through @supports
findings.breaks_when: `animation-timeline` written before `animation` (reset to initial, nothing animates); fill mode omitted (elements visible then jump to 0 when entering); keyframes touch layout/paint properties (not composited, scroll jank, Lighthouse finding); applied to an element in the first viewport or a `::before` overlay on the hero (render delay); `view()` subject is absolutely positioned relative to a non-scrolling parent (nearest-scroller lookup walks containing blocks, Chrome doc warning).
findings.how_to_apply: Ship one `motion.css` from the child theme (or an Elementor Global Class whose Custom CSS holds the rules, Elementor 4.x classes output to the per-document CSS); assign `reveal`/`cards` classes through Global Classes on `e-div-block`/`e-image`; keep keyframes to transform/opacity/clip-path; never add the class inside the first container (lint).
findings.how_to_verify: Chrome DevTools > Animations panel shows the scroll timeline; Performance trace while scrolling shows no main-thread 'Animation Frame Fired' from these rules; Lighthouse `non-composited-animations` empty; Firefox (no support) screenshot equals the final state; Safari 26 on a real iPhone scrolls without stutter.
findings.correction: Apply `view()` reveals only to short subjects (cards, images, headings; height < ~50% of 390x823 viewport) and never to a full section wrapper; prefer `animation-range: entry 0% entry 40%` or `cover 0% cover 30%` so subjects finish within a short scroll; add a lint: no `reveal` class on any element whose top edge at 390 px is < 100vh, not only the first container. Keep the `@supports` guard: Firefox stable has no scroll-driven animations as of 156.

findings.claim: Elementor 4.x Interactions: free core gives load/scroll-in/scroll-out with fade/slide/scale; Pro adds while-scrolling/hover/click and Custom; they require the e_atomic_elements experiment, enqueue Motion 11.13.5 plus two handlers (about 49.5 KB gz) only on pages that contain one, and pre-hide nothing, so they never delay LCP but flash on 'load'
findings.detail: Source (elementor/main): `modules/interactions/module.php` returns early unless `AtomicWidgetsModule::EXPERIMENT_NAME` ('e_atomic_elements', default inactive, release status beta) is active. It registers `motion-js` = `assets/lib/motion/motion.min.js` ver '11.13.5' (measured 128,346 B raw / 42,160 gz), `elementor-interactions-shared-utils` (8,548 / 2,975) and `elementor-interactions` (13,312 / 4,363), all in footer. `Interactions_Frontend_Handler::print_interactions_data()` (wp_footer priority 1) enqueues them only when any rendered document (header, footer, content) has interactions and prints `<script type="application/json" id="elementor-interactions-data">`. Presets: duration 600 ms, delay 0, slide distance 100 px, scale start 0, easing 'easeIn' (more: easeOut, easeInOut, backIn, backInOut, backOut, linear), repeat '', 'loop', 'times', while-scrolling start 85 / end 15 (% viewport), `relativeTo` viewport; `BASE_TRIGGERS ['load','scrollIn']`, `ADDITIONAL_TRIGGERS ['scrollOut','scrollOn','hover','click']`, `BASE_EFFECTS ['fade','slide','scale']`, `ADDITIONAL_EFFECTS ['custom']`; per-interaction `breakpoints.excluded` list. Live core runtime (4.3.5 interactions.min.js): `isSupportedInteraction` = trigger in [load, scrollIn, scrollOut] and effect != custom; on DOMContentLoaded it reads `[data-interactions]`, uses Motion `inView` (IntersectionObserver, `amount: 0` for scrollIn, `0.85` for scrollOut, `replay` false -> unobserve) and Motion `animate` (WAAPI) with inline `transition:none` during the animation; keyframes fade `opacity [0,1]`, slide `x/y [+-100, 0]`, scale `[0,1]`. Help page lists Page load, Scroll into view, While scrolling (start/end grid lines), On hover, On click; Fade/Slide/Scale, In/Out, direction arrows, Duration, Delay. No stylesheet is registered by the module and `frontend.min.css` 4.3.5 has zero `data-interactions` rules, so an element is painted in its final state first, then snapped to keyframe 0 when the footer JS runs (inferred from source, not filmed). Pro 4.3.0 `frontend.min.js` (80,170 / 24,597 gz) contains interactions code but the Pro runtime for scrollOn/hover/click/custom was not exercised (no agency page has one).
findings.breaks_when: Any interaction on a first-screen element: 'load'/'scrollIn' fade shows visible -> invisible -> fade (flash) exactly where the eye is; the page carries ~150 KB raw / 49.5 KB gz extra JS (one third of the 150 KB third-party budget if counted); on a 4 s LCP phone the footer JS runs after LCP, so LCP is unaffected but the flash is visible. Interactions silently do nothing if `e_atomic_elements` is off or on v3 widgets.
findings.how_to_apply: Allow `scrollIn` fade/slide (direction up, 24-48 px via Custom in Pro) on <= 2 elements per page, all below the first viewport; never 'load'; mobile: use `breakpoints.excluded: ['mobile']` when the effect is decorative. Lint the element JSON: `interactions.items[].value.trigger` != 'load' anywhere, and empty `interactions` in the first top-level container and in header/footer templates. Prefer finding 2 (CSS view()) whenever the designer accepts linear-progress reveals.
findings.how_to_verify: Network: `motion.min.js`, `interactions.min.js`, `interactions-shared-utils.min.js` present only on pages with interactions; Lighthouse `bootup-time` for the three < 100 ms; filmstrip at 390 px shows no element disappearing after first paint; `document.querySelectorAll('[data-interactions]').length` <= 2 and none inside the first `.e-con`/`e-div-block`.
findings.correction: Treat Interactions as active by default on new sites. Pro trigger pages cost ~54 KB gz (49.5 + 4.3). 'While scrolling' with the default Relative To = Viewport is a main-thread scroll handler and snaps first-screen elements to their start state after footer JS: ban it on mobile and in the first viewport; if used, set Relative To = Entire page (native ScrollTimeline) and transform/opacity only. Interactions do not honour reduced motion - restrict them to 'fade' (non-vestibular) or wrap decorative slide/scale in `breakpoints.excluded: ['mobile']`.

findings.claim: anime.js is at v4.5.0 (22 Jun 2026, MIT) and costs 40.5 KB gz as the full UMD but 14.4 KB gz tree-shaken for animate+stagger, 18.9 KB with onScroll and 7.6 KB in waapi mode; it beats GSAP on size and licensing simplicity for stagger/timeline/text/SVG work, while its onScroll is main-thread scroll tracking, so scrub effects stay in CSS
findings.detail: GitHub releases: v4.5.0 (22 Jun): `registerAdapter()`, Three.js adapter (`animejs/adapters/three`), stagger 3D grid/`jitter`/`seed`, pseudo-linear RGB blending (colours differ from earlier versions). v4.4.0 (29 Apr) BREAKING: transforms render in a fixed order regardless of declaration order; `matrix`/`matrix3d` no longer animatable; function-based values receive `(target, index, targets, prevTween)` instead of a total count; stagger callback signature changed the same way; `scrambleText()`, `stagger({grid:true})`, `priority`; DevTools integration removed. v4.3.0 (Jan): `createLayout()`. package.json 4.5.0: license MIT, exports `.`, `./animation`, `./timeline`, `./timer`, `./events` (onScroll), `./text` (splitText, scrambleText), `./svg`, `./waapi`, `./layout`, `./easings/spring`, `./adapters/three`. Measured from cdn.jsdelivr.net: `dist/bundles/anime.umd.min.js` 118,043 B raw / 40,553 gz; `anime.esm.min.js` 118,678 / 40,836. esbuild --bundle --minify of `import {animate, stagger} from 'animejs'` = 36,067 / 14,428 gz; + `onScroll` = 49,327 / 18,890; + `createTimeline, splitText, createDrawable` = 60,525 / 22,985; `import {waapi, stagger}` = 17,523 / 7,628. For comparison gsap@3 `gsap.min.js` 72,927 / 28,268 and `ScrollTrigger.min.js` 44,575 / 17,998 (GSAP is now '100% free for all users, thanks to Webflow' including ScrollTrigger, ScrollSmoother, SplitText, MorphSVG, DrawSVG per gsap.com/pricing). onScroll API: `animate(targets,{x:100, autoplay:onScroll({container, target, axis:'y', enter:'bottom top', leave:'top bottom', sync:true|1|'play pause'|'play pause reverse reset'|<number smooth>|<ease string>, repeat, debug, onEnter, onLeave, onUpdate, onSyncComplete})})`; threshold shorthands top/bottom/left/right/center/start/end with `+=`/`-=` offsets ('bottom-=50 top'); `sync: true` = scrub; default `'play pause'`. The 4.5.0 UMD contains 1 passive `addEventListener("scroll"`, 5 `requestAnimationFrame`, 3 `ResizeObserver` and no `ScrollTimeline`/`IntersectionObserver`: scroll syncing runs on the main thread. When anime beats GSAP: staggered reveals, timelines, `splitText`, `createDrawable`, `morphTo`, springs, draggable carousels, at 15-23 KB gz, MIT, named ESM imports; when GSAP still wins: pinned scrub storytelling (ScrollTrigger pin + ScrollSmoother), MorphSVG robustness, Flip, community snippets.
findings.breaks_when: Loading the full UMD from an unpinned CDN URL (`/npm/animejs/`) silently upgrades across 4.4's breaking changes; writing v3-style `anime({targets})` against v4; using `onScroll({sync:true})` for a long parallax page on a mid-range phone (main-thread scroll listener + rAF -> dropped frames, INP risk); any anime call before LCP or on first-screen elements.
