findings.how_to_apply: Bundle per site with esbuild (`npx esbuild src/motion.js --bundle --minify --format=esm --target=es2020 --outfile=assets/js/motion.min.js`) importing only what the page uses; pin `animejs@4.5.0`; prefer `waapi.animate` for simple reveals (`import {waapi, stagger} from 'animejs/waapi'` + `'animejs/utils'`), `animate`/`createTimeline` only for choreography; drive triggers with IntersectionObserver (finding 6) and leave scrubbing to CSS `view()`; keep every anime call below the first viewport and behind `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)')`.
findings.how_to_verify: `gzip -9 -c assets/js/motion.min.js | wc -c` <= 20,000; Lighthouse `bootup-time` for the file < 80 ms and `network-requests` shows it after LCP; DevTools Performance while scrolling: no `scroll` handler longer than 4 ms; `anime` global absent when ESM is used (`typeof anime === 'undefined'`).
findings.correction: Import path: `import {waapi} from 'animejs/waapi'` + `import {stagger} from 'animejs/utils'`. Pin exactly `animejs@4.5.0` (5.0 betas exist since Aug 2026). GSAP = free proprietary no-charge licence for all plugins; anime = MIT.

findings.claim: The local anime.js skill (/root/.claude/skills/synced/.../animejs) is a usable v4 API map but its sizes are wrong by ~65%, it has no WordPress/Elementor delivery, no performance gating, no 4.4/4.5 changes and no CSS alternative; the Elementor plugin must wrap it, not reuse it as-is
findings.detail: Path: `/root/.claude/skills/synced/0f9ef445-d1d5-4a4e-97a1-70ac904ac5a0_e06e400a-2525-4c7a-8066-4de32fa3ee5b/animejs/SKILL.md` (+ `references/api-reference.md` 619 lines, `references/examples.md` 721 lines). Provides: full v4 documentation sitemap (timer, animate, timeline, animatable, draggable, createLayout, scope, onScroll, svg utils, splitText, utils, easings, waapi, engine), quick-reference snippets, React hook, example recipes (reveal on scroll `onScroll({target, enter:'bottom 80%'})`, scroll-synced progress bar, parallax, SVG draw/morph/motion path, text char/word/line, modal/accordion/menu patterns). Lacks / wrong: (1) bundle table says 'Full Bundle ~24.5 KB' gz; measured 4.5.0 UMD is 40,553 B gz / 118 KB raw; per-module numbers are likewise unverifiable. (2) CDN snippets use unpinned `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/animejs/...` and `esm.sh/animejs`; no mention of the 4.4.0 breaking changes (function-value signature, fixed transform order, matrix removed) or 4.5.0 (`registerAdapter`, colour blending change). (3) No license line (MIT). (4) Nothing about WordPress: enqueue, `type="module"`, Delay-JS exclusions (`nowprocket`, `data-no-optimize`, Perfmatters/FlyingPress keyword lists), 'no script in HTML widget', Elementor selectors (`.e-con`, `.elementor-element-<id>`, `[data-id]`), conflict with `elementor-invisible`/`_animation`, Dynamic.ooo's bundled anime v3 global. (5) No performance gating: no `prefers-reduced-motion`, no IntersectionObserver-vs-onScroll cost note, no 'nothing above the fold / not on the LCP element', no compositor-property rule, no hidden-until-JS flash handling, no mention that `onScroll` is a main-thread scroll listener. (6) The 'Typewriter Effect' and 'Character by Character' headline recipes are rule-13 blockers when used on a hero h1. (7) No decision guidance versus CSS scroll-driven animations, WAAPI alone, or Elementor Interactions; the `waapi` section is listed but the recipes use the 10 KB `animate` path where the 3 KB `waapi.animate` suffices.
findings.breaks_when: An agent follows the skill literally: unpinned CDN UMD (40 KB gz global `anime`) in an HTML widget, reveal applied to hero text, `onScroll` parallax on mobile, no reduced-motion gate; Lighthouse loses 5-15 points (render delay + bootup) and the site gains a second anime global next to Dynamic.ooo's v3.
findings.how_to_apply: In the elementor-lean plugin add a `motion` reference/skill that says: 'load the generic animejs skill for API details, then apply these overrides' with the corrected sizes, pinned version 4.5.0, the esbuild recipe, the child-theme module loader (finding 7), the lint (no motion in first container/header, <= 20 KB gz motion bundle), the compositor-property rule and the CSS-first decision table (finding 1).
findings.how_to_verify: Diff the skill's size table against `gzip -9 -c anime.umd.min.js | wc -c` on each anime release; grep the generated site for `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/animejs` (must be absent) and for two anime globals (`window.anime` from Dynamic.ooo v3 vs v4 UMD).

findings.claim: The Web Animations API (Element.animate + IntersectionObserver) is the 0 KB way to do triggered reveals, staggers and counters with compositor-run animations in every browser; anime's waapi.animate adds stagger/easing sugar for 7.6 KB gz, and Safari drops hardware acceleration for custom linear() easings
findings.breaks_when: `fill:'forwards'` left on dozens of elements (each keeps a live WAAPI effect; use `'backwards'`/none and let the class hold the end state); hiding `.js-reveal` in CSS unconditionally (Delay-JS or a blocked script leaves content invisible forever, Googlebot indexes blank sections); animating `height`/`margin`/`box-shadow` (not composited); applying `.js-reveal` to hero children (render delay) or percentage translates (`translateX(-100%)` reported as 'Transform-related property depends on box size').
findings.how_to_apply: Ship `reveal.js` (~0.8 KB gz) with the child theme; add `js-reveal` through a Global Class or the element's CSS Classes field only below the first container; put the single CSS line in the theme stylesheet; prefer finding 2 when linear scroll-progress reveals are acceptable and use this when the design wants eased, time-based entrance.
findings.how_to_verify: With JS blocked (DevTools > Disable JavaScript) every section is visible; Lighthouse `non-composited-animations` empty; `document.getAnimations().length` returns to 0 a second after scrolling stops; Safari Web Inspector Timelines shows no main-thread frames during the reveal; first-viewport elements have `is-in` immediately (no flash in the filmstrip).

findings.claim: Delivery pattern for any motion JS on an Elementor site: one child-theme ES module, enqueued per page, excluded from Delay-JS, never inside an HTML widget, never a second anime global next to Dynamic.ooo's bundled anime v3
findings.breaks_when: The script lands in an HTML widget (duplicated per language/template, cached in post-N.css era pages, blocked by optimizers rewriting inline scripts); Delay-JS catches it (effects dead until interaction, blank sections if CSS pre-hides); a page that also has a Dynamic.ooo anime v3 widget (global clobbered -> one of them throws); `wp_is_mobile()` gating (page-cache poisoning, levers 7.1).
findings.how_to_apply: Add this loader to the build skill's 'site setup' step and the lint: `grep -r "<script" ` in element JSON `html` settings = 0; `ingl-motion` present in the optimizer exclusion list; `_ingl_motion` meta set by the builder only on pages that received a `js-reveal`/anime class; check `grep -rl "animejs" wp-content/plugins/*/assets` before adding anime.
findings.how_to_verify: View source: exactly one `<script type="module" ... motion.min.js>` with `nowprocket data-no-optimize`; Lighthouse `network-requests` shows it after LCP; cold load with no mouse movement at 390 px still animates on first scroll; `typeof window.anime` is 'undefined' (ESM scope) or exactly the v3 function from Dynamic.ooo, never both.

findings.claim: Page transitions: cross-document View Transitions (`@view-transition { navigation: auto }`) give native crossfades and shared-element hero morphs for 0 KB on Chrome 126+/Safari 18.2+, and the WordPress Performance Team's View Transitions plugin (1.2.1, WP 6.9+, reduced-motion aware) turns it on in Settings > Reading; Pro 'Page Transitions' with its Preloader does the opposite
findings.breaks_when: Polylang/WPML on language subdomains (cross-origin -> no transition, no error); a `pagereveal` handler in a deferred/module script (runs after first render, customisation lost); duplicate `view-transition-name` on two elements at once (transition skipped); long server TTFB > 4 s (skipped); the Pro Preloader enabled (content hidden on first arrival, LCP pushed to the preloader's end).
findings.how_to_apply: Install the View Transitions plugin (fade, 300-400 ms, header named so it stays fixed), or ship the 6 CSS lines above in the child theme; keep Pro Page Transitions and Preloader off; for the shared-hero morph add a 30-line classic `<script blocking="render">` in `wp_head` only on listing + detail templates; subdirectory language setup only.
findings.how_to_verify: Lab: Lighthouse score and LCP unchanged (cold navigations never run a transition); click a link in Chrome 126+/Safari 18.2+ with DevTools > Animations recording and confirm a `::view-transition` pseudo tree; enable OS 'Reduce motion' and confirm a hard cut; CrUX LCP p75 after 28 days must not regress.
findings.correction: Cite plugin 1.1.0 for reduced-motion/400 ms; use https://elementor.com/help/page-transitions/ as the Pro Page Transitions source.

findings.claim: Lottie is a below-the-fold luxury: Pro's Lottie widget loads lottie-web 5.6.8 at 252.6 KB raw / 63.2 KB gz plus the JSON, lazy-loads via IntersectionObserver when 'Lazy Load' is on, and the dotLottie web runtime is a 1.2 MB WASM (496 KB gz) that never belongs on these sites
findings.detail: Measured live: `elementor-pro/assets/lib/lottie/lottie.min.js` = `/* Version: 5.6.8 License: MIT */` 252,588 B raw / 63,171 gz. Pro 4.3.0 handler (in elements-handlers.min.js): `bodymovin.loadAnimation({container, path, renderer: e.renderer, autoplay: false})`; triggers `none`, `arriving_to_viewport` (IntersectionObserver with `offset: "end% 0% start%"`, plays on enter, pauses on leave), `bind_to_scroll`, click, hover; `lazyload` IntersectionObserver gates the file load. Help page: Source External URL or Media File (JSON upload, warning that JSON 'can contain malicious code'), Trigger 'Viewport: ... Use the Viewport slider to determine the exact percentage', On Click, On Hover, Scroll, None; 'toggle Lazy Load on ... the animation will only load when it becomes visible'. Alternatives measured from jsDelivr: lottie-web@5 `lottie.min.js` 305,704 / 76,054 gz, `lottie_light.min.js` 168,394 / 46,410, `lottie_svg.min.js` 242,630 / 62,320; `@lottiefiles/dotlottie-web@0.81.0` `dist/index.js` 165,443 raw / 32,933 gz + `dist/dotlottie-player.wasm` 1,238,072 raw / 496,333 gz (webgl 1,366,371, webgpu 1,398,289), `dotlottie-wc` 84,367 / 20,806 on top. dotLottie's win is the .lottie file (zip of JSON + assets), not the runtime. Rule 13 (sites-in-the-wild) already blocks Lottie before LCP; Pro Lottie has 'Lazy Load and Trigger, no device gate' (levers 7.1).
findings.breaks_when: A Lottie in the hero or header (63 KB gz + JSON + SVG DOM before LCP; lottie-web renders hundreds of SVG nodes -> DOM budget and TBT); Lazy Load off (file loads on every page view); looping Lottie longer than 5 s without a pause control (WCAG 2.2.2 A); JSON over ~100 KB (parse + render on main thread); dotLottie web component anywhere (0.5 MB gz before the first frame).
findings.how_to_apply: Default: convert the designer's Lottie to inline SVG + CSS keyframes (`view()`-driven if scroll-tied) or a <= 100 KB animated AVIF/WebP `` for decorative loops. If a real Lottie is required: Pro Lottie widget, Media File source, JSON <= 50 KB, renderer svg, Trigger Viewport, Lazy Load on, Loop off or <= 5 s, one per page, never in the first container; dequeue `elementor-pro` lottie assets on pages without the widget (rule 10).
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse `network-requests`: no `lottie.min.js`/`.json` animation before LCP, none at all on pages without the widget; `dom-size-insight` not raised by the SVG tree (< 300 nodes per animation); TBT delta < 50 ms with the widget vs without; `bootup-time` for lottie.min.js < 150 ms.

findings.claim: Pro Motion Effects (Scrolling: vertical/horizontal/transparency/blur/rotate/scale; Mouse: track/3D tilt) run a jQuery scroll + requestAnimationFrame handler on the main thread inside elements-handlers.min.js, so they are desktop-only decoration at most and never a mobile lever
findings.detail: Pro 4.3.0 `elements-handlers.min.js` (291,601 B raw / 72,980 gz, loaded on every Pro page regardless of use) contains the motion-fx module: `initInteractionsTypes(){this.interactionsTypes={scroll:..., mouseMove:...}}`, `jQuery.each(e.interactions, ...)`, `addEventListener("scroll"` and `requestAnimationFrame` calls, `motionFXLayer`, CSS transform variables per element, a perspective class for tilt. Help page: 'Apply Effects On - Choose where you want to apply the effects on - Desktop, Tablet or Mobile'; 'Effects Relative To' viewport vs entire page; 'Mouse effects will only affect desktop devices'; 'Elementor respects the "reduced motion property" ... motion effects is disabled for that user'; documented bug: Mouse Track in Safari can throw 'maximum call stack size exceeded' through jQuery and make elements such as carousel arrows disappear - fix is to 'Disable entrance animations for widgets with motion effects' or remove mouse effects from areas mixing scroll and mouse effects. Blur and transparency scroll effects animate `filter`/`opacity` via JS each frame; horizontal/vertical use transforms. Because Lighthouse emulation reports `prefers-reduced-motion` false (levers 7.6), the reduced-motion exemption does nothing for the score. Elements' settings carry `motion_fx_*` keys (design-to-elementor lint target).
findings.breaks_when: Scrolling effects on mobile (per-frame jQuery handler on a 4x-slowed CPU = scroll jank and INP > 200 ms on tap during scroll); any motion effect inside the first container (counts toward the 20-element rule 13 finding and moves the LCP element); blur effect on large images (paint-heavy filter each frame); combined with an entrance animation in Safari (documented crash).
findings.how_to_apply: Builder default: Motion Effects off. If the brief wants desktop parallax on a v3 widget, set Apply Effects On = Desktop, Effects Relative To = Viewport, transforms only (no Blur), <= 3 elements per page, none above the fold; prefer finding 2 (`view()` parallax) which also works on mobile at zero JS. Auditor: count `motion_fx_motion_fx_scrolling`/`motion_fx_motion_fx_mouse` = 'yes' in the element JSON and report per device.
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse: no change in TBT when effects are disabled (they must already be desktop-only); DevTools Performance (4x CPU, 390 px) scroll trace shows no `scroll` listener > 4 ms from elements-handlers; Safari desktop console clean on pages with Mouse Track; enable OS reduce-motion: effects stop.
findings.correction: Motion Effects runtime = elementor-pro/assets/js/frontend.min.js (24.6 KB gz, on every Pro page), not elements-handlers.min.js; it does gate on `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (user protection only - Lighthouse emulation still pays).

findings.claim: Only compositor properties (opacity, transform/translate/scale/rotate, and in Chrome/Safari clip-path and filter) may be animated; Lighthouse's non-composited-animations audit is the exact gate, and box-shadow/border-radius/width effects have drop-in compositor substitutes
findings.detail: web.dev: 'Before using any CSS property for animation (other than transform and opacity), determine the property's impact on the rendering pipeline. Avoid any property that triggers layout or paint'; `will-change` only after a measured problem and removed afterwards. motion.dev performance: 'In every modern browser, transform and opacity will operate directly on a layer'; Chrome/Firefox handle `filter` and SVG on the compositor, Chrome adds `background-color` and `clip-path`; substitutes: `animate(el,{filter:'drop-shadow(10px 10px black)'})` instead of `boxShadow`, `clipPath:'inset(0 round 50px)'` instead of `borderRadius`; each new layer costs GPU memory, 3D transforms promote more than expected. anime hw page: compositor everywhere = opacity, transform, translate, scale, rotate; some browsers = clip-path, filter; Safari drops acceleration for custom `linear()` easings. Lighthouse audit `non-composited-animations`: 'Animations which are not composited can be janky and increase CLS'; failure reasons reported per element: 'Unsupported CSS Property: {properties}', unsupported custom CSS property (CSS variables), 'Transform-related property depends on box size' (percentage translates such as `translateX(-100%)` on elements whose size is not fixed), 'Effect has composite mode other than "replace"', 'Target has another animation which is incompatible', 'Effect has unsupported timing parameters'. Premium-looking compositor-only recipes: card lift `transform: translateY(-4px) scale(1.01)` + `filter: drop-shadow(0 12px 24px rgb(0 0 0/.18))`; image zoom `img{transform:scale(1.04)}` inside `overflow:hidden`; reveal masks with `clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0)` -> `inset(0)`; gradient shimmer via a pseudo-element `translateX`.
findings.breaks_when: Animating `height`/`max-height` for accordions and mega menus (layout per frame), `box-shadow` on hover across a grid of 12 cards (paint storm), `top/left` parallax, `background-position` marquees, `%`-based translates on auto-sized elements, or `will-change` sprinkled site-wide (layer explosion on 2 GB phones).
findings.how_to_apply: Lint the child theme CSS and Global Class custom CSS: `transition`/`animation` property lists may contain only opacity, transform, translate, scale, rotate, filter, clip-path (and `display`/`overlay` with allow-discrete for finding 13); accordion/menus open with `grid-template-rows: 0fr -> 1fr`? no - use `clip-path`/`transform` reveals or `height:auto` via `interpolate-size` only after checking support; replace shadows with `filter: drop-shadow()` and radius animation with `clip-path: inset(0 round r)`; keep translates in px/rem/vw.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse `non-composited-animations` = 0 items on home, listing and detail pages; Chrome DevTools > Rendering > 'Paint flashing' shows no repaint while hovering/scrolling animated regions; Layers panel shows < 20 composited layers on a long page.

findings.claim: Reduced motion is a two-layer rule: WCAG 2.3.3 (AAA, C39) wants every non-essential interaction/scroll animation behind prefers-reduced-motion and 2.2.2 (A) wants auto-moving content > 5 s pausable, while Lighthouse emulates prefers-reduced-motion = false, so the score-protecting gates are viewport width and pointer type, not the media query
findings.detail: W3C Understanding 2.3.3: 'allow users to prevent animation from being displayed ... if scrolling a page causes elements to move (other than the essential movement associated with scrolling) it can trigger vestibular disorders. Another animation that is often non-essential is parallax scrolling'; 'Animation from interactions applies when a user's interaction initiates non-essential animation. In contrast, 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide applies when the web page initiates animation automatically'; solutions: avoid, provide a control, or 'take advantage of the reduce motion feature'. Technique C39: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { /* CSS to disable motion */ }` or the inverse `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { /* motion */ }`; test: enable OS reduce motion, check non-essential motion is suppressed. 2.2.2: 'Five seconds was chosen because it is long enough to get a user's attention, but not so long that a user cannot wait out the distraction'. Elementor: Motion Effects are disabled under reduced motion (help page); entrance animations: `prefers-reduced-motion` 'only cancels .animated keyframes, smooth scroll and Swiper autoplay - it never removes elementor-invisible' (breakage-checklist); Motion 11.13.5 inside Interactions tracks `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion)')` internally but whether Elementor's runtime honours it is unverified. Lighthouse: `prefers-reduced-motion` and Save-Data are false under its emulation (levers 7.1/7.6, 412x823, moto g UA), so a reduced-motion gate never improves the lab score; the lab-visible gates are `matchMedia('(min-width:1025px)')` and `(pointer:fine)`. CSS pattern used throughout: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .marquee{animation: slide 30s linear infinite} } .marquee:hover,.marquee:focus-within{animation-play-state:paused}` plus a visible pause button for loops > 5 s.
findings.breaks_when: A marquee/testimonial auto-slider/Lottie loop runs > 5 s with no pause control (2.2.2 A failure, also an INP/CPU drain); parallax or tilt not wrapped in the media query (2.3.3; vestibular complaints from hotel guests); a developer relies on `prefers-reduced-motion` to 'hide' heavy JS from Lighthouse (it never fires in the lab, so the score still pays).
findings.how_to_apply: Every motion rule in CSS lives inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`; every JS module starts with the matchMedia check (finding 6); loops get `animation-play-state` pause on hover/focus and a pause button when > 5 s; heavy desktop-only effects are gated by `(min-width:1025px)` and `(pointer:fine)` so phones (and Lighthouse) never load them; document in the audit which gate protects users and which protects the score.
findings.how_to_verify: Playwright `test.use({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` screenshot equals the static baseline and `document.getAnimations().length === 0` after scroll; a 390 px Lighthouse run with `--emulated-form-factor=mobile` still shows no desktop-only module in `network-requests`; manual: enable 'Reduce motion' on iPhone and scroll the home page - nothing moves except the page.

findings.claim: @starting-style gives zero-JS entry transitions for off-canvas menus, popups, dialogs and anything toggled from display:none (Chrome 117, Firefox 129, Safari 17.5), replacing JS 'open' animations and the hidden-until-JS problem for UI panels
findings.breaks_when: `@starting-style` placed before the open-state rule (overridden, no transition); transitioning `height`/`width` of the panel (layout per frame); forgetting `allow-discrete` when the element really goes `display:none` (instant pop, no fade); relying on it for first-screen content reveals (that is an entrance animation and hits rule 13).
findings.how_to_apply: Use for menus, popups, filters drawers, booking-widget sheets and FAQ answers (`clip-path`/`translate` + `@starting-style`), styled in the child theme or the element's Custom CSS; keep Elementor's JS for state toggling only; never pair with Pro Interactions on the same element.
findings.how_to_verify: Open/close the panel with DevTools > Animations recording: one CSS transition on opacity/translate, no JS animation entries; Lighthouse `non-composited-animations` clean; Firefox < 129 or Safari < 17.5 shows an instant open (acceptable), nothing hidden.
findings.correction: Prefer the class-toggle pattern (`.panel:not(.is-open){opacity:0;translate:0 16px;pointer-events:none}` + `@starting-style`) for Elementor off-canvas/popups; reserve `display ... allow-discrete` / `overlay` for native `<dialog>`/popover and accept a hard cut in Firefox.

findings.claim: Hover and tap micro-interactions are pure CSS transitions on transform/opacity/filter/clip-path gated by @media (hover:hover): zero bytes, INP-safe, and they are where a site reads as 'premium' on desktop without touching mobile at all
findings.breaks_when: Hover effects on touch devices without the `(hover:hover)` gate (first tap shows hover state, second tap navigates - a UX bug on booking CTAs); animating `box-shadow`/`border-radius`/`width` (paint/layout storms on 12-card grids); hover transitions on the hero image (`scale` triggers a repaint of the LCP area, harmless for the score but visible jank on weak GPUs).
findings.how_to_apply: Define `card`, `btn`, `link`, `img-zoom` Global Classes with these transitions in the child theme stylesheet or class Custom CSS; apply via `classes` in the element JSON; zero JS; keep `:active` feedback outside the hover gate for touch.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse `non-composited-animations` clean; DevTools Rendering > Paint flashing shows only the hovered card repainting (or nothing when only transform/opacity/filter change); on a phone, a single tap on a card navigates immediately (no sticky hover); INP in CrUX stays 'good'.

findings.claim: Elementor Interactions and anime/WAAPI must coexist with the existing per-page lint: no `interactions`, `_animation`, `motion_fx_*` or motion classes in the first container or header/footer templates, <= 2 Interactions per page, <= 20 animated elements per page, and one motion mechanism per element
findings.detail: Existing rules: sites-in-the-wild rule 13 (none above the fold or on the LCP element; > 20 `elementor-invisible`/motion-fx elements per page is a finding; Animated Headline/typewriter hero, Lottie, canvas rAF, `setInterval` marquees, Lenis before LCP are blockers; render delay < 40% of LCP); levers 7.6 (`elementor-invisible` = `visibility:hidden` removed by `global.js`, 7.8 s render delay on voreniahorizon's h1; 'v4 Interactions ... none on the first screen, <= 2 per page'); design-to-elementor sequence (lint: no non-empty `interactions` or `_animation`/`motion_fx` in the first section, <= 2 interactions per page, depth <= 4). This research adds: Interactions live in each atomic element's `interactions` array as `{ $$type: 'interaction-item', value: { interaction_id, trigger, animation: { $$type: 'animation-preset-props', ... effect, type, direction, timing_config: { duration, delay } }, breakpoints: { excluded: [...] }, config: { replay, easing, relativeTo, repeat, times, start, end } } }` (validation.php shape); the server validates `repeat` modes, `times >= 1`, `start`/`end` 0-100 and a maximum number of interactions per element (translators string in validation.php). Mixed mechanisms on one element (v3 `_animation` + Interactions, or Interactions + a `js-reveal` class) double-animate and can leave `elementor-invisible` unresolved when Delay-JS holds `frontend.min.js`. Count rule for the new motion classes: `js-reveal` + `reveal` + `[data-interactions]` + `.elementor-invisible` + `motion_fx` elements <= 20 per page.
findings.breaks_when: A builder adds a 'scroll into view' interaction to the hero heading (flash + counts) or a `_animation` to an element that also has `js-reveal` (two engines fight, element may stay hidden); header template elements get interactions (motion.min.js on every page of the site); > 20 animated nodes (rule 13 finding, INP from dozens of observers).
findings.how_to_apply: Extend the existing lint in the build skill: walk the element tree; for the first top-level element and the header/footer documents reject `interactions.length > 0`, `settings._animation`, any `settings.motion_fx_*`, and class names matching `/^(js-reveal|reveal|parallax|marquee)/`; globally cap `interactions` items at 2 and the union of animated markers at 20; reject elements with more than one mechanism; run `elementor-get-content` after `elementor-set-content` to confirm the arrays survived.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse `lcp-breakdown-insight` render delay < 300 ms and < 40% of LCP; `document.querySelectorAll('.elementor-invisible,[data-interactions],.js-reveal,.reveal').length <= 20` and none inside the first `.e-con, .e-div-block, .e-flexbox, .e-grid` or `header`; `motion.min.js` absent on pages without Interactions.

findings.claim: Pro 'While scrolling' Interactions default to Motion scroll() with a target element, which forces the main-thread JS fallback; only Relative To = Entire page uses the native ScrollTimeline
findings.detail: interactions-pro.min.js 4.3.0: `function Yt(...){ start=85, end=15, relativeTo=e.animation.relativeTo||'viewport'; animate(el, fromValues, {duration:0}); p=animate(el, keyframes, {...,autoplay:false}); relativeTo==='viewport' ? (m.target=el, m.offset=['start 85%','start 15%']) : m.offset=['15%','85%']; scroll(p, m) }`. Elementor's bundled motion.min.js (Motion 11.13.5): `!n.target && supportsScrollTimeline() ? new ScrollTimeline({source, axis}) : <JS fallback that writes currentTime from measured progress>`. motion.dev/docs/scroll: 'Browsers that support the ScrollTimeline API will use this to run supported animations with hardware acceleration' - but the code path only does so without a `target`. Consequence: the default While-scrolling mode is a scroll-measured, main-thread driven WAAPI animation; 'Entire page' mode is compositor-driven in Chrome 115+/Safari 26. The start-state snap at init also means a first-screen element with scrollOn is painted final, then snapped to its start keyframe when footer JS runs.
findings.breaks_when: A builder leaves Relative To = Viewport (default) and enables the effect on mobile: every frame of scroll runs JS progress math for each element; on a 4x-slowed moto g the scrub lags and INP during scroll suffers. Any scrollOn inside the first viewport flashes to its start state after LCP.
findings.how_to_apply: Lint `interactions.items[].value.trigger === 'scrollOn'`: reject on mobile unless `breakpoints.excluded` contains 'mobile'; require `config.relativeTo === 'page'`; reject inside the first top-level container. Prefer CSS `animation-timeline: view()` (finding 2) for the same visual.
findings.how_to_verify: DevTools Performance (390 px, 4x CPU) while scrolling a page with one scrollOn: 'viewport' mode shows per-frame scripting from motion.min.js; 'page' mode shows none and `document.getAnimations()[0].timeline instanceof ScrollTimeline` is true in Chrome.

findings.claim: Elementor Interactions (core and Pro runtimes) ignore prefers-reduced-motion entirely, so they fail WCAG 2.3.3 unless limited to fade effects or excluded per breakpoint
findings.detail: interactions.min.js (4.3.5) and interactions-pro.min.js (4.3.0) contain no `prefers-reduced-motion`/`matchMedia` call. motion.min.js registers `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion)')` into an internal flag (`To.current`), but the only readers are the React-style VisualElement (`this.shouldReduceMotion = To.current` on mount); the vanilla `animate`/`inView`/`scroll` functions Elementor calls never consult it. Pro Motion Effects, by contrast, skip init under `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` (Pro frontend.min.js onInit). Fade-only effects are not vestibular triggers; slide/scale/while-scrolling are.
findings.breaks_when: A hotel site uses slide/scale Interactions on content and a guest with OS 'Reduce motion' still sees them (2.3.3 AAA failure, complaints); a plugin lint that assumes 'Elementor honours reduced motion' passes it.
findings.how_to_apply: Builder rule: Interactions effect must be 'fade' unless the element is decorative AND `breakpoints.excluded` includes 'mobile'; document in the audit that only Motion Effects (not Interactions) respect reduced motion. For user protection on content motion use the CSS/WAAPI paths (findings 2/6) which are gated.
findings.how_to_verify: Playwright `test.use({reducedMotion:'reduce'})` on a page with a slide Interaction: `document.getAnimations().length > 0` after scroll proves the gap; same page with Motion Effects shows no `motionFX` transforms.

findings.claim: CSS view() reveals on fold-straddling or tall subjects leave content partially faded at load and for a long scroll distance on 390 px phones; restrict reveals to short subjects and short ranges
findings.detail: With `animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 0% entry 60%; fill both`, progress is 0 when the subject's top edge reaches the viewport bottom and 100% at `entry 60%` (60% of the subject's height inside). A section whose top is at 70% of the first viewport on load has its timeline mid-way: it is painted at e.g. opacity 0.3/translated and stays so until the user scrolls (Chrome doc: view progress tracks the subject's position in its scroller; nothing advances without scroll). A 1,400 px tall section at 390x823 needs ~840 px of scroll before `entry 60%` is reached. Short subjects (cards 200-400 px) complete within one swipe. The partially transparent state also shows in the Lighthouse filmstrip even though opacity > 0 elements remain LCP candidates.
findings.breaks_when: The `reveal` Global Class is put on `e-div-block` section wrappers or on the second top-level container that starts above 100vh at 390 px; hero-adjacent 'intro' text is half-visible in screenshots and feels broken to users who do not scroll.
findings.how_to_apply: Lint: `reveal`/`cards` classes only on elements whose rendered height < 400 px and whose top at 390 px is >= 100vh (compute from the Elementor JSON tree: never the first two top-level containers' direct children unless measured). Use `animation-range: entry 0% entry 40%` (or `cover 0% cover 25%` for images) so the effect completes within ~40% of the subject height.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse mobile filmstrip final frame: no element with computed opacity between 0.05 and 0.95; Playwright at 390x823 without scrolling: `[...document.querySelectorAll('.reveal')].every(e=>getComputedStyle(e).opacity==='1'||e.getBoundingClientRect().top>innerHeight)`.

findings.claim: anime.js 5.0.0 is in public beta (beta.2, 17 Aug 2026); unpinned CDN or `^4` ranges will cross a major in the coming months - pin 4.5.0 and keep the esbuild bundle in the repo
findings.detail: npm registry: 5.0.0-beta.1 2026-08-05, 5.0.0-beta.2 2026-08-17 under dist-tag `beta`; `latest` still 4.5.0. jsDelivr `/npm/animejs/` and `/npm/animejs@4/` both resolve to 4.5.0 today; the first will move to 5.x on release. The 5.0 beta UMD is 120,082 B raw (listed on jsDelivr), i.e. not smaller. Combined with the 4.4.0 breaking changes already in the finding, the agency should commit the built `motion.min.js` and the exact version, not a CDN link.
findings.breaks_when: A later site build runs `npm i animejs` without a lockfile after 5.0 ships, or an HTML widget references `/npm/animejs/` - API drift breaks reveals silently (effects dead, no console error if the import names still exist).
findings.how_to_apply: `npm i -E animejs@4.5.0` in the child-theme build; commit `package-lock.json` and `assets/js/motion.min.js`; lint the rendered HTML for `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/animejs` and `esm.sh/animejs` (must be 0).
findings.how_to_verify: `node -e "console.log(require('animejs/package.json').version)"` prints 4.5.0; `grep -c animejs wp-content/themes/*/assets/js/motion.min.js` shows the bundled header only.

findings.claim: Elementor's legacy Hover Animations live in `assets/lib/hover/hover.min.css` (10,019 B / 1,233 gz, 29 `elementor-animation-*` classes) and are loaded conditionally, so a designer's insistence costs ~1.2 KB gz - acceptable but the CSS-transition Global Classes remain the default
findings.detail: HTTP 200 at `/wp-content/plugins/elementor/assets/lib/hover/hover.min.css` on limnoupolis.gr (Elementor 4.3.5); 29 unique `.elementor-animation-*` selectors; the limnoupolis home page HTML has 0 references to it, so it is enqueued only when a widget uses a hover animation (consistent with Elementor's conditional asset loading). frontend.min.css 4.3.5 has 0 such classes. Which properties the 29 classes animate (some hover.css effects use box-shadow) was not inspected.
findings.breaks_when: A hover animation class that animates box-shadow/border is applied to a 12-card grid (paint storm, non-composited audit); the stylesheet is forced site-wide by a 'preload all Elementor CSS' optimizer rule.
findings.how_to_apply: Auditor: flag `hover_animation` settings in element JSON and the presence of hover.min.css; builder: allow only transform/opacity-based classes (grow, shrink, float, sink, push, pop, bob, hang, rotate, etc.) after checking the class body, otherwise use the Global Class transitions of finding 14.
findings.how_to_verify: View source: hover.min.css absent on pages without hover animations; Lighthouse `non-composited-animations` clean while hovering is irrelevant (lab) - check with DevTools Rendering > Paint flashing on hover.

findings.claim: WordPress' native script-module API cannot carry Delay-JS exclusion attributes, so the child-theme motion module must stay on classic wp_enqueue_script + script_loader_tag
findings.detail: wordpress-develop trunk `wp-includes/class-wp-script-modules.php`: `register()`/`enqueue()` accept `$args` with only `fetchpriority` ('auto'|'low'|'high'); the only filters are `script_module_loader_src` (src URL) and `script_module_data_{$module_id}`; there is no equivalent of `script_loader_tag` for `<script type="module">` output, so `data-no-optimize`, `nowprocket` or a Perfmatters keyword cannot be injected. The classic enqueue in finding 7 (`strategy => 'defer'`, then `script_loader_tag` adding `type="module" data-no-optimize="1" nowprocket`) remains the only core-API path that both runs as a module and survives LiteSpeed/WP Rocket/Perfmatters/FlyingPress Delay-JS.
findings.breaks_when: A developer 'modernises' to `wp_enqueue_script_module()`: the optimizer's Delay-JS rewrites the module tag, reveals stay dead until first tap and Googlebot never triggers them (sections hidden if CSS pre-hides).
findings.how_to_apply: Keep the finding-7 loader verbatim; add a code comment `shortcut: core has no module tag filter (class-wp-script-modules.php), switch to wp_enqueue_script_module when WP adds one`.
findings.how_to_verify: `grep -n apply_filters wp-includes/class-wp-script-modules.php` on the installed WP version shows only `script_module_loader_src` and `script_module_data_*`; view-source shows the attributes on the motion tag.

title: Design excellence and complete UX for hospitality and small-business sites (hotels, villas, water-park shop, restaurants, forum; Greek + English)
summary: What makes a hospitality site look expensive and convert is mostly restraint applied with precision, and almost all of it is compatible with the plugin's performance rules (static hero, text or one LCP, two Greek-capable fonts, no animation above the fold, third-party JS deferred to interaction). The evidence-based core: (1) the booking path must be visible in the first viewport with the all-in price shown up front (MeasuringU 2017 Best Western failure; Baymard 2022; FTC 16 CFR 464 since 12 May 2025; EU CPC/ACM commitments 2019-2020); (2) WCAG 2.2 AA numbers are now a legal floor for e-commerce under the European Accessibility Act (28 June 2025) and are cheap to meet in Elementor Variables/Classes: 4.5:1 text, 3:1 UI/large text, 24x24 CSS px targets (48 recommended), 320 px reflow, 2 px/3:1 focus ring not hidden under the sticky header; (3) static hero beats carousel (NN/g, 57 % of viewing time above the fold, <= 5 frames if any), visible or combo navigation on desktop (hidden nav used 27 % vs 48-50 %), logo top-left (6x easier to get home); (4) real photography is scrutinised, stock is ignored (NN/g eyetracking); (5) fluid type with clamp() between a 1.2 (mobile) and 1.25-1.333 (desktop) ratio, 45-80 character measure, 1.5 line height, 16-18 px body, and two Greek-subset families verified against the Google Fonts API (Manrope, Commissioner, Inter, Roboto Flex, IBM Plex Sans, Fira Sans, Literata, Source Serif 4, EB Garamond, Alegreya, Noto Serif Display, Vollkorn, Cardo; NOT Playfair Display, Cormorant, Montserrat, Raleway, Lora, Fraunces, DM Sans, Jost, Marcellus, Cinzel); (6) Greek typographic correctness (uppercase strips tonos only in Chrome 34+/Firefox 15+, never Safari; final sigma) and a `lang` attribute per language; (7) micro-interactions limited to transform/opacity transitions of 150-300 ms, `@media (hover:hover)`, `:focus-visible`, and CSS scroll-driven animations below the fold behind `@supports` (Chrome 115, Safari 26, Firefox only from 159 - not in stable yet); Elementor v4 Interactions (Page load / Scroll into view / While scrolling / On hover / On click; Fade / Slide / Scale; apply to all devices) are allowed below the fold only. Speed itself is a conversion lever in travel: a 0.1 s mobile improvement moved travel conversions +10.1 % (Deloitte/Google, 37 brands, 2020), which is the business case for not trading PageSpeed for decoration. Taste (palette proportions, photo grading, thumb-zone layouts, bottom "Book" bars) is labelled as such; Awwwards/CSSDA/Elementor showcase pages could not be opened from this environment and vendor conversion benchmarks (1.5-4 % hotel CVR) are unaudited.
critic_notes: Method: WebFetch failed DNS for ftc.gov, elementor.com, developer.chrome.com, eur-lex, w3.org, nngroup.com, mdn, web.dev, wordpress.org; all were re-opened via curl through the proxy (EUR-Lex still returned 202 challenge pages, FederalRegister/eCFR HTML returned CAPTCHA pages but the FederalRegister JSON API worked; the EAA text was read from legislation.gov.uk's copy of the original EU directive). Elementor source read from raw.githubusercontent.com (main) and the shipped interactions scripts from the agency's public sites (read-only GET of plugin assets; no Novamira calls, no site changes). Greek font subsets were verified live against fonts.googleapis.com/css2 with a Chrome UA. Still unverified and should stay open: Greek Law 2251/1994 / UCPD Art. 7(4)(c) wording (EUR-Lex blocked), Commission Art. 6a guidance scope text, Law 4276/2014 licence-display duty, Elementor Pro Form aria-describedby output, clamp() in Size variables, iOS input-zoom primary source. Not checked: NN/g scrolling-attention and photos articles (accepted as cited), MeasuringU/Baymard pages, Deloitte study, GSAP file sizes. Risk to flag: the design-to-elementor reference caps v4 Interactions at 2 per page while this dimension's researcher proposed ~10 - the synthesis step must pick one number.

findings.claim: The booking path must be in the first mobile viewport and show the total, all-in price; this is both the strongest usability evidence for hotel sites and, since 12 May 2025, a legal requirement for short-term lodging sold to US consumers (and an EU consumer-law commitment already enforced against Booking.com/Expedia).
findings.detail: MeasuringU's 2017 SUPR-Q benchmark (405 + 160 participants, Best Western/Hilton/Hyatt/Marriott) found the one concrete usability failure was the Book button below the fold while an 'Update' button sat above it - users clicked Update and stalled; Hilton lost users when the hero promo linked to the loyalty site with no way back. Baymard (992 h of travel-accommodation testing, 2022): sites funnel users to the 'Booking' search (destination, check-in/out, rooms, guests); 4 rate names for one room each 'Excluding Taxes & Fees' made comparison impossible; users wanted min nightly rates inside the calendar and clearly marked unavailable dates; boutique-hotel users abandon when room pages lack bathroom/bed detail and photos. Law: FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees, 16 CFR Part 464, effective 12 May 2025, makes it unlawful to present any price for short-term lodging without disclosing the total price (all mandatory fees, taxes may be excluded if disclosed before payment) clearly, conspicuously and prominently, including on hotel-owned sites and apps. EU: after the CPC action led by ACM, Booking.com (late 2019) and Expedia (2020) committed that 'the total price of the accommodation includes all unavoidable costs', no artificial scarcity, deals must be genuine; regulators said the whole accommodation sector would be held to the same. Implementation that keeps the score: hero = h1 + one + a 'Check availability' button that scrolls/anchors to a static form (dates, guests) rendered as plain HTML inputs; the booking engine's JS (WebHotelier, Bookonline, YITH, WC Bookings, Hotelrunner) loads on first focus/click of that form or on the /book page only (rule 6: <= 150 KB third party before interaction). Show 'from EUR 180 / night, taxes included' on room cards; never 'excl. fees'.
findings.breaks_when: The booking engine widget is embedded as an iframe/script in the hero (adds 300-900 KB JS before interaction, often becomes LCP or shifts layout, CLS > 0.05); Delay-JS wakes the calendar only after a user gesture so the first tap does nothing (breakage-checklist §4 'no prior mouse movement' test); prices shown without taxes/fees on a site selling to US guests (FTC rule) or EU guests (UCPD).
findings.how_to_apply: Builder: hero container = h1, one-line value proposition, primary button (anchor #book) and a static availability form (two date inputs + guests select, labels visible) as the second element; room cards carry 'from EUR X / night, incl. taxes'. Load the engine with an interaction facade (same pattern as levers.md 7.1 HTML-widget facade): `<form id="book" ...>` + `addEventListener('focusin', loadEngine, {once:true})`. Checkout/booking page: Elementor Canvas template, minimal header (design-to-elementor §3).
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse: LCP element is h1 or the hero , booking vendor domain absent from network-requests before interaction; Playwright cold-profile test taps the date field with no prior gesture and asserts the calendar opens; grep room/offer templates for 'excl'/'χωρίς φόρους'; screenshot at 390x844 shows the Book CTA without scrolling.
findings.correction: Rewrite the legal sentence: 'EU consumer law (UCPD Art. 7(4)(c)) already requires the displayed price to include taxes and unavoidable charges; the FTC junk-fee rule (16 CFR 464, effective 12 May 2025) adds the same for US guests.' Keep implementation unchanged. Add `pointerdown` alongside `focusin` on the facade so an engine that needs a touch handler still wakes on the first tap; and exclude the engine loader token from Delay-JS (levers 7.1).

findings.claim: Urgency and offers are allowed only when truthful and data-backed: scarcity messages ('only 1 room left'), countdowns and fake discounts are enforcement targets under the EU UCPD (2021 guidance explicitly covers dark patterns) and were the subject of CMA/CPC actions against OTAs; a hotel site should show real availability counts from the PMS, genuine prior prices, and trust signals instead.
findings.detail: Which? (Sept 2019) spot-checked Booking.com after the CMA 1 Sept 2019 deadline: 5 of 10 'only X rooms left on our site' prompts were false; CMA had concluded false popularity impressions and not displaying full cost up front can break consumer law; 25 companies incl. TripAdvisor, Airbnb, Google agreed to change displays. ACM/CPC (Dec 2020): 'no more suggestions of artificial scarcity; deals must be genuine; a price cannot be presented as a discount if that is not the case'. The Commission's UCPD Guidance (17 Dec 2021) adds interpretation on 'data-driven personalisation and dark patterns' and covers the Omnibus amendments applicable from 28 May 2022 (prior-price rule for announced reductions - written for products; its application to accommodation services was not confirmed in an opened primary source). Legitimate, evidence-compatible persuasion: real 'X rooms left for your dates' pulled from the engine after the user picks dates; 'Best price guaranteed - direct' only if contractually true; strike-through prices only with a real prior price; trust strip under the fold (licence number, awards, review score with source and count, cancellation terms, secure-payment logos as inline SVG).
findings.breaks_when: A countdown or 'X people viewing' widget is a third-party script (adds JS before interaction and a timer loop that hurts INP - rule 13 forbids setInterval marquees before LCP); hard-coded scarcity text in Elementor that is never true for the dates chosen; strike-through prices generated by a plugin without a prior-price record.
findings.how_to_apply: Builder: urgency copy only via dynamic tags bound to the booking engine's availability after date selection; a static 'Why book direct' list (3 items max) and a trust strip (SVG icons, review count + source link); offers page shows 'was EUR X (lowest price last 30 days)' only if the PMS records it. Auditor: flag any 'only N left', 'N viewing', countdown, or '%-off' not bound to data.
findings.how_to_verify: grep page_content/Elementor meta for 'left|viewing|hurry|ends in|μόνο .* δωμάτι|απομένουν'; confirm each has a dynamic source; Lighthouse network: no fomo/countdown vendor scripts; visually compare strike-through price to engine's real rate.
findings.correction: State: 'The 30-day prior-price rule applies to goods (e.g. water-park shop merchandise, tickets sold as products may be arguable), not to room rates; room-rate strike-throughs are still judged under the UCPD misleading-practice test, so keep a dated record of the real prior rate.' Add the Elementor Pro Countdown widget to the auditor's grep list (it is first-party JS but a timer loop before LCP; rule 13).

findings.claim: WCAG 2.2 AA is the design floor and, for hotel/villa/shop sites that sell online in the EU, a legal one since 28 June 2025 (European Accessibility Act covers e-commerce; microenterprises < 10 staff AND <= EUR 2 M turnover are exempt for services - check per client). The numbers are cheap to bake into Elementor Variables and Global Classes.
findings.detail: Contrast (1.4.3 AA): 4.5:1 body text, 3:1 for large text = 18 pt / 24 CSS px regular or 14 pt / ~18.66 px bold; non-text contrast (1.4.11 AA): 3:1 for input borders, icons, focus indicators, button boundaries against adjacent colours (2.999:1 fails - no rounding). Target size (2.5.8 AA, new in 2.2): every target >= 24x24 CSS px or spaced so 24 px circles don't overlap; exceptions: inline text links, native controls (input type=date calendar), essential (map pins); Lighthouse/Material/web.dev recommend 48x48 (about 9 mm) and the Lighthouse tap-targets audit fails below 48 px or when 25 % of the 48 px area overlaps another target. Focus not obscured (2.4.11 AA): a focused element must not be fully hidden under a sticky header/cookie bar - use `scroll-padding-top: var(--header-h)` on html and `:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--color-focus); outline-offset:2px}`; Focus appearance (2.4.13, AAA but the practical target): indicator area >= 2 px perimeter, 3:1 change. Reflow (1.4.10 AA): no horizontal scroll at 320 CSS px (test at 320 px, not 360). Resize text (1.4.4 AA): 200 % zoom must work - fluid clamp() must include a rem term. Text spacing (1.4.12 AA): layout must survive line-height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter 0.12em, word 0.16em - so no fixed-height text containers. Dragging (2.5.7 AA): any drag (gallery, range slider) needs a tap alternative (arrows). Motion: 2.2.2 (A) auto-moving content > 5 s needs pause/stop/hide; 2.3.3 (AAA) honour prefers-reduced-motion for scroll-triggered motion. Elementor's free 'Web Accessibility (formerly Ally)' plugin (wp.org slug pojo-accessibility) adds an on-demand page scanner (180+ WCAG 2.1 AA checks, alt-text detection, contrast 'coming soon'), an accessibility-statement generator and a floating usability widget; use scanner + statement, do NOT ship the widget (extra front-end JS on every page).
findings.breaks_when: Accessibility overlay widgets (Ally widget, accessiBe, UserWay) add 100-300 KB JS and a floating button on every page - counts against the 150 KB third-party budget and can become an LCP candidate like cookie banners (rule 8); brand palettes with light-grey body text (#999 on white = 2.85:1) fail 1.4.3; icon-only buttons at 20 px fail 2.5.8; clamp() with only vw units fails 200 % zoom.
findings.how_to_apply: Design System: define `--color-text` / `--color-text-muted` / `--color-surface` pairs that pass 4.5:1 and 3:1 before creating classes; `btn-*` classes min-height 48px / min-width 48px, padding 12px 24px; `icon-btn` 44-48 px; html{scroll-padding-top: var(--header-h)}; global `:focus-visible` rule in the child theme CSS; Elementor Site Settings > Layout: breakpoints checked at 320 px. Install Web Accessibility plugin, run scanner on home/room/offer/contact/booking, publish the statement, keep widget off.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse accessibility >= 95 with color-contrast and target-size audits passing; axe-core (rules color-contrast, target-size) 0 violations on 5 page types; Chrome DevTools device 320 px wide: no horizontal scrollbar; keyboard Tab through header + hero: focus ring visible, never under the sticky header; 200 % zoom screenshot readable.
findings.correction: Replace 'Lighthouse tap-targets audit fails below 48 px' with 'Lighthouse 12+ reports axe `target-size` (24 px WCAG 2.2); enforce 48 px yourself in the Playwright check'. State the EAA exemption precisely: '< 10 staff AND (turnover <= 2 M OR balance sheet <= 2 M)'; note the EAA harmonised standard is EN 301 549 (WCAG 2.1 AA level) so the Ally scanner's 2.1 AA scope matches the legal baseline while 2.2 AA stays the design floor. Keep: scanner + statement, widget off.

findings.claim: Typography is the cheapest 'expensive look': two Greek-subset families, a fluid modular scale (1.2 on mobile to 1.25-1.333 on desktop via clamp()), 16-18 px body, 45-80 character measure and 1.5 line height - and most 'premium' display fonts designers pick (Playfair Display, Cormorant, Montserrat, Raleway, Lora, Fraunces, Marcellus, Cinzel) have NO Greek glyphs.
findings.detail: Verified today against fonts.googleapis.com/css2 subsets: WITH greek - sans: Inter, Manrope, Commissioner, Roboto Flex, IBM Plex Sans, Fira Sans, Open Sans, Noto Sans, Ubuntu Sans, Didact Gothic, Comfortaa, Advent Pro; serif: Literata, Source Serif 4, EB Garamond, Alegreya, Noto Serif Display, Noto Serif, Vollkorn, Cardo, Gentium Plus, GFS Didot (Greek-first Didot, latin basic). WITHOUT greek: Playfair Display, Cormorant (all cuts), Montserrat, Raleway, Lora, Fraunces, DM Sans, Jost, Libre Caslon Text, Gelasio, Crimson Pro, Spectral, Merriweather, Figtree, Outfit, Plus Jakarta Sans, Onest, Hanken Grotesk, Instrument Sans, Bricolage Grotesque, Red Hat Display, Marcellus, Cinzel, Josefin Sans, Nunito Sans, Mulish, Work Sans, Exo 2, Philosopher. Pairings that pass (taste, not evidence): Noto Serif Display 500 + Manrope; Literata + Inter; EB Garamond + Commissioner; GFS Didot (Greek) + Source Serif 4 for a classic hotel; IBM Plex Sans alone (two weights) for the water-park shop. Scale: Utopia's method - define a ratio of 1.2 at 320 px and 1.333 at 1500 px and interpolate each step with clamp(); e.g. --step-0: clamp(1rem, 0.95rem + 0.25vw, 1.125rem); --step-4 (h1): clamp(2.07rem, 1.3rem + 3.3vw, 4.2rem). The preferred value must keep a rem term so 200 % browser zoom still scales (WCAG 1.4.4; Smashing). Measure: 45-90 characters (Butterick), WCAG 1.4.8 says <= 80 - set `max-width: 65ch` on prose and `max-width: 20ch` on display headings; line-height 1.5 body, 1.1-1.2 display; paragraph spacing >= 1em. Lighthouse 13 dropped the 'legible font sizes' SEO audit, so enforce >= 16 px body / >= 12 px captions yourself. Spacing rhythm (taste, widely used): a 4/8 px base, section padding clamp(3rem, 2rem + 4vw, 7rem), 8-step spacing tokens stored as Elementor Size variables.
findings.breaks_when: A third family sneaks in via a widget-level override or a V4 atomic style (`elementor_atomic_styles_fonts-*`), breaking rule 11 (2 families / 4 files / ~150 KB); a Latin-only display font renders Greek headings in the fallback (visible brand break on the Greek site); clamp() built only from vw fails zoom; `ch`-based max-width on a Greek font differs - check Greek line length visually (Greek words average longer).
findings.how_to_apply: Design System > Variables: Font variables for exactly two families; Size variables --step--1..--step-5 with clamp() strings (design-to-elementor §1 says clamp() accepted - verify on 4.3.x); Global Classes heading-display/h2/h3/body/caption with font-size: var(--step-n), line-height, max-width in ch; Defaults h1-h6/p use the classes. Subset both families latin+greek (pyftsubset command in design-to-elementor §1) and upload as Pro Custom Fonts with display swap; Google Fonts = Disable.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse network: <= 4 same-origin woff2, no googleapis; fontTools cmap count U+0370-03FF >= 100 per family; screenshot Greek + English h1/h2/p at 390 px and 1440 px; `document.fonts` on the Greek home page lists only the two families; measure body line length at 1440 px = 55-75 characters.

findings.claim: Greek typographic correctness is a visible quality marker: uppercase Greek must drop the tonos (and sigma must become final-ς), which browsers do only with `lang="el"` and only in Chrome/Firefox - Safari never strips accents - so all-caps Greek headings via CSS are unreliable and a `lang` attribute per language is mandatory.
findings.detail: MDN: with text-transform: uppercase in Greek (el), vowels lose their accent except disjunctive ή (Ή), and accented diphthongs move the accent to a diaeresis (άι -> ΑΪ); lowercase picks σ or final ς by context. MDN browser-compat-data: greek_accented_characters supported Chrome 34+, Firefox 15+, Safari: false; lowercase_sigma Chrome 30+, Firefox 14+, Safari 6+. Consequences for Elementor builds: (1) every Polylang/WPML page must emit <html lang="el"> / "en" (Polylang does; verify on Elementor Theme Builder templates and popups); (2) if the design uses all-caps labels (common in luxury hotel UIs: 'ΔΩΜΑΤΙΑ', 'ΚΡΑΤΗΣΗ'), write the Greek text in capitals in the content rather than relying on text-transform, or accept accents on iOS; (3) never put Greek text in images or in fonts without Greek glyphs (previous finding); (4) letter-spacing on uppercase Greek 0.05-0.1em is fine but tracking on lowercase Greek hurts legibility (taste). Greek copy runs longer than English - give buttons `min-width` not fixed width and test nav wrapping at 1024 px.
findings.breaks_when: Theme Builder header/footer/popup output lacks lang (screen readers read Greek with an English voice; uppercase rule not applied); CSS `text-transform: uppercase` on Greek menu items shows tonos on iPhones (Safari) and no tonos on Android - inconsistent brand; fixed-width nav items overflow with Greek labels.
findings.how_to_apply: Builder: Global Class `label-caps` used only for Latin text; Greek labels typed in capitals; `hreflang` and `lang` via Polylang; mu-plugin check in the audit that `html[lang]` matches the page language on every template. Design-to-Elementor: component widths in Figma must be tested with the Greek string lengths.
findings.how_to_verify: Playwright: for each language visit 3 templates, assert `document.documentElement.lang` startsWith 'el'/'en'; screenshot uppercase Greek headings in WebKit (Playwright webkit) vs Chromium and compare; nav at 1024 px has no wrapped items.
findings.correction: Drop 'Theme Builder output lacks lang' as a failure mode; keep the Playwright `documentElement.lang` check and add: any element containing text in the other language carries its own `lang` (switcher items `lang="el"`/`lang="en"`). Keep 'type Greek caps in content, do not rely on text-transform'.

findings.claim: Hero composition: one static, art-directed photograph (or a text-first hero) with a short headline and one CTA beats sliders and video on every measured axis - attention, comprehension, accessibility and LCP; 57 % of viewing time is spent above the fold and 74 % in the first two screenfuls, so the hero and the section directly below carry the page.
findings.detail: NN/g eyetracking (2018): 57 % of page-viewing time above the fold, 74 % in the first 2160 px, 65 % of above-the-fold time in the top half of the viewport. NN/g carousel guidance (2013, reviewed Aug 2026): a static hero forces one powerful image and sentiment, is less distracting and increases visibility of the global navigation; if a carousel is used: <= 5 frames, show count and position, no auto-forward when content needs reading (auto-forwarding reduces accessibility, international readers can't finish, moving UI reads as an ad). 'Scroll-triggered text animations delay users' (NN/g) and 2.2.2 reinforce no motion on hero copy. Composition rules that read as expensive (taste, consistent with award-winning hotel sites): image with a clear subject and quiet area for text, headline <= 8 words set in the display face at --step-4/5, sub-line <= 20 words, one primary button + optional text link, no overlay darker than 30-40 % (lets the photo breathe; check 4.5:1 on text via a local gradient scrim `linear-gradient(to top, rgb(0 0 0 / .55), transparent 60%)` rather than a full-bleed tint). Height: `min-height: 80svh` to `100svh`, never `100vh` (mobile toolbars make 100vh taller than the visible viewport, pushing the CTA below the fold - web.dev viewport-units). Keep the first element below the hero as the booking form or the 'Rooms' grid, not a decorative band. Consistent with levers 7.1 and rules 3-4: hero image <= 100 KB AVIF/WebP at 828-1080 px wide for phones via <picture>, fetchpriority=high, explicit width/height, zero entrance animation; video or 3D only on >= 1025 px behind the facade.
findings.breaks_when: Slider/background slideshow (Pro Slides paints CSS backgrounds - LCP blocker), Animated Headline, Lottie or fade-in on h1 (render delay 3.6-7.8 s measured on agency sites), `height:100vh` hero hiding the CTA on iOS, overlay text at < 4.5:1 over bright sky.
findings.how_to_apply: Builder hero recipe: e-div-block.hero (min-height 100svh on mobile, 80svh desktop) > HTML widget with <picture> hero img (absolute, object-fit cover) > e-flexbox.hero-copy (h1, p, button, text-link). Scrim as a pseudo-element on .hero. Auditor: hero of type slider/video/animated headline = finding; CTA bounding box must be inside 390x844.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse mobile: lcp-breakdown-insight node is h1 or hero img, render delay < 300 ms, no .elementor-invisible above the fold; Playwright at 390x844: `button.cta` getBoundingClientRect().bottom < 844; contrast check of h1 against the sampled scrim area >= 4.5:1.

findings.claim: Navigation: on desktop keep the main links visible (or a visible subset plus a menu), logo top-left linking home, and a 'Book' button always visible; on mobile a hamburger plus an always-visible Book/Call button (the 'combo' pattern). Sticky headers must be opaque, small and not animated.
findings.detail: NN/g quantitative study (179 participants, 6 sites, 2016): hidden navigation was used in 27 % of desktop tasks vs 48 % (visible) and 50 % (combo); on mobile hidden 57 % vs combo 86 %; content discoverability dropped > 20 % with hidden nav; perceived difficulty +21 % vs visible; 5-7 s longer to reach navigation on desktop. NN/g (2016): getting home is about 6x harder with a centred logo than top-left. NN/g sticky headers (2021): maximise content-to-chrome ratio (13:1 good, 2:1 bad), opaque background that contrasts with every section it floats over, no animation other than a shrink, never a 'stalker' header that scoots in late, and consider whether sticky is needed at all. For hospitality IA (Baymard 2022 boutique findings) the primary nav is 5-7 items: Rooms/Villas, Offers, Experiences or Facilities (restaurant, spa, water park), Gallery, Location, Contact + language switcher + Book. Height budget: <= 64 px mobile, <= 88 px desktop; sticky via Elementor Pro Sticky (jquery.sticky ~1 KB) or plain `position: sticky` in a class (zero JS). Mega menus only if >= 12 destinations; for the forum, search in the header.
findings.breaks_when: Nav Menu widget with hover-only dropdowns (fails touch/keyboard; also a 2.5.8/2.1.1 issue), translucent sticky header over photos (NN/g: low contrast, distracts), header that animates in on scroll-up with transform (counts as layout shift if not composited; see breakage-checklist §6 CLS gate), centred logo, 'Book' hidden inside the hamburger on mobile.
findings.how_to_apply: Header template (one per language): e-div-block.header[position:sticky;top:0;background:var(--color-surface)] > logo (img, exact width/height, link home) + e-n-menu (4.3 nested menu; mobile toggle) + Book button class btn-primary + language switcher. Header elements: no entrance animation, no transparency on scroll effects. Mobile: Book button stays outside the hamburger panel.
findings.how_to_verify: Playwright: at 1440 px all primary links visible without hover; at 390 px Book button visible and tappable (>= 48 px) before opening the menu; logo link resolves to the language home; computed header height <= 64 px mobile; CLS gate from breakage-checklist stays <= 0.05 while scrolling 3 screens; keyboard Tab opens sub-menus.

findings.claim: Imagery direction: users scrutinise photographs that carry information (the actual room, the actual pool, the actual owners and staff) and ignore decorative stock; so the 'no stock look' is evidence-based, and the image budget (<= 100 KB hero, <= 200 KB first-viewport, <= 300 KB any) is where art direction and PageSpeed meet.
findings.detail: NN/g eyetracking (2010, reviewed Aug 2026): 'some pictures are completely ignored - big feel-good images used purely to jazz up pages; photos of products and real people (as opposed to stock photos of models) are treated as content and scrutinised'; users spent 10 % more time on real team portraits than on bios that took 316 % more space. Translation for hospitality: every image answers a guest question (what does the bed/bathroom/view/breakfast look like; how far is the beach; who will greet me). Practical direction (taste, consistent across the hotel sites in the sites-in-the-wild corpus and award galleries): one photographer, one consistent grade (warm, low-saturation, no HDR), 3:2 landscape for cards, 4:5 portrait for mobile hero crops via <picture>, people shown mid-action not posed, no text baked into images, galleries as a 2-column grid of <= 12 images per room with a lightbox (Elementor Gallery/Lightbox, or native <dialog>) rather than a Swiper carousel. Alt text describes the information ('Sea-view double room, balcony, Elounda bay'), empty alt for purely decorative images.
findings.breaks_when: Gallery widgets that load all full-size images at once (rule 5: no page image > 300 KB; no -scaled originals); Pro Media Carousel/Slides (CSS-background slides, LCP blocker); stock photos of generic models; images with text (fails translation + 1.4.5).
findings.how_to_apply: Builder: register sizes (hero-mobile 900x1200 crop, card 800x533, gallery 1200x800), Image widget with registered size and `loading=lazy` below the fold only; Gallery as e-grid of Image widgets linking to a lightbox; alt from the media library, enforced non-empty for content images. Design handoff checklist: photographer brief per site type (hotel: room, bathroom, view, breakfast, pool, staff, map context; restaurant: 5 dishes, room, team, exterior at dusk; water park: slides in use, family, food, tickets desk).
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse: no image > 300 KB, first viewport <= 200 KB, hero <= 100 KB; `uses-responsive-images`, `modern-image-formats` pass; axe `image-alt` 0 violations; manual review: every content image answers a guest question, none is a model stock shot.

findings.claim: Micro-interactions that signal quality cost nothing in PageSpeed if they are CSS-only, transform/opacity, 150-300 ms, hover-gated and below the fold: button/card hover lifts, link underlines that grow, focus rings, accordions, and CSS scroll-driven reveals behind @supports; Elementor v4 Interactions and GSAP are for below-the-fold sections only.
findings.detail: NN/g (2014): slow fades without position change are least distracting for non-user-initiated motion; fast transitions suit user-triggered actions and should not displace text being read; movement in the periphery hijacks attention (so no sliding elements near reading areas). Recipe: `.card{transition: transform .2s ease, box-shadow .2s ease} @media (hover:hover){.card:hover{transform: translateY(-4px); box-shadow: var(--shadow-2)}}` - the hover media query prevents 'sticky hover' on touch (CSS-Tricks; support solid), and hybrid devices are the known false-positive, so every hover state must also exist on :focus-visible. Reduced motion: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){*{transition-duration:.01ms !important; animation-duration:.01ms !important}}` in the child theme (WCAG 2.3.3; remember Lighthouse emulation has it false, so it does not change scores). CSS scroll-driven animations (`animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 0% entry 40%`) run off the main thread (Chrome blog) - compat per MDN BCD today: Chrome 115+, Safari 26+, Firefox only 159 (not yet in stable as of Oct 2026) - wrap in `@supports (animation-timeline: view())` and apply only to elements that start below 100svh (rule 13). Elementor v4 Interactions (help page): triggers Page load / Scroll into view / While scrolling (start/end points) / On hover / On click; effects Fade / Slide / Scale, In/Out, direction, Duration and Delay in ms; they 'apply to all devices' and are JavaScript (motion.min.js ~128 KB, enqueued only on pages that have one - levers 7.6). Use: Scroll into view + Fade/Slide, 400-600 ms, on cards from the second section down; never Page load on hero or header; cap ~10 per page.
findings.breaks_when: Any interaction/animation on the first top-level container or header (LCP render delay, rule 13); 'While scrolling' bound to many elements (continuous JS on scroll - INP/TBT); hover-only disclosure of prices or CTAs (touch users never see them); transitions on width/height/top (layout thrash); more than 20 animated elements per page (finding); third-party 'hover effect' add-ons (extra CSS/JS packs, rule 16).
findings.how_to_apply: Global Classes: card, btn-primary, link-underline with the transitions above; child theme `interactions.css` with @supports scroll-driven reveal for `.reveal` class; reduced-motion block. Builder lint: element.interactions non-empty only when element is not in container[0] or header; count <= 10; duration 300-600 ms; trigger not 'Page load'. GSAP only via the 7.1 facade on >= 1025 px.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse mobile: `.elementor-invisible` above fold = 0, TBT < 300 ms, motion.min.js absent on pages without interactions; DevTools Performance: no long tasks during a 3-screen scroll; Playwright with `reducedMotion: 'reduce'`: no transform changes recorded; touch emulation: tap a card - no stuck hover state after navigating back.
findings.correction: Use Interactions only on elements that start below 100svh (the flash is invisible there); keep the plugin's existing cap (<= 2 per page) unless the team raises it deliberately, and never 'Page load' or 'While scrolling'. Honour reduced motion yourself: `wp_add_inline_script('elementor-interactions', "if(matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches)document.querySelectorAll('[data-interactions]').forEach(e=>e.removeAttribute('data-interactions'))", 'before')` (handle name from module.php; verify on a dev site). State motion.js as '~42 KB gzip + 22 KB handlers'. For the CSS reduced-motion block, scope it (`.reveal, .card, .btn-*`) instead of `* !important`, which also kills Swiper/booking-engine inline transition timings.

findings.claim: Date picker and availability search: the calendar must communicate availability and nightly price, users must be able to type dates, month names must be spelled out for an international (EL/EN) audience, and the picker must work on first tap - the 'engine wakes only after a gesture' failure is the most common booking breakage on delay-JS sites.
findings.detail: Baymard (2022): users turn to the calendar to confirm availability; when it does not accurately show it they abandon; min nightly rates in the calendar let users shift dates ('a Monday night is cheaper'); unavailable dates clearly identified (Expedia example). NN/g (2017): calendar pickers for dates within a year, two months side by side for ranges on desktop, always allow typing the date, spell out month names (10/11 ambiguity), avoid scrolling drum pickers for far dates. GOV.UK date input (research-based, public sector): three text inputs with inputmode=numeric for known dates - the right pattern for birth dates in guest forms, not for check-in. WCAG 2.5.8: an unmodified native <input type=date> calendar is a 'user agent control' exception, so native inputs are the lowest-risk accessible choice for the static first-screen form; a custom engine calendar must give >= 24 px day cells (48 px recommended). Defaults: check-in = today or next available, check-out = +2 nights (hotel) / +7 (villa, weekly), guests 2; disable past dates; show currency and 'incl. taxes'. Mobile: one month at a time, full-width, sticky 'Search' button at the bottom of the sheet.
findings.breaks_when: Engine JS held by Delay-JS so the first tap on the date field does nothing (breakage-checklist §4 cold-profile test); engine calendar day cells < 24 px or hover-only prices; months shown as numbers only; past dates selectable; calendar renders in English on the Greek site; CSS-background date widget becomes LCP.
findings.how_to_apply: Static first-screen form uses native inputs (date, number) styled through a Global Class (min-height 48px, 16px font to prevent iOS zoom - taste/known behaviour); the vendor engine opens on /book or after focus; for engines with configurable calendars set two-month desktop/one-month mobile, show rates and unavailable states; exclude the engine's script token from Delay-JS (levers 7.1 'Delay-JS must skip the loader').
findings.how_to_verify: Playwright cold profile, no prior gesture: click date field -> calendar visible within 1 s; day cell bounding box >= 24x24 (ideally 44+); past date disabled; month label matches `html[lang]`; both languages; page served from cache >= 13 h after purge still opens the calendar (breakage-checklist).
findings.correction: Verify the locale only for the vendor engine's calendar; for native inputs assert instead that the visible `<label>` text is in the page language and that `lang` is set on the form. Keep defaults (check-in today/next available, +2 / +7 nights, 2 guests, past dates disabled via `min` attribute).

findings.claim: Forms and error states: visible labels (never placeholder-as-label), correct type/autocomplete/inputmode, inline errors next to the field in plain language with text + colour + icon, and spam protection that does not load reCAPTCHA before focus. Enquiry forms on hotel/villa sites convert direct requests, so a broken or ugly form is a lost booking.
findings.detail: web.dev form best practices: use <form>, <label for>, <button>; one label per input; do not use placeholders as labels or to show formats (hidden once typing starts, stressful on phones); type=email, type=tel (right keyboard), inputmode=numeric for numbers that are not quantities, never type=number for phone/card; autocomplete values (name, email, tel, bday-day/month/year, address-line1, postal-code, country) let browsers fill and help assistive tech. NN/g error-message guidelines (2023): noticeable, redundant, accessible indicators (bold, high-contrast, red text AND highlight on the field; never colour alone - ~350 M people with CVD), human-readable language, no codes; keep the user's input; place the message by the field. Elementor Pro Form: keep 'Label' shown (the Content > Form Fields > Label toggle; hiding labels and relying on placeholders is the common agency mistake), 'Required Mark' on, success/error messages customised per language, Honeypot action on, reCAPTCHA only if spam persists and then loaded on focus (rule 7); send via Webhook/email action - validate in smoke tests (breakage-checklist §4). Field sizing: min-height 48 px, 16 px text, 12-16 px vertical gap, single column on mobile (multi-column only for first/last name or day/month/year). Submit button: descriptive ('Send enquiry' / 'Αποστολή'), not 'Submit'.
findings.breaks_when: reCAPTCHA v2/v3 enqueued on every page (300+ KB and up to 500 ms blocking, often loaded twice - rule 7); placeholder-only fields (fail 1.3.1/3.3.2 and NN/g); error shown only by red border (fails 1.4.1); type=number for phone; form inside a popup that is in the LCP path.
findings.how_to_apply: Global Classes form-field (min-height 48px; font-size 1rem; border 1px solid var(--color-border) >= 3:1), form-error (text + icon). Elementor Form settings: labels visible, required mark, custom messages EL/EN, honeypot, no reCAPTCHA by default; Advanced > Custom attributes: autocomplete values per field; Webhook action to the agency test endpoint for smoke tests.
findings.how_to_verify: axe: label, color-contrast, aria-* 0 violations on the contact and booking-request pages; Lighthouse network: no recaptcha__en.js before focus; Playwright: submit empty form -> each required field shows text error adjacent to it; correct keyboard type by checking `inputmode`/`type` attributes; submission reaches the webhook.

findings.claim: Content architecture and trust: boutique-hotel visitors first scroll the home page to 'get a feel', then hunt the gallery, amenities, room detail (bathroom!), offers, map and 'what makes it unique' - so the IA is Home > Rooms (each room = photos, size, bed, bathroom, view, price-from) > Offers > Experiences/Facilities > Location (map facade) > Gallery > Contact/Book; pair it with LocalBusiness structured data and the legally required Greek identifiers.
findings.detail: Baymard (2022): boutique users scroll the homepage for feel, seek photo gallery and amenities list, dig into special features/events/neighbourhood, have keen interest in offers; absence of bathroom info + no room photos made a user give up and 'call'; users wanted a map immediately and bed-type filters; unclear multi-rate pricing hurt comparison. MeasuringU: hero promo that navigates away from the booking path hurt Hilton. Structured data (Google local-business doc): LocalBusiness subtypes (Hotel/LodgingBusiness, Restaurant with priceRange, openingHoursSpecification, address, geo, telephone, image) are eligible for knowledge-panel details; schema.org LodgingBusiness adds checkinTime/checkoutTime, petsAllowed, amenityFeature, starRating; Restaurant adds hasMenu, servesCuisine, acceptsReservations. Put JSON-LD in the child theme or an SEO plugin, not an Elementor HTML widget per page. Trust signals (evidence: ACM/CMA require they be true): licence number (Greek ΜΗ.Τ.Ε./Ειδικό Σήμα Λειτουργίας for hotels, Α.Μ.Α. property registration number for short-term-rental villas - AADE requires it on listings; EU Reg. 2024/1028 extends registration-number display to platforms from 20 May 2026 per secondary sources), review score with count and source link, cancellation terms in one sentence near the price, payment logos inline SVG, physical address and phone in the footer. Keep footers to text/links/SVG (design-to-elementor §3: no forms, maps or feeds in the footer).
findings.breaks_when: Google Maps JS on every page (rule 7: maps API only on pages with a map, and never with empty key) - use a static map image linking to Google Maps or a click-to-load facade; a social feed or review widget script in the footer (third-party budget); room pages without price/size/bed/bathroom (Baymard abandonment); structured data duplicated by SEO plugin + widget (Rich Results errors).
findings.how_to_apply: Site map template per site type in elementor-build; room single template fields: name, size m2, bed type, max guests, bathroom, view, price-from incl. taxes, 6-12 photos, amenities list (SVG icons), 'Check availability' CTA; Location page: static map (<= 150 KB) with facade; JSON-LD from a mu-plugin reading ACF/options; footer: licence number + address + phone + languages.
findings.how_to_verify: Rich Results Test on home, a room page and the restaurant page: 0 errors; grep rendered room pages for size/bed/bathroom/price fields; Lighthouse network: no maps.googleapis.com on non-map pages; licence/registration number present in footer of each language.
