findings.correction: Keep the IA and the JSON-LD in a mu-plugin; describe the structured-data gain as 'knowledge panel / Maps details and consistent NAP', not rich results with prices. Make the licence-number footer rule 'owner-confirmed' until the agency's lawyer confirms Law 4276/2014 as amended.

findings.claim: Colour system: <= 8 semantic tokens with pre-verified contrast pairs is what reads as 'expensive' and passes WCAG; the proportions (dominant neutral, one accent for the single primary action) are taste, the ratios are not.
findings.detail: Evidence side: 4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text/UI (WCAG 1.4.3, 1.4.11; axe uses 24 px regular or ~18.66 px bold as 'large'); state changes need not contrast with each other but each state must keep 3:1 with surroundings; disabled controls exempt. Taste side (common to the premium hotel sites in the corpus): a warm off-white surface (not pure #fff) and a near-black ink (not #000), one deep brand hue for the primary button, one accent (sand/terracotta/sea) for highlights, muted text at >= 4.5:1 (e.g. #5f5a54 on #faf7f2 = 6.1:1), borders at >= 3:1 (#8a847c on #faf7f2). Reserve the accent for Book/Reserve so the primary action is the only saturated element on the screen; secondary buttons are outlined. Dark sections (footer, restaurant night mood) need the same checks with inverted tokens. Elementor: Design System > Variables > Color for V4 elements plus the matching v3 Global Colors for Pro widgets (design-to-elementor §1); never per-element colour.
findings.breaks_when: Designer palette uses light grey #a0a0a0 body text on white (2.6:1 - fails); accent colour used for both links and decorative chips (CTA loses prominence); pure white + pure black with photos (harsh; taste); more than 8 colour variables (classes proliferate, unused CSS grows).
findings.how_to_apply: Token sheet step in elementor-build: compute contrast for every (text, surface) pair with a small script before creating Variables; name tokens semantically (color-ink, color-ink-muted, color-surface, color-surface-alt, color-brand, color-accent, color-border, color-focus); button classes map to them; footer uses inverted set.
findings.how_to_verify: Script over the token sheet asserting 4.5:1/3:1; Lighthouse color-contrast audit passes on 5 templates incl. a dark section; visual check: exactly one saturated element in the first viewport.

findings.claim: Mobile-first behaviour that converts: the first screen contains headline + Book CTA, targets are 48 px, inputs are 16 px, content reflows at 320 px, and the page is one DOM (no hidden desktop twin). A persistent bottom 'Book / Call' bar is widely used but only vendor-reported as a lift - treat as taste, implement as pure CSS if used.
findings.detail: Evidence: WCAG 1.4.10 reflow at 320 CSS px; 2.5.8 24 px minimum with 48 px recommended by Lighthouse/web.dev (9 mm); NN/g 2016: on mobile combo navigation was used 86 % vs 57 % hidden - keep a visible Book action; NN/g 2018: top of viewport gets > 65 % of above-the-fold attention. Vendor claims for sticky bottom CTAs (7-12 % lift, 50 % click lift) come from unaudited marketing posts - do not promise numbers. Design-to-Elementor §3 already forbids a second hidden tree ('Hide on Mobile' is display:none; assets still load). Practical rules: body text 16-18 px, h1 32-40 px on 390 px, section padding 48-64 px, cards single column, tap targets 48 px with 8 px gaps, telephone as `tel:` link in header on mobile, no horizontal carousels for rooms (vertical list), `min-height:100svh` hero, images <picture> with mobile crop, nothing fixed except the header (and optionally one bottom bar <= 56 px which must be opaque, have 2 targets max, hide on the booking page, and respect `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`).
findings.breaks_when: Bottom bar implemented with a plugin (extra JS/CSS, often a sticky element that shifts layout on load -> CLS) or overlapping the cookie banner and the booking engine's own footer; two fixed bars eating > 25 % of a 390x844 screen (NN/g content-to-chrome); hidden mobile duplicate sections (rule 15, LCP slot theft).
findings.how_to_apply: Builder: responsive style variants (mobile breakpoint values) on the same elements; optional `.book-bar` e-flexbox with position:fixed;bottom:0 via a Global Class, CSS-only, hidden on /book and when the hero CTA is visible (IntersectionObserver 5 lines, optional); DevTools device 320 px check in the audit.
findings.how_to_verify: Playwright 320x568 and 390x844: no horizontal scroll (`document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth`), Book CTA visible, all buttons >= 48 px; Lighthouse tap-targets/target-size pass; CLS gate <= 0.05 with the bar; fixed elements total height <= 120 px.
findings.correction: Verify step: 'Lighthouse `target-size` passes AND Playwright asserts every button/link >= 48x48 with >= 8 px gaps'. Bar: opaque, <= 56 px, 2 targets, hidden on /book and when the hero CTA is in view; `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` only matters if the site opts into `viewport-fit=cover`.

findings.claim: Speed is itself the conversion lever in travel - a 0.1 s mobile speed improvement raised travel conversions 10.1 % in the Google/Deloitte study - which is the business argument for refusing decorative JS, sliders and video heroes on hospitality sites; hotel-site conversion benchmarks (1.5-4 %) are vendor numbers and should be quoted only as 'directional'.
findings.detail: Deloitte Ireland for Google ('Milliseconds Make Millions', 24 Mar 2020; data from 37 retail, travel, luxury and lead-gen brands in EU/US over 4 weeks, via Fifty-Five): a 0.1 s improvement across 4 metrics (First Meaningful Paint, Estimated Input Latency, observed page load, TTFB) on every page of the journey correlated with travel conversions +10.1 %, travel AOV +1.9 %, retail conversions +8.4 %, retail AOV +9.2 %, luxury page views/session +8.6 %, lead-gen bounce -8.3 %. web.dev notes FMP is deprecated - read LCP. Caveats: correlational, pre-CWV metrics, agency-reported; use it to frame design trade-offs with owners ('this slider costs ~1.5 s LCP; in this study that scale of change moved travel conversion by double digits'), not to predict a number. Vendor benchmarks found (Roomstay/Cloudbeds roundups, 2026): hotel website CVR 1.5-2.5 % all traffic, 0.5-1.5 % mobile, OTAs ~12-15 % - unaudited, inconsistent denominators.
findings.breaks_when: Owners accept slow decorative features because 'design sells' without a measured counterfactual; agency quotes a precise CVR uplift from vendor blogs.
findings.how_to_apply: Add to the elementor-build owner brief: one paragraph citing the Deloitte figures and the site's current LCP/TBT from the audit, with the hero/slider/video decision framed as a conversion decision; track booking-engine entry rate per device in GA4 before/after the rebuild (28-day windows) to build the agency's own evidence.
findings.how_to_verify: GA4 event 'begin_checkout' or engine 'search' per session by device, 28 days before vs after; CrUX p75 LCP/INP for the origin; keep both in the plugin's audit report.

findings.claim: Awards and showcases could not be used as evidence from this environment: awwwards.com reset the connection, cssdesignawards.com returned only its gallery shell and elementor.com/showcase returned marketing copy; the 2025 Awwwards Honorable Mentions found via search (Hotel Jägerhof by upgreight, 26 Dec 2025; Grand Hotel Central, 16 Dec 2025) were not opened and must not be cited as references in the plugin until verified.
findings.detail: What awards reward (motion-heavy WebGL heroes, custom cursors, smooth-scroll) is exactly what the plugin forbids above the fold; the useful lesson from them is composition (large type, generous whitespace, one photograph per section, restrained palette), which the typography/colour/hero findings already encode. Elementor's own showcase page (elementor.com/showcase) is now a marketing page without a filterable hotel gallery. Recommendation: build the plugin's reference list from sites the audit can measure (the 32-site sites-in-the-wild corpus plus pallada.gr at 86 as the agency's best pattern) and add award sites only after a Lighthouse run confirms they can be imitated within budget.
findings.breaks_when: A builder copies an Awwwards hero (Lenis + GSAP + WebGL) into an Elementor site - rule 13 blockers, TBT in seconds (limnoupolis three.js: 142 s TBT).
findings.how_to_apply: Keep a `references/design-references.md` that lists only measured sites with their Lighthouse median and what to borrow (composition) vs what not to (motion); open Awwwards/CSSDA from a normal browser to populate it.
findings.how_to_verify: Each listed reference has a dated mobile Lighthouse score and LCP element type recorded.

findings.claim: Elementor v4 Interactions neither pre-hide elements nor honour prefers-reduced-motion; the plugin must add both gates itself or restrict Interactions to elements that start below the first screen
findings.detail: interactions.min.js (13.3 KB) + interactions-shared-utils.min.js (8.5 KB) as served on pallada.gr/limnoupolis.gr: keyframes are built at runtime (`fade` -> opacity [0,1], `scale` -> [scaleStart,1], `slide` -> x/y [+-slideDistance,0]); grep finds no `prefers-reduced-motion`, `matchMedia` or `IntersectionObserver` in those two files and no `[data-interactions]` rule in frontend.min.css. So (a) an element in view at init paints, then jumps to opacity 0 and fades back (flash), unlike the `elementor-invisible` mechanism; (b) WCAG 2.3.3 reduced motion is not honoured. module.php registers handles `motion-js` (motion v11.13.5, 128,346 B raw / 42 KB gzip), `interactions-shared-utils`, `interactions`, only when the atomic-widgets experiment is active, enqueued on pages that use one.
findings.breaks_when: An inline script that strips `data-interactions` runs after the frontend handler initialised (wrong handle or position), or the attribute/handle names change in a future 4.x release; Delay-JS holds motion.js so scroll-into-view cards stay un-animated (acceptable) or, if a pre-hide CSS is added, invisible (not acceptable - never add a pre-hide).
findings.how_to_apply: Builder lint: element.interactions allowed only when the element's top-level container index >= 2 (below 100svh on 390x844); trigger in {Scroll into view, On hover, On click}; <= 2 per page (design-to-elementor §4). Child theme: `wp_add_inline_script('elementor-interactions', "if(matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches)document.querySelectorAll('[data-interactions]').forEach(e=>e.removeAttribute('data-interactions'))", 'before')`; confirm the exact handle in `modules/interactions/module.php` of the installed version.
findings.how_to_verify: Playwright with `reducedMotion: 'reduce'`: no `[data-interactions]` attributes remain and no opacity change recorded over a 3-screen scroll; default profile: filmstrip shows no element flashing in the first viewport; Lighthouse network: motion.min.js absent on pages without interactions.

findings.claim: Several Lighthouse audits the plugin's verify steps may name no longer exist: tap-targets (removed in 12.0, replaced by accessibility target-size), font-size, third-party-facades, offscreen-images, uses-rel-preload, preload-fonts, no-document-write, uses-passive-event-listeners, first-meaningful-paint (all removed in 13.0.0, 2025-10-10)
findings.detail: Changelog 13.0.0: 'remove font-size audit (#16701)', 'remove third-party-facades audit (#16710)', 'remove offscreen-images audit (#16748)', 'remove preload-fonts, uses-rel-preload audits (#16716)', 'remove no-document-write', 'remove uses-passive-event-listeners', 'remove empty first-meaningful-paint audit'; 12.0: 'tap-targets ... replaced with the target-size audit in accessibility', 'viewport and font-size ... moved to best practices'. Current default-config.js lists `accessibility/target-size` (weight 7, wcag22aa) and no seo/font-size or seo/tap-targets. levers.md already reads `third-parties-insight` for 13.x, but the design-dimension verify steps and `references/data/levers-research.json` still cite the removed ids; a check keyed on a missing audit silently passes.
findings.breaks_when: The auditor script reads `audits['tap-targets']` or `audits['third-party-facades']` and treats undefined as pass; a client runs PSI (13.x) and the report cites an audit they cannot see.
findings.how_to_apply: In the new skills, reference only: `target-size` (24 px), `color-contrast`, `third-parties-insight`, `lcp-breakdown-insight`/`largest-contentful-paint-element`, `network-requests`, `total-blocking-time`, `cumulative-layout-shift`; enforce body >= 16 px and 48 px targets in Playwright. Grep the plugin for the removed ids and replace or mark '(12.x only)'.
findings.how_to_verify: `grep -rn 'tap-targets\|third-party-facades\|offscreen-images\|font-size audit' plugins/elementor-lean` returns only historical notes; a 13.x Lighthouse JSON contains every audit id the skills read.

findings.claim: Greek glyph coverage of a design's fonts can be checked automatically from the Google Fonts CSS2 API in one line, and should be a hard gate in elementor-build before any font is subset or uploaded
findings.detail: `curl -sA 'Mozilla/5.0 ... Chrome/130' 'https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=<Family>:wght@400&display=swap' | grep -c '/\* greek \*/'` returns 1 (or 2 with greek-ext) when the family ships Greek; 0 otherwise. Verified today: 0 for Playfair Display, Montserrat, Lora, Raleway, Cormorant Garamond, Fraunces, DM Sans, Jost, Nunito Sans, Mulish, Spectral, Cinzel, Marcellus; >= 1 for Manrope, Noto Serif Display, Literata, Commissioner, GFS Didot. For non-Google fonts use `pyftsubset --unicodes=U+0370-03FF` dry run or `fontTools` cmap count (>= 100 Greek code points). Also catches the common designer handoff where Figma shows Greek via a silent fallback font.
findings.breaks_when: The API is queried without a browser UA (returns a TTF-only CSS with no subset comments); a variable font listed as 'latin' only on Google but shipped with Greek by the foundry (check the foundry file instead).
findings.how_to_apply: Step 1 of the token sheet in elementor-build: for each of the two families run the check; if 0, stop and propose a Greek-capable pairing (Noto Serif Display + Manrope; Literata + Inter; EB Garamond + Commissioner; GFS Didot + Source Serif 4). Store the result in the build log.
findings.how_to_verify: Build log shows both families with greek >= 1 (or cmap count); Greek h1/h2/p screenshots render in the chosen family (`document.fonts.check('16px <Family>', 'Ωμέγα')` true).

findings.claim: GSAP is now 100 % free including all formerly 'Club' plugins (ScrollTrigger, ScrollSmoother, SplitText, MorphSVG, DrawSVG, Flip, etc.), so licensing is no longer a reason to avoid it; performance budget is the only gate, and the plugin should say so to stop builders reaching for anime.js or Lenis as a 'free alternative'
findings.detail: gsap.com/pricing (opened today): 'GSAP is now 100% free for all users, thanks to Webflow's support ... we're able to offer the entire GSAP library for free'; the plugin list on the page includes Draggable, Inertia, ScrollTrigger, ScrollSmoother, Observer, Flip, SplitText, ScrambleText, Physics2D, PhysicsProps, CustomBounce, CustomWiggle, DrawSVG, MorphSVG, MotionPath, MotionPathHelper, GSDevTools. For this dimension the consequence is purely about where GSAP may run: desktop-only, behind the levers 7.1 facade, below the fold, never for hero text (SplitText on the h1 is the platonos 1.78 s bootup pattern).
findings.breaks_when: GSAP + ScrollTrigger + SplitText loaded on mobile before interaction (platonos: 1.78 s bootup); ScrollSmoother/Lenis-style smooth scroll anywhere (rule 13 blocker, breaks native scroll-padding/anchors used by the booking CTA).
findings.how_to_apply: In the motion skill: 'GSAP core + plugins are free (gsap.com/pricing). Allowed only via the desktop facade (`matchMedia('(min-width:1025px)')`, `type=module`, excluded from Delay-JS), on elements below the first screen; ScrollSmoother never.' Prefer CSS scroll-driven animations behind @supports for simple reveals.
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse network: no `gsap`, `ScrollTrigger`, `SplitText` requests; desktop run shows them loading after LCP; TBT < 300 ms on both.

findings.claim: The first-screen booking form must use native controls styled only through Global Classes: iOS Safari zooms the page when a focused input's font-size is under 16 px, and WCAG 2.5.8 exempts unmodified user-agent controls, so 16 px inputs with 48 px min-height are both the accessible and the no-surprise choice
findings.detail: WCAG 2.5.8 'User Agent Control' exception text confirmed (W3C Understanding page): 'The size of the target is determined by the user agent and is not modified by the author'. The iOS auto-zoom on inputs < 16 px is long-standing WebKit behaviour (not re-verified against a primary doc in this pass; widely reproduced). Keeping the native date/number/select controls means zero picker JS in the first screen and no engine wake-up dependency; the vendor engine opens on /book or after focus.
findings.breaks_when: Designer insists on a custom-styled calendar in the hero (engine JS before interaction, rule 6; day cells < 24 px; Delay-JS first-tap failure); `font-size: 14px` on inputs (iOS zoom, layout jump that users read as breakage); `-webkit-appearance: none` on the date input removes the native calendar affordance.
findings.how_to_apply: Global Class `form-field`: min-height 48px; font-size 1rem (16 px); border 1px solid var(--color-border) (>= 3:1); do not override appearance on `input[type=date]`; `min` attribute = today; labels visible above fields.
findings.how_to_verify: Playwright webkit (iPhone 14 profile): focus each hero input, `visualViewport.scale` stays 1; computed font-size >= 16 px; calendar opens on first tap in a cold profile.

findings.claim: EAA scope should be stated from the directive text, not vendor blogs: Art. 2(2)(f) e-commerce services from 28 June 2025; Art. 3(30) defines e-commerce as distance services via websites 'with a view to concluding a consumer contract' (so a hotel's own booking/enquiry-to-contract flow is in, a brochure site without contracting is arguably out); Art. 4(5) exempts microenterprises providing services; Art. 32 gives no transition for new websites
findings.detail: Verified on legislation.gov.uk (original EU text of Directive 2019/882): Art. 2(2) 'applies to the following services provided to consumers after 28 June 2025: ... (f) e-commerce services'; Art. 3(23) microenterprise 'employs fewer than 10 persons and ... annual turnover not exceeding EUR 2 million or an annual balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 2 million'; Art. 3(30) e-commerce definition; Art. 4(5) 'Microenterprises providing services shall be exempt'; Art. 32(1) transitional period to 28 June 2030 applies to products used to provide services and to 'service contracts agreed before 28 June 2025 ... no longer than five years'. Greek transposition (Law 4994/2022) and national guidance remain unverified; the harmonised standard is EN 301 549 (WCAG 2.1 AA level).
findings.breaks_when: Agency tells a 12-staff family hotel it is exempt (headcount test fails), or tells a 6-staff villa owner with EUR 2.5 M turnover it is exempt (both turnover and balance-sheet tests must be checked - either one under 2 M suffices for exemption, so check both before deciding); or treats a WooCommerce water-park shop (clearly e-commerce) as out of scope.
findings.how_to_apply: Add a 3-line client intake question to elementor-build: staff count, turnover, balance sheet; record the answer; apply WCAG 2.2 AA regardless (design floor) and publish the accessibility statement when in scope.
findings.how_to_verify: Intake record present per site; Ally scanner + axe pass on 5 templates; accessibility statement page exists for in-scope sites.

title: Implementing sophisticated designs in Elementor 4.x: structure, CSS architecture, custom code
summary: Elementor 4.3.x (source read at elementor/elementor 4.3.5, commit 2e8b3c1, plus Pro 4.3.1 files read read-only from the kand-dev6 site) gives a real CSS-first architecture when the Atomic Editor is on: V4 Variables become plain `:root{--<label>:<value>}` custom properties in the kit CSS file, Global Classes become `.elementor .<label>` rules split into one CSS file per breakpoint (each enqueued with its own `media` attribute), local styles become `.elementor .s-<id>`, and every state/breakpoint/custom-CSS variant lives in the same `styles[].variants[]` JSON that Novamira `elementor-set-content` already writes. That lets one agent build hover/focus micro-interactions (Transition + Transform per state), image treatments (mix-blend-mode, filter, backdrop-filter, aspect-ratio, object-fit, background-clip:text), CSS Grid compositions (spans, dense auto-placement), sticky stacking (CSS `position:sticky`, no JS since V4) and fluid type with zero added JavaScript and no add-on packs. The two JS features Elementor offers for "sophistication" are measured and bounded: Interactions load `motion.min.js` 11.13.5 + `interactions.js` only on pages that hold one (free triggers load/scrollIn; scrollOut/scrollOn/hover/click, custom keyframes, easing, repeat are Pro), and Pro Page Transitions inject a head-blocking `page-transitions.js`, `instant-page` and a full-screen `<e-page-transition>` overlay on every singular/archive page, which the plugin should ban in favour of the zero-JS `@view-transition{navigation:auto}` (Chrome 126 / Safari 18.2) and CSS scroll-driven animations (`animation-timeline:view()`, Chrome 115 / Safari 26) as progressive enhancements below the fold. Custom code placement is now exact: element Custom CSS replaces `selector` with `.elementor-{post} .elementor-element.elementor-element-{id}` inside post-N.css; Site Settings Custom CSS is appended to post-{kit}.css; Pro Custom Code snippets are printed inline at `wp_head`, `wp_body_open` or `wp_footer` priority 21 ordered by `_elementor_priority` 1-10 with Theme Builder conditions; everything else (enqueues with `strategy=>defer`, image sizes, `@font-face` for woff2 variable fonts, Hello reset toggles) is child-theme or sandbox-plugin code. Important reality check for the build pipeline: on the agency's dev sites Novamira 1.12.7 registers none of `elementor-create-global-class`, `elementor-get-style-schema` or `elementor-add-interaction` because `e_atomic_elements` is OFF (`atomic.runtime_available:false`); Elementor 4.3.5 ships its own MCP abilities (`elementor/manage-classes`, `elementor/manage-global-variable`, `elementor/manage-elements` with CSS strings supporting `&:hover` and `@media(--mobile)`) as a second programmatic path once site MCP exposure is enabled.
critic_notes: Method: Elementor 4.3.5 source at /home/user/elementor/elementor (git 2e8b3c1, 2026-10-13) was grepped directly; Pro 4.3.0/4.3.1 files (interactions hooks.php, interactions-pro.js, widget-mega-menu.min.css, directory listings) were read read-only through novamira/read-file and novamira/list-directory on kand.dev6.inglelandi.com; official pages were fetched with curl through the session proxy (WebFetch could not resolve most hosts) and saved as text under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/docs/ (sda.txt, vt.txt, gsap.txt, inter/vars/cc/comp/pt/menu/classes/pos.body.txt, wpenq.txt, mdnat.txt, anime.txt, motion.txt). Open questions answered: Pro hover/click/scrollOn use Motion hover()/press()/scroll() with an autoplay:false animation (ScrollTimeline where supported), Pro JS is 10,991 B min and only loads when core would have; Elementor MCP needs the separate MCP Adapter plugin + Abilities API + exposure toggle; Size variables accept clamp() at the REST/MCP validation layer (UI untested); the Menu widget's focus-within hack is unnecessary (aria-expanded button). Not checked this pass: Loop Grid help text, v3 Mask help, MDN image/CSS baseline pages, Hello parent functions.php filters, Custom Fonts TTF/woff2 acceptance, Design System export coverage, Novamira write-file ability text, whether `custom_css.raw` is base64 (Utils::decode_string) — the researcher's statements on those stand unverified by me. Risk to flag: the Motion version was inferred by matching the bundled file size (290,987 B) to motion@12.23.12 dist/motion.dev.js (289,902 B); treat as '~12.23', not exact.

findings.claim: Where each layer of custom CSS actually lands, its generated selector and its specificity, so the plugin can pick the cheapest layer that wins the cascade without `!important`.
findings.detail: Verified in source. V4 local styles: `Styles_Renderer::DEFAULT_SELECTOR_PREFIX = '.elementor'` + `.`+(`cssName` ?? `id`) → `.elementor .s-hero{...}` (specificity 0,2,0); hover variant → `.elementor .s-hero:hover,.elementor .s-hero:focus-visible{...}` (Style_States maps hover → also focus-visible); breakpoint variant wrapped as `@media(max-width:767px){...}` (direction min/max from kit breakpoints); a variant's `custom_css.raw` is decoded and appended inside the same rule block (`$selector.'{'.$css.$custom_css.'}'`), so `custom_css` written in a class is scoped to that class and state automatically. V4 global classes render `.elementor .<label>` because `Atomic_Global_Styles` replaces `id`/`label` with the ordered label and `transform_classes_names` writes labels into the markup `class=""`. Files: `Atomic_Styles_Manager::render()` writes one file per breakpoint under uploads/elementor/css/ with handle `implode('-', path)` (e.g. `local-<postId>-frontend-mobile.css`, `global-<postId>-frontend-desktop.css`) and enqueues each with `media` = `@media(max-width:767px)` etc. or `all` for the base breakpoint — non-matching breakpoint files are not render-blocking. Pro v3 element Custom CSS (`modules/custom-css/module.php`): `str_replace('selector', $post_css->get_element_unique_selector($element))` → `.elementor-{postId} .elementor-element.elementor-element-{id}` (0,3,0) appended to post-{postId}.css via `elementor/element/parse_css`; Page Settings > Advanced > Custom CSS: `selector` → document wrapper selector, via `elementor/css-file/post/parse`; Site Settings > Settings > Custom CSS (tab id `settings-custom-css`, Pro licence feature `global-css`) is appended to the kit's post-{kitId}.css by the same hook (no `selector` keyword — help: 'Use the selector keyword for individual elements, not page-level CSS or site-level CSS'). V4 Variables are also appended to post-{kit}.css as `:root{--label:value;}` (only when `kits_manager->is_kit($post_css->get_post_id())`). Hello child theme: `hello-elementor-child-style` is enqueued at `wp_enqueue_scripts` priority 20 depending on `hello-elementor-theme-style`; use it for non-Elementor markup (Woo, forms, comments) and for `@font-face`/`@view-transition`/`@keyframes` blocks that need no element scope.
findings.breaks_when: Writing `selector{}` in Site/Page Custom CSS (keyword not replaced, rule silently dead); overriding a V4 class from the child theme with a lower-specificity selector than `.elementor .card` (0,2,0) or relying on load order (Elementor post CSS loads after theme CSS, so equal specificity loses); using `!important` on hover states, which then also blocks the generated `:focus-visible` twin; targeting `.elementor-widget-container` under Optimized Markup (wrapper gone).
findings.how_to_apply: Decision table for the builder: (1) style belongs to a reusable component → Global Class (variants per state/breakpoint, `custom_css.raw` for anything the schema lacks); (2) one-off tweak → element local style variant; (3) rule for non-Elementor DOM, `@font-face`, `@keyframes`, `@view-transition`, `@supports` → child theme `style.css`/`site.css`; (4) third-party `<script>` → Pro Custom Code (finding 8); (5) PHP → sandbox plugin. When a theme rule must beat a V4 class use `.elementor .<label>` or `:where(.elementor) .<label>`-free specificity (0,2,0)+1; never `!important`. Lint: grep child theme and Custom CSS fields for `selector` outside element scope and for `.elementor-widget-container`.
findings.how_to_verify: View-source: `<link id="local-<post>-frontend-mobile-css" media="(max-width:767px)">` style links exist per breakpoint; DevTools Coverage shows the base file render-blocking only; `document.styleSheets` list shows post-{kit}.css containing `:root{--...}`; Lighthouse `render-blocking-insight` lists only base-breakpoint Elementor CSS; grep post-N.css for `/* Start custom CSS for` to confirm element CSS placement.

findings.claim: V4 Variables are a real token system: each variable becomes a CSS custom property named after its label on `:root` in the kit CSS, so custom CSS, child-theme CSS and Interactions-free effects can all reference `var(--color-brand-primary)`.
findings.detail: `CSS_Renderer::build_css_variable_entry()` emits `--{label}:{value};` (the `e-gv-xxxx` id is used as the name only for soft-deleted variables) wrapped in `:root { ... }` and `Hooks::register_css_renderer()` adds it to the kit's post CSS on `elementor/css-file/post/parse`. Types registered: `global-color-variable`, `global-font-variable`, `global-size-variable` (Size is Pro, added in 3.32; Color and Font in 3.31). Quota config 100000 per type. REST (namespace `elementor/v1`, base `variables`): `/list` GET, `/create` POST {type,label,value}, `/update` {id,label,value,type}, `/delete` {id}, `/restore`, `/batch`. Help (26 May 2026): variables 'limited to font family, text color and size (for Pro users)'; typing a value first makes it the default; saving a variable is immediate (no publish). Elementor's own MCP ability `elementor/manage-global-variable` does bulk create/update/delete (1-50 ops) with `type` from `get_allowed_types()`. Variables are kept on kit import (`elementor/kit/meta_to_preserve_on_kit_import`) and exported with the Design System ZIP.
findings.breaks_when: Labels with spaces/Greek are sanitised with `sanitize_text_field` only, so a label like `Primary Color` yields `--Primary Color:` which is invalid CSS and silently drops the whole declaration; two variables with the same label collide; renaming a label changes the CSS variable name and breaks any child-theme `var(--old-name)` references; v3 Pro widgets (Nav Menu, Form, Loop Grid controls) ignore V4 variables and still need kit Global Colors.
findings.how_to_apply: Name variables kebab-case ASCII (`color-brand-primary`, `space-section`, `font-heading`, `radius-card`) and mirror them 1:1 in the kit v3 Global Colors/Fonts for Pro widgets. In child theme or class `custom_css` reference `var(--color-brand-primary)` directly. For a fluid type scale store the clamp() string as a Size variable value (verify acceptance on 4.3.x, see open questions) or put `font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 1.2rem + 2.4vw, 3.5rem)` in the heading class `custom_css`. Create programmatically through Elementor MCP `elementor/manage-global-variable` or `POST /wp-json/elementor/v1/variables/batch`; Novamira exposes no variable ability on the agency sites today.
findings.how_to_verify: Fetch post-{kit}.css and confirm `:root{--color-brand-primary:#...;}` present; in DevTools `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--color-brand-primary')` returns the value; Lighthouse shows no new request (variables add zero files).

findings.claim: Global Classes are the component layer: class name = label, hierarchy = Class Manager order (local always wins), states hover/focus/active/focus-visible/checked plus class-states, hard cap 1000, and only classes used on a page are emitted into that page's `global-*.css` files.
findings.detail: Source: `Global_Classes_REST_API::MAX_ITEMS = 1000` (`global_classes_limit_exceeded`), routes `GET/PUT elementor/v1/global-classes` (PUT body `items`, `order`, `changes{added,deleted,modified,order}`), `/post`, `/styles`, `/usage`. `Atomic_Global_Styles::get_document_global_styles()` collects class ids via `Global_Classes_Relations::get_styles_by_post()` for the post plus embedded posts (header/footer/loop items via `elementor/document/related_posts`) and renders them in Class Manager order, so unused classes cost 0 bytes on other pages. Labels: max 50 chars, duplicates get `DUP_` prefix. States available in `Style_States`: `hover`, `active`, `focus`, `focus-visible`, `checked`; class states `e--selected`, `e--disabled`, `e--playing`, `e--paused`; `hover` selector additionally matches `:focus-visible`. Help (classes, 1 Oct 2026): every element has a `local` class (pink) and global classes (green); 'the local class always has top priority'; priority between globals 'is set in the class manager' (drag-and-drop, 4.0 blog); Convert to global class via the ellipsis next to `local`; Class Manager filters Unused/Empty/Page-specific (3.32); Duplicate. Elementor MCP `elementor/manage-classes`: bulk 1-50 ops, `create` needs `label` + `css` as plain CSS string 'Supports &:hover/&:focus/&:active nesting and @media(--breakpoint) blocks', `mode` patch|replace, `prop: null` removes a prop; `elementor/reorder-classes` sets hierarchy. Third-party reports of a '50 class limit' refer to an older alpha; current cap is 1000.
findings.breaks_when: Two classes on one element set the same property and the Class Manager order is wrong (help example: Secondary_button font applied under Main_button); renaming a class label changes the public class name and breaks child-theme selectors and RUCSS safelists; a class used only inside a popup/template that Pro renders conditionally is not in the page relations until the embedding document is saved (cached relations), so its CSS can be missing after programmatic writes until `elementor-clear-document-cache`/Regenerate CSS.
findings.how_to_apply: Create ≤ 30 semantic classes per site (`btn-primary`, `btn-ghost`, `card`, `card--media`, `section-boxed`, `section-full`, `heading-display`, `eyebrow`, `img-cover`, `img-duotone`), each with desktop/tablet/mobile variants and hover/focus-visible variants, zero local colour/font overrides. Through Novamira today: `elementor-set-content` with `settings.classes` referencing class ids (and `styles` for local); through Elementor MCP: `elementor/manage-classes` create with CSS string, e.g. `{action:'create',label:'card',css:'display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:var(--space-2);border-radius:var(--radius-card);transition:transform .3s ease,box-shadow .3s ease; &:hover{transform:translateY(-4px);box-shadow:0 12px 32px rgb(0 0 0 / .12)} @media(--mobile){gap:12px}'}`. Export via Design System panel for reuse.
findings.how_to_verify: `GET /wp-json/elementor/v1/global-classes` returns items with the expected labels and order; page HTML shows `class="card"` (label, not id); the page's `global-<post>-frontend-*.css` files contain only classes used on that page; Lighthouse unused-CSS for those files is low; keyboard Tab shows hover styles on focus-visible without extra rules.

findings.claim: The exact V4 style-schema property names that `styles.props` / Novamira's flat `styles` map accept — this is the whole 'sophisticated CSS without code' surface (effects, transforms, transitions, grid, position, aspect-ratio, blend modes, background clipping).
findings.detail: From `modules/atomic-widgets/styles/style-schema.php` (4.3.5): size `width height min-width min-height max-width max-height overflow aspect-ratio object-fit object-position`; position `position` (static|relative|absolute|fixed|sticky) `inset-block-start inset-inline-end inset-block-end inset-inline-start z-index scroll-margin-top` (= Anchor offset); typography `font-family font-weight font-size color letter-spacing word-spacing column-count column-gap line-height text-align font-style text-decoration text-transform direction stroke all cursor`; spacing `padding margin` (dimensions `block-start/block-end/inline-start/inline-end`); border `border-radius border-width border-color border-style outline-width outline-color outline-style outline-offset`; background `background` (color/overlay layers image|gradient, clip via Background clipping: Border edges/Padding edges/Content edges/Text); effects `mix-blend-mode` (normal multiply screen overlay darken lighten color-dodge color-burn saturation color difference exclusion hue luminosity soft-light hard-light) `box-shadow opacity filter backdrop-filter transform transition`; layout `display flex-direction gap flex-wrap flex grid-template-columns grid-template-rows grid-auto-flow (row|column|row dense|column dense) grid-auto-rows grid-auto-columns grid-column grid-row` (span types) and alignment `justify-content justify-items align-content align-items align-self order`. Help confirms UI names: Filters (Blur, Brightness, Contrast, Hue Rotate, Saturate, Grayscale, Invert, Sepia, Drop shadow), Backdrop Filters (same list), Transform (Move, Scale, Rotate, Skew; per-state; Z-axis + perspective), Transitions (free: one combined transition; Pro: per-property repeater), Object fit Fill/Cover/Contain/None/Scale down, Aspect ratio dropdown + Custom, Position Sticky now CSS (not JS). Novamira: 'Shapes are auto-detected: every top-level key that matches a v4 Style Schema CSS property ... routes through the ergonomic path'; unknown names return `unknown_style_properties`.
findings.breaks_when: Animating `box-shadow`, `filter: blur()` or `backdrop-filter` on many cards at once (repaint, INP risk on phones; only `transform`/`opacity` stay on the compositor); `backdrop-filter: blur(10px)` on a fixed full-width header repaints on every scroll frame; `mix-blend-mode` creates a stacking context and can break `position: sticky` children; `aspect-ratio` set on an `` without matching width/height attributes still needs the attributes for CLS-free LCP discovery.
findings.how_to_apply: Card recipe (global class `card`): props `display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap; border-radius; background; transition: transform 300ms ease, box-shadow 300ms ease`; hover variant `transform: translateY(-4px); box-shadow: ...`; focus-visible comes free. Image recipe (`img-cover`): `aspect-ratio: 4/3; object-fit: cover; object-position: center`. Duotone (`img-duotone` on the e-image, parent div with brand `background`): `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.1)` + `mix-blend-mode: multiply` (or `screen` on dark). Glass header: `backdrop-filter: blur(8px)` only on the header, never on cards. Overlap: parent `position: relative`, child `position: absolute; inset-*; z-index: 2`. Pass these as the flat `styles` map in `elementor-set-content`/`elementor-add-element`; use verbose variants for hover/mobile.
findings.how_to_verify: `elementor-get-style-schema` (atomic sites) or the write response's `unknown_style_properties`; rendered CSS in `local-*/global-*` files contains the props; DevTools Performance: scrolling over a card grid shows no 'Paint' > 16 ms frames; Lighthouse `total-blocking-time` unchanged and INP p75 < 200 ms after 28 days; mobile CLS ≤ 0.05 with aspect-ratio images.
findings.correction: Add `clip-path`, `content`, `appearance` to the accepted-props list. Prefer `clip-path: inset()/polygon()/url(#id)` over `mask-image` with external SVG for masks on non-LCP media.

findings.claim: Elementor Interactions have an exact JSON shape, a measured loading model (motion.min.js 11.13.5 + interactions.js, enqueued only when a rendered document holds an interaction, data printed as JSON in the footer) and a clear free/Pro split; the plugin can write them with `elementor-set-content` and lint them.
findings.detail: `interactions[]` items (`Interaction_Item_Prop_Type`): `interaction_id` (string, assigned by `Parser` as `<elementId>-N`), `trigger` ∈ `load`, `scrollIn` (free) | `scrollOut`, `scrollOn`, `hover`, `click` (meta pro), `animation` = `{effect: fade|slide|scale (free) | custom (Pro), type: in|out, direction: left|right|top|bottom|top-left|top-right|bottom-left|bottom-right|'', timing_config: {duration, delay} (time-size), config: {replay (Pro), easing: easeIn (free) | easeOut|easeInOut|backIn|backInOut|backOut|linear (Pro), relativeTo (Pro, default 'viewport'), repeat: loop|times|'' (Pro), times, start % (default 85), end % (default 15)}, custom_effect: {keyframes: [{stop, settings:{opacity, move, rotate, scale, skew}}]} (Pro)}`, `breakpoints: {excluded: [...]}`. Defaults: duration 600 ms, delay 0, slide distance 100, scale start 0. Frontend: `Interactions_Frontend_Handler::collect_document_interactions` (filter `elementor/frontend/builder_content_data`, cached in postmeta) → `wp_footer` priority 1 prints `<script type="application/json" id="elementor-interactions-data">[{elementId,dataId,interactions}]</script>` and only then `wp_enqueue_script('motion-js')` (assets/lib/motion/motion.min.js, v11.13.5, footer) + `elementor-interactions`; elements carry `data-interaction-id`. Core `interactions.js` handles only `load|scrollIn|scrollOut` via motion `animate` + `inView` (IntersectionObserver); Pro JS handles hover/click/scrollOn (not inspected). Help (19 Jun 2026): Triggers Page load, Scroll into view, While scrolling (start/end gridlines), On hover, On click; Effects Fade/Slide/Scale; Type In/Out; Direction arrows; Duration/Delay in MS; 'Interactions apply to all devices' (schema now has `breakpoints.excluded`). Blog 3.34: Duration 0.1–3 s, Delay 0–2 s, stackable, Preview button.
findings.breaks_when: Any interaction on an element in the first viewport or on the LCP node (the element's initial keyframe is applied by JS after `motion.min.js` loads in the footer → render delay, same class of failure as `elementor-invisible`); Delay-JS/cache plugin delaying `motion-js`/`elementor-interactions` (reveal never fires until interaction); `repeat: loop` or `scrollOn` on many elements (continuous rAF, INP); hover triggers on touch devices do nothing (no fallback state); more than ~2 interactions per page breaks the plugin's own budget (design-to-elementor §4).
findings.how_to_apply: Allowed pattern per page: ≤ 2 `scrollIn` fade/slide `in` interactions on below-fold sections, duration 400–600 ms, delay 0, excluded breakpoints `['mobile']` when the motion adds nothing on phones. Example node fragment: `"interactions":[{"$$type":"interaction-item","value":{"trigger":{"$$type":"string","value":"scrollIn"},"animation":{"$$type":"animation-preset","value":{"effect":{"$$type":"string","value":"fade"},"type":{"$$type":"string","value":"in"},"direction":{"$$type":"string","value":"bottom"},"timing_config":{"$$type":"timing-config","value":{"duration":{"$$type":"time-size","value":{"size":500,"unit":"ms"}},"delay":{"$$type":"time-size","value":{"size":0,"unit":"ms"}}}}}}}}]` (confirm envelope names with `elementor://interactions/schema` resource or a read-back of an editor-saved element before first write). Lint: first top-level container and header/footer templates must have `interactions: []` on every node; count of non-empty `interactions` ≤ 2; exclude `motion-js` and `elementor-interactions` handles from Delay-JS.
findings.how_to_verify: Page without interactions: no request for `lib/motion/motion.min.js` and no `#elementor-interactions-data` script; page with one: both present, `elementor-interactions-data` JSON lists only intended ids; Lighthouse mobile: LCP element has no `data-interaction-id`, `lcp-phases-insight` render delay < 300 ms, TBT delta < 50 ms; WebPageTest filmstrip shows below-fold sections revealed within 600 ms of entering view.
findings.correction: Replace 'motion.min.js 11.13.5' with 'Motion ~12.23 build, 128 KB min / 42 KB gzip, first-party'. Rewrite breaks_when: above-fold or `load` interactions cause a visible flash + repaint after DOMContentLoaded (not an LCP delay); `load` trigger should be banned outright. Add Pro handles `elementor-interactions-pro` and `elementor-interactions-shared-utils` to Delay-JS exclusions. Note breakpoints.excluded works despite the help text.

findings.claim: CSS scroll-driven animations give 'While scrolling' and 'reveal on scroll' effects with zero JavaScript and off-main-thread execution, now in Chrome 115+ and Safari 26, and degrade to static in Firefox — the right default for below-fold motion in a 95-100 site.
findings.detail: Chrome docs (opened): `animation-timeline: view()` / `scroll(root block)`, `animation-range: entry 25% cover 50%`, `animation-duration: auto`; 'the ability to have scroll-driven animations run off the main thread'; Browser Support box lists 115 (Chrome), 115 (Edge), 26 (Safari); named timelines via `view-timeline-name: --revealing-image`; ranges derive from the untransformed box so scaling during scroll does not flicker. MDN `animation-timeline` page opened for syntax. Example from the doc: `.revealing-image{animation: auto linear reveal both; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 25% cover 50%;} @keyframes reveal{from{opacity:0;scale:.8} to{opacity:1;scale:1}}`. Lighthouse emulation reports `prefers-reduced-motion` false, so gating on it does not help the score but is still correct for users.
findings.breaks_when: Applied above the fold or on the LCP ``/h1 (the element starts at opacity 0 → LCP render delay, exactly like entrance animations); animating layout properties (`height`, `margin`) instead of `transform`/`opacity`/`clip-path` (main-thread); Firefox users see the end state only if `both` fill-mode is used and keyframes start from the visible state fallback — write the CSS inside `@supports (animation-timeline: view())` so unsupported browsers render the normal static design; parent `overflow: hidden` on an Elementor container changes the nearest scroller and the view timeline silently tracks the wrong box.
findings.how_to_apply: Put in the child theme `site.css` (or a global class `custom_css`): `@supports (animation-timeline: view()) { @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .reveal { animation: reveal-up auto linear both; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 10% entry 60%; } .parallax-media img { animation: parallax auto linear both; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: cover 0% cover 100%; } } } @keyframes reveal-up { from { opacity: 0; translate: 0 24px } to { opacity: 1; translate: 0 } } @keyframes parallax { from { translate: 0 -8% } to { translate: 0 8% } }`. Add class `reveal` through `settings.classes` on below-fold cards; never on the hero. Use this instead of Interactions 'While scrolling' and instead of Elementor v3 Scrolling Effects (JS).
findings.how_to_verify: Chrome DevTools Animations panel shows scroll-linked timelines; Performance trace while scrolling shows no scripting; Lighthouse: no change in TBT, LCP element not in `.reveal`; Safari 26 and Chrome render motion, Firefox renders the static final state (screenshot diff at 390 px shows identical layout).

findings.claim: Ban Elementor Pro Page Transitions/Preloader and use cross-document View Transitions (`@view-transition { navigation: auto }`) for page-to-page motion: zero JS, Chrome 126 / Safari 18.2, nothing in Firefox, and no overlay in front of the LCP.
findings.detail: Pro `modules/page-transitions/module.php` (4.3.1, read read-only): when Site Settings > Page Transitions has an Entrance Animation or a Preloader Type, `should_render()` is true on every `is_singular()||is_archive()` non-paged page; it enqueues `page-transitions.js` with `in_footer = false` (head, render/parse-blocking) plus `instant-page` (as module) and prints `<e-page-transition class="e-page-transition--entering" ...>` at `wp_body_open` — a full-page overlay with background colour (default `#FFBC7D`) that animates away (`--e-page-transition-animation-duration` default 1500 ms); options Entrance/Exit animation (fade/zoom/slide variants), Animation Duration up to 5000 ms, Preloader Type None/Animation/Icon/Image with 13 loader animations, Preloader Delay; links can opt out with `data-e-disable-page-transition|true`. Chrome doc (opened): cross-document view transitions supported from Chrome 126 / Edge 126 / Safari 18.2, Firefox none; both pages must be same-origin and opt in with `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }`; customised with `view-transition-name`, `pageswap`/`pagereveal` events (Chrome 124+/Safari 18.2) and `navigation.activation` (Chrome 123, Firefox 147, Safari 26.2); scripts customising transitions must be render-blocking in `<head>` (`blocking=render`) — avoid scripts, use CSS only. Note: a cross-origin redirect in the navigation cancels the transition.
findings.breaks_when: Pro Page Transitions enabled: a 1.5 s overlay precedes first paint on every page (LCP element becomes the overlay or is delayed; PSI measures it), plus a head-blocking script and instant-page prefetch traffic; View Transitions: default root cross-fade on very long pages snapshots the whole document (brief main-thread cost at navigation, not measured by Lighthouse); naming many elements with `view-transition-name` or duplicate names on one page aborts the transition; Polylang language switch to another domain (cross-origin) gets no transition; cache plugins that inline critical CSS must keep the `@view-transition` rule in the always-served CSS.
findings.how_to_apply: Site Settings > Page Transitions: Entrance Animation None, Preloader Type None (lint `elementor_page_transitions_*` kit settings empty). Child theme `site.css`: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { @view-transition { navigation: auto; } ::view-transition-old(root) { animation: 180ms ease-out both fade-out } ::view-transition-new(root) { animation: 220ms ease-in both fade-in } .site-logo { view-transition-name: logo } }` with `@keyframes fade-out/fade-in`. Keep ≤ 3 named elements (logo, page title). Do not add `pageswap`/`pagereveal` scripts.
findings.how_to_verify: view-source shows no `<e-page-transition>` and no `page-transitions.min.js`/`instant-page`; Chrome 126+ DevTools > Animations captures a `::view-transition` pseudo-tree on navigation; Lighthouse mobile LCP unchanged vs. no-transition build (±50 ms) and `lcp-discovery-insight` still names the hero img/h1; Firefox navigation is a plain load with identical layout.

findings.claim: Elementor Pro Custom Code is the correct home for third-party and facade scripts: snippets are CPT `elementor_snippet` posts printed inline at `wp_head`, `wp_body_open` or `wp_footer` priority 21, ordered by priority 1-10, scoped by Theme Builder conditions, and bypassed in `?elementor-mode=safe` — but it is not a dependency-aware enqueue and has no device or consent gating.
findings.detail: Pro `modules/custom-code` (4.3.1): post type `elementor_snippet` (capability `manage_options`, `show_in_rest` true), meta `_elementor_location` ∈ `elementor_head` (default), `elementor_body_start`, `elementor_body_end`; `_elementor_priority` integer 1-10 default 1 (query `orderby meta_value_num ASC, ID ASC`, so 1 prints first); `_elementor_code` (raw HTML; `wp_kses_post` for users without `unfiltered_html`); `_elementor_extra_options` with `ensure_jquery` ('Always load jQuery ... may have a minor impact on loading speed'). `frontend_actions()`: `wp_head` → head snippets, `wp_body_open` → body start, `wp_footer` priority 21 ('After wp_print_footer_scripts') → body end; each location is a Theme Builder location (`register_location`, multiple, not public) and snippets print when `Conditions_Manager::get_documents_for_location()` matches or the snippet has no `_elementor_conditions` (= everywhere). Help (14 Jan 2024): no PHP; CSS allowed inside `<style>` for condition-scoped CSS; linter built in; publish/draft/schedule. REST meta is registered for the three fields (location enum, priority, code) so `POST /wp-json/wp/v2/elementor_snippet` can create a snippet, but conditions are saved from the metabox `_conditions` field and the conditions cache is regenerated on save — set conditions in the UI or via `elementor-set-template-conditions`-style tooling (verify).
findings.breaks_when: Putting GTM/pixels/chat in `<head>` with priority 1 (render-blocking, third-party before LCP; rule: ≤ 150 KB / ≤ 300 ms third-party); `ensure_jquery` on a page that otherwise defers jQuery; snippets with no conditions print on checkout/booking pages; Delay-JS plugins treat inline scripts as delayable unless excluded (LiteSpeed: `data-no-optimize`/non-`text/javascript` type; WP Rocket `nowprocket`; Perfmatters/FlyingPress keyword lists); a `<script type="module">` facade loader placed in Body Start runs before the DOM it targets exists unless it waits for `DOMContentLoaded`.
findings.how_to_apply: Policy: one snippet per third party, Location `</body> - End`, Priority 5-10, Conditions = only the pages that need it (Exclude checkout, booking, landing); CMP loaded directly (not via GTM) with Body Start; desktop-only heavy hero loader (levers §7.1) as `<script type="module" id="hero-3d" data-no-optimize="1" nowprocket>if(matchMedia('(min-width:1025px)').matches) import('/wp-content/themes/CHILD/js/hero-3d.js');</script>` in Body End with conditions = home only. Never `ensure_jquery`. Site-wide CSS never goes into a `<style>` snippet (uncacheable inline, re-sent per page) — use kit Custom CSS or the child theme; condition-scoped CSS only when a single template needs it.
findings.how_to_verify: view-source of a page outside the conditions contains no snippet text; on the target page the snippet sits after `wp_print_footer_scripts` output (last `<script>` block); Lighthouse `third-parties-insight` ≤ 150 KB / ≤ 300 ms on mobile; `render-blocking-insight` lists no inline head script; `?elementor-mode=safe` shows the page without snippets (sanity check).

findings.claim: What needs theme code instead of the editor, and how Novamira can write it: enqueues with WordPress loading strategies, image sizes, `@font-face` for woff2 variable fonts, Hello reset toggles, Polylang conditions — with PHP restricted to the Novamira sandbox plugin and non-PHP assets writable anywhere.
findings.detail: WordPress: `wp_enqueue_script($handle,$src,$deps,$ver,['strategy'=>'defer','in_footer'=>true])` (6.3+; 'the most eligible loading strategy is applied' across the dependency tree, never stricter than requested); `wp_enqueue_script_module($id,$src,$deps,$ver,['in_footer'=>...])` (6.5+; `in_footer` 'Only relevant to block themes'); Elementor hooks `elementor/frontend/after_enqueue_styles` and `elementor/frontend/after_enqueue_scripts` fire when Elementor frontend assets are registered/enqueued (use them so your handle can depend on `elementor-frontend`). Hello theme `functions.php` (master): styles `hello-elementor` (reset.css, filter `hello_elementor_enqueue_style`), `hello-elementor-theme-style` (theme.css, filter `hello_elementor_enqueue_theme_style`), `hello-elementor-header-footer` (filter `hello_elementor_header_footer`); the Hello settings screen (help, 25 Sep 2026) exposes toggles Disable description meta tag, Disable skip link, Disable theme header & footer, Hide page title, Deregister Hello reset.css, Deregister Hello theme.css, all off by default. Hello child: `hello-elementor-child-style` depends on `hello-elementor-theme-style` at priority 20 — if you deregister theme.css the dependency must be dropped or the child style never loads. Variable fonts: Pro Custom Fonts 'Add Variable Font' accepts a `.ttf` ('Select ttf file') and needs Weight/Width min-max; woff2 variable fonts (Inter latin 47 KB in the plugin's measurements) therefore go in the child theme as `@font-face{font-family:'Inter';src:url(/wp-content/themes/CHILD/fonts/inter-latin-greek.woff2) format('woff2');font-weight:100 900;font-display:swap;unicode-range:U+0000-00FF,U+0370-03FF}` and the family name is referenced by a V4 Font variable (free-text value) — verify the picker accepts a non-registered family. Novamira `write-file`: 'PHP files (*.php) ... can ONLY be written to the sandbox directory (wp-content/novamira-sandbox/)', loaded by an mu-plugin loader with crash safe-mode (`.crashed` marker); 'Other non-PHP files can intentionally go anywhere under ABSPATH' → child theme `assets/css/site.css`, `assets/js/*.js`, fonts (binary via `create-upload-link`).
findings.breaks_when: Writing PHP into the child theme via `write-file` (refused); a fatal in a sandbox file puts all sandbox plugins into safe mode (site keeps running, features vanish); `strategy=>defer` on a script whose dependents are inline blocking scripts is silently downgraded; deregistering Hello theme.css without re-adding form/comment resets breaks Woo and comment forms; `font-weight: 100 900` with a static (non-variable) file renders faux-bold.
findings.how_to_apply: Sandbox plugin `wp-content/novamira-sandbox/agency-site.php`: image sizes (`add_image_size('hero-mobile',780,0)` + `image_size_names_choose`), `add_filter('elementor_pro/custom_fonts/font_display', fn()=>'swap')`, AVIF quality filter, Polylang `general/pll_language_<slug>` conditions, `add_filter('hello_elementor_enqueue_style','__return_false')` only when the child theme carries its own reset, and `add_action('elementor/frontend/after_enqueue_scripts', function(){ wp_enqueue_script('site-ux', get_stylesheet_directory_uri().'/assets/js/site-ux.js', ['elementor-frontend'], '1.0', ['strategy'=>'defer','in_footer'=>true]); })`. Child theme files via `write-file`: `assets/css/site.css` (fonts, view transitions, scroll-driven animations, non-Elementor markup) enqueued after `hello-elementor-child-style`. Keep all JS ≤ 20 KB gzip and deferred; nothing executes before LCP.
findings.how_to_verify: `novamira/list-directory wp-content/novamira-sandbox` shows the file and no `.crashed`; view-source: `<script defer src=".../site-ux.js">` after Elementor frontend; DevTools Network font filter shows ≤ 4 woff2 from the site origin with `font-weight 100 900` in the `@font-face`; Greek paragraph renders in the brand font (ά, ώ, ς); Lighthouse `font-display-insight` clean; `render-blocking-insight` lists no theme JS.

findings.claim: Layout techniques for asymmetric, overlapping, full-bleed and sticky-stacking compositions map to exact V4 controls and CSS, and V4 sticky is pure CSS (no `jquery.sticky`), so the layouts cost zero JS.
findings.detail: V4 Grid (help, 20 Jul 2026, free): Layout panel 'Grid columns, rows, gaps, and auto-flow settings ... any CSS unit, including fr'; 'Show Grid Outline' is editor-only; Grid Child settings 'Grid Column / Grid Row' span, 'Align Self & Order'; 'Dense auto-placement' fills holes left by spanned items; a Flex container can be switched to Grid in the Layout panel. Schema props: `grid-template-columns`, `grid-template-rows`, `grid-auto-flow` (row|column|row dense|column dense), `grid-auto-rows`, `grid-auto-columns`, `grid-column`/`grid-row` spans, `order`, `align-self`. Position (help, 7 Aug 2026): Static/Relative/Absolute/Fixed/Sticky; 'In Version 4, Elementor switched from using JavaScript to the CSS Sticky property ... it will not work if the parent element is set to Overflow hidden'; Absolute is relative to the closest Relative ancestor; tip for overlap: Absolute + Z-index ≥ 1 + top/left numbers, 'Do not use margin settings for absolute positioning'; Anchor offset (= `scroll-margin-top`) for sticky headers. v3 containers keep Advanced > Custom Positioning (Absolute/Fixed, Horizontal/Vertical Orientation Start/End, offsets in px/%/vw/vh) and Advanced > Motion Effects > Sticky (Top/Bottom, Sticky On devices, Offset, Effects Offset, Anchor offset, Stay in Column — JS-driven, class `elementor-sticky--effects`). Scroll Snap (Page Settings > Advanced > Scroll Snap: Snap Position Top/Center/Bottom, Scroll Padding px, Scroll Snap Stop Normal/Always) works on pages only, not templates. Container widths: kit `container_width` (kand-dev6 reports 1920 px with 0 padding), so 'boxed' must be modelled explicitly with a `section-boxed` class.
findings.breaks_when: `position: sticky` child inside any ancestor with `overflow: hidden` (common on Elementor containers used for rounded corners/masks) — silently not sticky; stacking cards taller than the viewport on 390 px phones (card never fully visible); `grid-template-columns` with fixed px tracks overflowing 390 px (horizontal scroll, CLS); Absolute-positioned decorative elements without `max-width`/`inset` clamps leaking outside the viewport on mobile; v3 Sticky with Effects Offset plus Custom CSS state classes when the cache plugin delays `elementor-pro` JS (header jumps); 'Hide on mobile' as a layout strategy (still downloads).
findings.how_to_apply: Section pattern: `e-div-block.section-full` (full-bleed band: `background`, `padding-block: var(--space-section)`) → `e-flexbox|e-grid.section-boxed` (`width:100%; max-width: var(--container-max, 1200px); margin-inline:auto; padding-inline: clamp(16px, 4vw, 40px)`), depth ≤ 4. Full-bleed media inside a boxed parent (rare, prefer the band pattern): `.bleed{ width:100vw; margin-inline: calc(50% - 50vw) }` in class custom_css. Asymmetric editorial grid: `e-grid` with `grid-template-columns: repeat(6, minmax(0,1fr))`, `grid-auto-flow: row dense`, children `grid-column: span 4|span 2`, mobile variant `grid-template-columns: 1fr` and spans reset to `span 1`. Overlapping cards: parent `position: relative`, child `position: absolute; inset-block-end: -32px; inset-inline-end: 16px; z-index: 2`, mobile variant `position: static`. Sticky stacking cards: wrapper `e-div-block` with `overflow: visible`, each card `position: sticky; inset-block-start: calc(var(--header-h) + 16px); z-index` incrementing, heights ≤ 70vh on mobile, no `overflow:hidden` on ancestors (round corners via `border-radius` + `clip-path` on the card itself). Header: V4 `position: sticky; inset-block-start: 0` instead of v3 Motion Effects Sticky.
findings.how_to_verify: Screenshots at 390/768/1024/1440 px match the design frame within 5 px (kallyas parity loop); `document.documentElement.scrollWidth === innerWidth` at 390 px (no horizontal overflow); DevTools Layout shows grid overlay; sticky cards tested by scrolling in Chrome and Safari; Lighthouse CLS ≤ 0.05 and no `jquery.sticky`/`elementor-sticky` request on V4 pages; `dom-size-insight` depth ≤ 4 from `content[]`.
sources: novamira/elementor-check-setup output on kand.dev6.inglelandi.com (kit container_width 1920, padding 0)

findings.claim: Image treatments (masks, duotone, blend, aspect-ratio/object-fit, background-clip text) are available as native controls or 2-3 CSS lines in a class, and are compatible with the hero `` rules as long as the LCP image itself stays an unmasked ``.
findings.detail: v3 Advanced > Mask (help, 28 Sep 2025): Mask toggle; Shape Circle/Flower/Sketch/Triangle/Blob/Hexagon/Custom (PNG or SVG upload); Fit: Fit/Fill/Custom; Position 9 options; Repeat No Repeat/Repeat/Repeat-X/Repeat-Y/Round/Space — implemented with CSS `mask-image` (MDN: Baseline widely available since Dec 2023, `-webkit-mask-image` prefixes handled by Elementor's CSS). V4 (3.33+): Blend Mode control = `mix-blend-mode` with 16 values; Filters and Backdrop Filters (blur, brightness, contrast, hue-rotate, saturate, grayscale, invert, sepia, drop-shadow); Background clipping Border edges/Padding edges/Content edges/Text; Size > Object fit Fill/Cover/Contain/None/Scale down + Object position; Aspect ratio dropdown + Custom. MDN baselines opened: `mix-blend-mode` (Jan 2020), `aspect-ratio` (Sep 2021), `object-fit` (Jan 2020), `<filter-function>` (Sep 2016), `<textPath>` (Jul 2015). Duotone needs no image processing: grayscale filter + tinted parent background + multiply/screen blend; all of it paints on the GPU and ships 0 bytes.
findings.breaks_when: Mask or `mix-blend-mode` applied to the hero LCP `` with a heavy custom SVG mask (extra request before the hero paints; Lighthouse may pick the h1 but the image appears late); `backdrop-filter` on scrolling content (repaint per frame); custom PNG masks > 50 KB; blend modes on an element whose parent has `isolation`/stacking changes (effect disappears); `background-clip: text` headings need a solid fallback colour for Firefox screenshots/Reader mode and must not be the LCP text node on a slow background image (text paints only when the image paints — keep gradient backgrounds, not image backgrounds, for clipped headings).
findings.how_to_apply: Global classes: `img-cover {aspect-ratio: 4/3; object-fit: cover; width:100%}`; `img-duotone {filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05); mix-blend-mode: multiply}` on the `e-image` inside a `e-div-block` with `background: var(--color-brand-primary)`; `img-rounded-blob` via Advanced > Mask Shape Blob (v3) or custom_css `mask-image:url(/wp-content/themes/CHILD/img/blob.svg); mask-size: contain; mask-repeat: no-repeat; mask-position:center` (inline the SVG ≤ 2 KB as data URI to avoid a request); `heading-gradient {background: linear-gradient(90deg,var(--color-brand-primary),var(--color-accent)); -webkit-background-clip:text; background-clip:text; color: transparent}` with mobile variant falling back to `color: var(--color-text); background: none` if contrast fails. Keep the hero `` plain; apply treatments to secondary imagery.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse `largest-contentful-paint-element` still the plain hero img/h1; no new image/SVG requests for masks (data URIs) or ≤ 1 small SVG; Performance trace while scrolling shows paint < 16 ms per frame; axe/Lighthouse contrast checks pass on text over blended images; Firefox screenshot of clipped heading shows gradient text (supported) or fallback colour.

findings.claim: Typographic effects: fluid type with `clamp()`, variable-font axes, and text on a path with SVG `<textPath>` — all static CSS/SVG, with the exact Elementor entry points and the one gotcha (Custom Fonts' variable path wants TTF).
findings.detail: MDN `clamp()` (Baseline Jul 2020): `font-size: clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 2rem)` 'has the same effect as ... Fluid Typography but in one line, and without the use of media queries'. V4 typography props accept `font-size`, `line-height`, `letter-spacing` as Size prop types with typography units (`Size_Constants::typography()`); a `clamp()` string must go either into a Size variable value (string, Pro) or into class `custom_css` — the help page does not state clamp() support for Size variables, so treat it as verify-on-site. Variable fonts (help, 1 Oct 2026): WP Admin Elementor > Editor > Custom elements > Add New font > Add Variable Font, 'Select ttf file', check Width and/or Weight and enter min/max ('You must set a minimum and maximum weight and/or width'); fonts then appear under 'Variable fonts' with Weight/Width sliders; only `wght`/`wdth` axes supported. Text on path: MDN `<textPath href="#path">` (Baseline since Jul 2015) — put an inline `<svg viewBox="0 0 600 200" aria-hidden="true"><path id="arc" d="M20,180 Q300,-60 580,180" fill="none"/><text><textPath href="#arc" startOffset="50%" text-anchor="middle">Villa Thalassa</textPath></text></svg>` in an `e-svg`/HTML widget, styled with `font: inherit; fill: var(--color-brand-primary)`, and keep the real heading as a visually-hidden `h2` for a11y/SEO. Plugin budget still applies: 2 families, ≤ 4 woff2, ~100 KB, swap, Greek subset.
findings.breaks_when: Uploading a 300 KB unsubsetted TTF through Custom Fonts (Latin+Greek variable TTF often 600 KB+) blows the font budget and ships `.ttf` (uncompressed) — the plugin's rules say woff2 only; `clamp()` with a `vw` middle term and no `rem` component fails WCAG 1.4.4 zoom (text does not scale with user font-size) — always `clamp(min, rem + vw, max)`; `` text as the LCP/h1 (SVG text is not an `` nor a text node Lighthouse treats well, and it is not selectable/readable by some screen readers without the hidden heading); animating variable-font axes (font-weight transitions) causes continuous re-layout.
findings.how_to_apply: Child theme `site.css`: `@font-face{font-family:'Inter';src:url(.../inter-var-latin-greek.woff2) format('woff2');font-weight:100 900;font-display:swap;unicode-range:U+0000-00FF,U+0131,U+0152-0153,U+2000-206F,U+20AC,U+0370-03FF}`; preload only the heading file. V4 Font variable `font-heading = Inter`, `font-body = Inter`. Classes: `heading-display {font-family: var(--font-heading); font-weight: 650; font-size: clamp(2rem, 1.2rem + 3.2vw, 4.5rem); line-height: 1.05; letter-spacing: -0.02em}` via `custom_css` for the clamp line if the Size control rejects it; `text-balance` via `custom_css: text-wrap: balance`. Text on path only as decoration below the fold, inside `e-svg` with `aria-hidden="true"`.
findings.how_to_verify: DevTools Network font filter: ≤ 4 same-origin woff2, no `.ttf`; computed `font-size` of h1 at 390 px vs 1440 px within the clamp range; browser zoom 200% enlarges the heading (rem term present); Greek glyphs render in the brand font; Lighthouse `font-display-insight` clean and LCP element is the h1 text or hero img, never the SVG.

findings.claim: Mega menu and off-canvas done cleanly: the Pro Menu widget (needs Flexbox Containers + Nested Elements + Menu experiments) exposes per-item 'Dropdown Content', one 'Content Width' for the whole menu, 'Open On' Click/Hover and a 'Breakpoint' None/Mobile Portrait/Tablet Portrait; the Off-Canvas widget is the mobile drawer with ESC/overlay/scroll-lock controls and should run with Entrance Animation None or Fade In.
findings.detail: Menu widget help (opened): experimental; activating it 'will replace the Nav Menu widget with two new widgets – the WordPress Menu widget (which functions like the Nav Menu widget), and the Menu widget'; per item Title, Link (dynamic Site > Internal URL), Dropdown Content toggle (arrow appears, a container opens under the item for any widgets, even another Menu widget — but 'You cannot put a menu widget inside another menu widget'), Icon, CSS ID; Layout: Content Width 'Full Width' | 'Fit To Content' ('applies to the entire menu'), Item Layout Horizontal | Dropdown, Open On Click | Hover, Animation + Animation Duration, Menu Toggle icon/alignment, Horizontal Scroll Disable/Enable, Breakpoint None | 'Mobile Portrait (>767px)' | 'Tablet Portrait (>1024)'. Off-Canvas help (15 Sep 2026): requires Flexbox Containers and Nested Elements; cannot be used in loop/nested carousels; Editing Mode toggle; Horizontal Position right/left/center, Vertical Position top/center/bottom, Width slider, Height Fit to Content | Custom; Animation Entrance/Exit dropdowns (Fading, Zooming, Bouncing, Sliding, Rotating, Attention Seekers, Light Speed, Specials); Interactions: Prevent Closing on Overlay, Prevent Closing on ESC, Disable Page Scrolling; HTML tag H1–H6/Div/Span/Paragraph; Style: Background, Border, Box Shadow, Overlay (toggle, Background Type, Color, Image); opened from any link field via dynamic tag Actions > Off Canvas > 'Choose Off Canvas widget'; multiple off-canvas widgets are numbered top-down. Plugin's measured costs (design-to-elementor §2): Mega Menu adds smartmenus 6.9 KB + `widget-mega-menu.min.css` 2.7 KB render-blocking; mobile-menu-as-popup adds a second document and post-N.css on every page.
findings.breaks_when: Dropdown Content holding a Form, Google Map, Loop Grid or Lottie (rendered server-side on every page in the header, hidden with CSS — the plugin's 'Hide on mobile' trap); Open On Hover with touch devices (opens on tap anyway, but hover-only intent fails) and no visible focus styles for keyboard users; Off-Canvas Entrance 'Bounce/Rotate/Light Speed' (long JS-driven keyframes, layout jank on phones); header elements with entrance animation (rule 13); menu built as a Popup (second nav + logo + CSS on every page); RUCSS removing `.e-n-menu-content`, `.elementor-off-canvas`, `.e-off-canvas__*` states — safelist them.
findings.how_to_apply: Desktop: Menu widget, Item Layout Horizontal, Open On Hover + CSS `:focus-within` fallback via class custom_css (`.e-n-menu-item:focus-within .e-n-menu-content{display:block}` — verify selector on the site), Content Width Fit To Content, Animation None, dropdown content = headings, text links, one `e-image` ≤ 40 KB. Mobile: Breakpoint Mobile Portrait (>767px) or Tablet Portrait (>1024) so the compact dropdown takes over; or Off-Canvas: Horizontal Position right, Width 86 %, Height Fit to Content, Entrance Fade In / Exit Fade Out (or none), Prevent Closing on ESC = No, Disable Page Scrolling = default, Overlay on with 40 % colour; trigger = a Button with Link → dynamic Actions > Off Canvas. Header template: no interactions, logo with exact width/height, V4 sticky via Position Sticky. RUCSS safelist: `.e-n-menu-content .e-n-menu-item .elementor-off-canvas .e-off-canvas__main .e-off-canvas__overlay .e-off-canvas--open .elementor-sticky--effects`.
findings.how_to_verify: Header HTML size < 40 KB and only one `<nav>`; no `post-N.css` for a popup on pages that do not open one; Lighthouse mobile: `render-blocking-insight` lists at most `widget-mega-menu.min.css`; keyboard: Tab opens dropdowns and ESC closes the off-canvas; axe: menu toggle has an accessible name and `aria-expanded`; breakage checklist 'mobile menu open, sticky header' screenshots at 390 px.
findings.correction: Drop the `:focus-within` custom CSS; rely on the built-in `aria-expanded` button and just style `.e-n-menu-dropdown-icon:focus-visible`. RUCSS safelist must include `.e-active`, `.e-n-menu-dropdown-icon`, `[aria-expanded]`, `.e-n-menu-mobile`, `.e-n-menu-tablet`, `.e-n-menu-layout-dropdown`, `.e-n-menu-toggle`, `.e-current`, in addition to `.e-n-menu-content`/`.e-n-menu-item`. Record the CSS as ~20 KB raw / ~2.7 KB compressed render-blocking.

findings.claim: Loop Grid is the repeated-content engine: exact control names for templates, alternate templates (position, Apply Once, Static item position, Column Span), query and pagination, with 'Load on Click' + registered image sizes as the performance-safe configuration.
findings.detail: Loop Grid help (19 Jun 2026): Layout → 'Choose template type' Posts | Post Taxonomy | Products | Product Taxonomy ('Your products will not display in a Posts template type Loop Grid'), 'Choose a template' / 'Edit template', Columns, Items Per Page, Masonry, Equal height (applies to all parent containers in the loop), 'Apply an alternate template'; Query → Source (Posts, Pages, Landing pages, Manually selected, 'The Current Query', Related), Include/Exclude, Include By/Exclude By, Date, Hide Empty, Filter by depth, Order By, Order DESC/ASC, Ignore Sticky Posts, Query ID; Pagination → Numbers | Previous/Next | Numbers + Previous/Next | Load on Click | Infinite Scroll, Page Limit, Shorten, Alignment, 'Load type' Page Reload | AJAX ('Reloads only the loop grid widget'), 'Individual Pagination' (all grids on a page must match), Nothing Found Message (text, alignment, HTML tag). Alternate template help (2 Sep 2025): toggle 'Apply an alternate template', 'Alternate Template' picker, 'Position in grid', 'Apply Once' (default off = repeats every Nth), 'Static item position' (inject without overriding items), 'Column Span', multiple alternates via copy icon or 'Add Item'; not available for Post Taxonomy type. Pagination help: Load on click 'will insert the next page, while leaving the previous page visible' with customizable button, icon, Button ID, 'No More Posts Message'; Infinite Scroll shows a spinner and 'users scrolling will often be interrupted as new items need time to load'. Plugin data: loop item cost = N copies of the template + one inline `<style id="loop-N">`; Loop Carousel = Swiper 38 KB.
findings.breaks_when: Loop item template images with Image Resolution 'Custom' or 'Full' (hand-built lazy `` without width/height/srcset → CLS and oversized downloads × N items); `_animation` on the Loop Grid or loop item (grid invisible until JS); Infinite Scroll on mobile (continuous XHR + layout shifts); Equal height with Masonry (ignored/odd gaps); alternate template with Column Span 2 on a 1-column mobile grid (overflow); AJAX pagination with Element Cache on (stale fragments); a Taxonomy Filter + JetSmartFilters on the same grid (double query scripts).
findings.how_to_apply: One loop-item template per content type (room, offer, post, product) built from containers + `card` class, image via Image widget with a registered size (`card-2x`), heading h3, excerpt, button; Loop Grid: Columns 3/2/1 per device, Items Per Page 6-9, Masonry off, Equal height on, Pagination Load on Click (Page Limit 5), Load type AJAX only for Numbers styles, Individual Pagination on when two grids share a page; editorial rhythm via 'Apply an alternate template' (e.g. wide feature card at Position 1 with Column Span 2, Apply Once on; promo card Static item position at Position 4). Never Loop Carousel above the fold; Loop Grid itself never in the first viewport on landing pages.
findings.how_to_verify: Rendered grid `` tags carry width/height/srcset and a registered size URL (`-800x600`), none `-scaled`; no `elementor-invisible` on `.elementor-loop-container`; Lighthouse mobile CLS ≤ 0.05 after clicking Load More (manual check); request count for the archive page ≤ 50; `

findings.claim: Programmatic reality check: on the agency's dev sites Novamira registers none of `elementor-create-global-class`, `elementor-get-style-schema`, `elementor-add-interaction` or any variable ability because the atomic runtime is off; the build pipeline must gate on `elementor-check-setup`, and Elementor 4.3.5's built-in MCP abilities are a second route for classes, variables, elements and interactions.
findings.detail: `novamira/mcp-adapter-discover-abilities` on kand.dev6.inglelandi.com (Elementor 4.3.3, Pro 4.3.1, Novamira 1.12.7 + Pro 1.11.0, WP 7.1.3, PHP 8.3.36) returned 172 abilities; the Elementor set is exactly: get-content, set-content, create/list/get/edit/delete-template, get/set-template-conditions, add-element, edit-element, delete-element, delete-element-style, get-schema, list-v3-styles, create/edit/delete-v3-color, create/edit/delete-v3-typography, list-dynamic-tags, get-dynamic-tag, apply-dynamic-tag, check-setup, clear-document-cache. platonos.dev6 (Polylang Pro 3.8.10, Novamira Pro 1.10.1): 129 abilities, same 24 Elementor ones. `elementor-add-element`'s own description references `novamira/elementor-create-global-class.styles`, `novamira/elementor-create-atomic-widget.base_styles` and `novamira/elementor-get-style-schema` 'on atomic-capable sites', and `elementor-check-setup` on kand-dev6 returned `atomic.runtime_available:false, style_schema_available:false, global_classes_available:false, variables_available:false, interactions_available:false` with the issue 'the `e_atomic_elements` experiment is OFF ... Enable Elementor → Settings → Features → "Atomic Widgets" (and optionally "Editor V4")'. Novamira `write-file`: PHP only under `wp-content/novamira-sandbox/`, other files anywhere. Elementor core 4.3.5 `modules/mcp` (requires WP Abilities API `wp_register_ability`, `WP\MCP\Core\McpAdapter`, and site exposure enabled via `McpSettingsController::is_enabled()`) registers abilities `elementor/manage-classes` (bulk create/update/delete with plain CSS incl. `&:hover` and `@media(--mobile)`), `elementor/reorder-classes`, `elementor/manage-global-variable`, `elementor/manage-elements` (ops with `settings`, `styles` as CSS string + `style_apply_mode` patch|replace, `global_classes` labels, `interactions` 'array of interaction items in the native shape ... Read elementor://interactions/schema'), `elementor/manage-component`, `elementor/manage-default-styles`, `elementor/get-widget-schema`, `elementor/get-page-structure`, `elementor/build-composition`, `elementor/create-page`, `elementor/publish-document`, `elementor/create-preview-link`, `elementor/update-page-settings`, resources `elementor/global-classes-resource`, `elementor/global-variables-resource`, `elementor/interactions-schema-resource`. REST fallbacks exist for classes (`PUT elementor/v1/global-classes`) and variables (`elementor/v1/variables/batch`).
