findings.breaks_when: The builder assumes `elementor-create-global-class`/`elementor-add-interaction` exist and the run aborts mid-page with half-written content (set-content with `[]` wipes a document); enabling Atomic Widgets on an existing v3 site changes the editor for every page (owner OK, staging first — 4.0 blog: existing sites unchanged until enabled; Novamira refuses mixed v3/atomic subtrees); Elementor MCP site exposure is an admin-level switch that opens write abilities to any connected MCP client (treat as owner OK, scope the client); `elementor/manage-elements` CSS strings bypass Novamira's validation/read-back.
findings.how_to_apply: Pipeline step 0 on every site: `elementor-check-setup` → if `atomic.runtime_available` is false, either stop and request 'Atomic Editor → Activate the new experience' (staging first) or fall back to v3 containers + kit globals (`elementor-create-v3-color/typography`) and skip Interactions entirely (v3 has only entrance animations, which the plugin bans above the fold). Step 1: re-run `mcp-adapter-discover-abilities` after enabling atomic and record which of `elementor-create-global-class`, `elementor-get-style-schema`, `elementor-add-interaction`, `elementor-create-atomic-widget` appear; read each with `get-ability-info` before first use. Step 2: where Novamira lacks a surface, use Elementor MCP (`elementor/manage-classes`, `elementor/manage-global-variable`) if site MCP exposure is enabled, else `novamira/run-wp-cli` with `wp eval` calling the REST handlers, else create in the editor. Theme assets always via `write-file`; PHP via a sandbox plugin.
findings.how_to_verify: `elementor-check-setup` JSON shows all five `atomic.*` flags true before any `e-*` write; `discover-abilities` lists the four atomic abilities; a dry run creates one global class and reads it back via `GET /wp-json/elementor/v1/global-classes`; `elementor-get-content` returns the written ids; the editor opens the page without a migration notice.
sources: novamira/mcp-adapter-discover-abilities output (kand.dev6.inglelandi.com, 172 abilities; platonos.dev6.inglelandi.com, 129 abilities) — saved under /root/.claude/projects/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/tool-results/

findings.claim: Pro Components (V4) are the right vehicle for repeated sections (CTA bands, room cards with exposed text/image props) and keep styling in Global Classes; they are atomic-only, Pro-only and admin-only, so the plugin should use them for consistency, not as a performance lever.
findings.detail: Components help (2 Feb 2026): 'reusable design blocks that remain globally synced ... while permitting per-instance customization'; requirements: 'Components can only be created using Atomic elements', 'Only users with Admin-level permissions can create and edit components', 'You must have Elementor Pro'; create via right-click container → Create component → name; in Edit Mode click the properties icon next to a General-tab field ('Only the settings in the General tab displaying the properties logo can be customized') to expose text/media/link/HTML tag per instance; publish from Edit Mode (component only) or with the page; instances added from the Components tab in the Elements panel. Elementor MCP `elementor/manage-component` exists (`overridable_props` mapping keys to element/prop/label per the jsDelivr-mirrored ability doc found in search; `list-components` ability). Elementor's own blog frames Components alongside Variables and Classes as the three reuse layers; the plugin's loop-item templates remain the tool for query-driven repetition.
findings.breaks_when: Overriding styles per instance (not possible — only General-tab props; designers expecting per-instance colours will add local classes and break the token system); component instances in header/footer templates multiply their CSS into every page's global/local files if styled locally instead of via classes; non-admin editors cannot fix a component; exporting a kit without components (verify export coverage before relying on it for the agency blueprint).
findings.how_to_apply: Build `cta-band`, `room-card`, `testimonial`, `stat` as components from `e-div-block` trees that reference only Global Classes and Variables; expose heading text, paragraph, image, button text/link; place instances inside `e-grid` sections; for dynamic content (rooms from CPT) still use Loop Grid + loop-item template. Lint component trees like pages: depth ≤ 4, `e-image` with registered size, no interactions.
findings.how_to_verify: Editing the master changes every instance (spot-check two pages); page CSS files do not grow per instance (compare `local-*.css` sizes with 1 vs 5 instances); Element Manager usage scan shows no add-on widgets inside components.

findings.claim: GSAP is now 100% free for everyone including all formerly paid Club plugins (ScrollTrigger, SplitText, MorphSVG, ScrollSmoother) — but its byte cost, not its licence, is what the plugin must budget, and ScrollSmoother must stay banned.
findings.detail: gsap.com/pricing (opened, (c)2026 'GSAP - A Webflow Product'): 'GSAP is now 100% free for all users, thanks to Webflow's support.' Current npm version 3.15.0 (jsDelivr resolved). Minified sizes on jsDelivr: gsap.min.js 72,927 B, ScrollTrigger.min.js 44,575 B, SplitText.min.js 7,732 B, MorphSVGPlugin.min.js 21,195 B, ScrollSmoother.min.js 13,373 B (raw minified, roughly 1/3 after gzip/brotli). Core + ScrollTrigger is ~118 KB minified (~40 KB compressed) of first-party JS that executes on the main thread; ScrollSmoother hijacks native scrolling, which breaks CSS `position: sticky`, CSS scroll-driven animations and scroll-anchoring, and raises INP.
findings.breaks_when: GSAP loaded site-wide or before interaction on mobile (TBT and bytes); ScrollSmoother or `scrub` animations on layout properties; SplitText on the h1 (LCP text re-rendered as spans after JS); GSAP used for what CSS scroll-driven animations or Interactions already do.
findings.how_to_apply: Allow GSAP only for a desktop-only, below-fold showpiece (same rule as the hero-3d loader in finding 8/9): `import('/wp-content/themes/CHILD/js/showpiece.js')` guarded by `matchMedia('(min-width:1025px)')` and `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, self-hosted modules `gsap/dist/gsap.min.js` + `ScrollTrigger.min.js` only, loaded after `requestIdleCallback`/first interaction. Lint: no `gsap` request in a mobile Lighthouse run; never ScrollSmoother.
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse network list contains no gsap/ScrollTrigger; desktop trace shows GSAP fetched after LCP; `document.documentElement.scrollHeight` unchanged and `position: sticky` elements still stick (no ScrollSmoother wrapper).

findings.claim: Current library sizes the builder must budget against: anime.js 4.5.0 UMD bundle is 118 KB minified (ESM tree-shakes), Motion is at 14.5.0, and a page that already has an Elementor Interaction has `window.Motion` (~12.23 build, 42 KB gzip) loaded in the footer — reuse it instead of adding a second animation library.
findings.detail: jsDelivr: animejs latest 4.5.0, `/dist/bundles/anime.umd.min.js` 118,043 B, `/dist/bundles/anime.esm.min.js` 118,678 B; the docs install page shows `import { animate } from 'animejs'` and ESM CDN `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/animejs/+esm` (tree-shakable, so a bundled `animate`-only build is far smaller — measure per build). motion latest 14.5.0; motion.dev quick-start: 'When a value can be hardware accelerated, like x, y, opacity, filter or transform etc, it will be' and 'scroll() binds animations to scroll progress, hardware-accelerated where supported'. Elementor exposes its bundled Motion as the UMD global `Motion` (header of assets/lib/motion/motion.min.js) only on pages whose documents contain an interaction (`print_interactions_data` early return otherwise).
findings.breaks_when: Adding anime.js or a second Motion copy on a page that already ships Elementor's Motion (double ~40 KB); relying on `window.Motion` on pages without interactions (it is not loaded); using `motion@latest` CDN URLs (unpinned, cross-origin, not cacheable by the site's own cache plugin).
findings.how_to_apply: Decision: CSS (scroll-driven, transitions, view transitions) first; Elementor Interactions second (0 extra bytes beyond Motion); if JS is unavoidable on a page that already has an interaction, write `const {animate, inView, scroll} = window.Motion` in a deferred child-theme script that depends on handle `motion-js`; only otherwise bundle a tree-shaken anime.js/Motion ESM module (<= 20 KB gzip) self-hosted under the child theme with a pinned version.
findings.how_to_verify: Network panel shows at most one animation library per page; `typeof window.Motion` is 'object' only on pages with `#elementor-interactions-data`; total first-party JS executed before interaction <= plugin budget.
tools: wp_enqueue_script with deps ['motion-js'] in sandbox plugin

findings.claim: Interactions run at DOMContentLoaded from footer scripts and only replace the element's inline style at that moment, so the lint must (a) ban the `load` trigger entirely, (b) require `breakpoints.excluded: ['mobile']` by default, and (c) exclude four handles from Delay-JS.
findings.detail: Core `interactions.js` and Pro `interactions-pro.js` both end with `if ('loading' === document.readyState) document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init); else init();` and call `animateFunc(element, keyframes, options)` immediately for `load` (keyframes `opacity:[0,1]`, `y:[100,0]`, `scale:[0,1]` from `getKeyframes`), so a `load` interaction always shows the element, hides it, then animates — the plugin's filmstrip/CLS-free rule cannot be satisfied with `load`. `scrollIn` uses `inView(element, cb, {amount: 0, root: null})` (first pixel). Pro `scrollIn` resets to `initialKeyframes` on leave only when replay is on. Breakpoint exclusion is evaluated client-side by `interactions-shared-utils.js` using the kit breakpoints from `ElementorInteractionsConfig`. Handles: `motion-js`, `elementor-interactions-shared-utils`, `elementor-interactions` (free) or `elementor-interactions-pro` (Pro, swapped at wp_footer priority 2).
findings.breaks_when: A delay-JS plugin defers these handles (reveal never fires until first touch; elements stay in their normal state, so no visual harm, but the designer's motion is gone); a `load` interaction on any element (flash); `replay` + `scrollIn` on long lists (re-animates on every scroll pass, INP).
findings.how_to_apply: Lint rules for `elementor-audit`/`elementor-build`: reject `trigger: load`; allow `scrollIn` only on nodes whose first ancestor section is not the first top-level container; default `breakpoints.excluded` to `['mobile']` unless the designer asks for mobile motion; write `motion-js, elementor-interactions, elementor-interactions-pro, elementor-interactions-shared-utils` into the Delay-JS exclusion list for LiteSpeed/FlyingPress/Perfmatters/WP Rocket.
findings.how_to_verify: WebPageTest/Chrome filmstrip at 390 px shows no element disappearing after first paint; `#elementor-interactions-data` JSON contains no `"trigger":{..."value":"load"}`; with cache plugin on, the four scripts load without `type="rocketlazyloadscript"`/`data-no-optimize` deferral markers.

findings.claim: Variable-naming lint: labels must be ASCII kebab-case, non-empty, <= 50 chars, unique; values non-empty, <= 512 chars, never bare `0`; a label rename is a breaking change for every `var(--old)` reference in child-theme/custom CSS.
findings.detail: `Rest_Api::MAX_LABEL_LENGTH = 50`, `MAX_VALUE_LENGTH = 512`; validators check only emptiness and length; `build_css_variable_entry()` returns null when `empty($value)` (PHP treats '0' as empty) and uses `sanitize_text_field($label)` as the custom-property name with no transformation; soft-deleted variables fall back to their `e-gv-*` id as the name. Global class labels share the 50-char cap and get `DUP_` on collisions.
findings.breaks_when: Greek or spaced labels (`Κύριο Χρώμα`, `Primary Color`) produce `--Κύριο Χρώμα:` / `--Primary Color:`; Greek is technically valid in CSS custom properties but the space is not, and both are hostile to grep/safelists; a spacing variable set to `0` silently disappears; renaming `color-brand-primary` after launch breaks child-theme CSS.
findings.how_to_apply: Builder step: generate labels from the design tokens as `color-*`, `font-*`, `space-*`, `radius-*` (ASCII, kebab-case, <= 50 chars); use `0px` not `0`; keep a `tokens.json` in the child theme as the single source and never rename after the first production deploy (create a new variable and migrate). Validate with `GET /wp-json/elementor/v1/variables/list` before writing CSS that references them.
findings.how_to_verify: post-{kit}.css `:root{}` block has one `--name:value;` per token, all names match `^--[a-z0-9-]+$`; `grep -o 'var(--[^)]*)' child-theme/*.css | sort -u` is a subset of the names in post-{kit}.css.

findings.claim: Elementor's built-in MCP route has three prerequisites the pipeline must check before relying on it: the WordPress MCP Adapter plugin (`WP\MCP\Core\McpAdapter`), the Abilities API (`wp_register_ability`, core since WP 6.9), and the Elementor-side exposure toggle (`McpSettingsController::is_enabled()`), plus an admin (`manage_options`) user.
findings.detail: `modules/mcp/module.php`: `is_active()` returns `class_exists(McpAdapter::class) && function_exists('wp_register_ability') && ...`; registration bails when `! function_exists('wp_register_ability_category')`; ability visibility `$mcp['public'] = McpSettingsController::is_enabled()` (abstract-ability.php:65); `current_user_can('manage_options')` check at module.php:78. Elementor has no `vendor/` directory in the repo, so the adapter is not bundled.
findings.breaks_when: The pipeline assumes `elementor/manage-classes` exists on a site without the MCP Adapter plugin; the exposure toggle is left on in production (any connected MCP client with an admin token gets write abilities); Novamira's MCP adapter (`mcp-adapter-discover-abilities`) and Elementor's abilities share the same WP Abilities registry, so ability names can appear in Novamira's listing once both are active — verify with discover-abilities rather than assuming.
findings.how_to_apply: Step 0 of the build: `novamira/mcp-adapter-discover-abilities` and look for `elementor/manage-classes`; if absent, check `wp plugin list` (via `novamira/run-wp-cli`, read-only) for the MCP Adapter plugin and ask the owner before installing/enabling; turn the Elementor MCP exposure off after the build. Fall back to `PUT elementor/v1/global-classes` and `elementor/v1/variables/batch` REST calls, which need no adapter.
findings.how_to_verify: `discover-abilities` output lists `elementor/manage-classes`; `elementor/get-page-structure` dry-run returns the page tree; after the build, the same call fails with a permission/not-public error when exposure is off.

findings.claim: A `<script type="module">` facade loader printed by Pro Custom Code or enqueued via `wp_enqueue_script_module` must sit in the footer or be deferred, or dynamic `import()` of mapped specifiers fails because the import map is printed later.
findings.detail: WordPress `wp_enqueue_script` reference (opened): `module_dependencies` — 'When provided, the script must either be printed in the footer (with in_footer set to true) or use a deferred loading strategy (defer), so that the script modules import map is printed before the script is evaluated. Otherwise dynamic imports may fail to resolve.' Custom Code 'Body - End' prints at `wp_footer` priority 21, after `wp_print_footer_scripts`, which is where the import map lands, so the recommended Body-End placement is correct; Head/Body-Start placements of a module loader are not.
findings.breaks_when: Hero-3d/desktop-only loader placed in `<head>` or `<body> - Start` with bare specifiers; absolute-URL `import('/wp-content/themes/CHILD/js/x.js')` is unaffected by the import map but still runs before the target DOM exists unless it waits for DOMContentLoaded.
findings.how_to_apply: Keep facade loaders in Custom Code 'Body - End' (priority 5-10) or `wp_enqueue_script_module(..., ['in_footer'=>true])` from the sandbox plugin; use absolute URLs, not bare specifiers, inside `import()`.
findings.how_to_verify: No console error 'Failed to resolve module specifier'; the loader `<script type=module>` appears after `<script type="importmap">` in view-source.

title: Motion and design within the 95-100 budget: measured costs and safe patterns
summary: Motion is affordable on mobile only when it costs zero bytes and zero main-thread time before LCP. Measured on 2026-10-21 (Lighthouse 12.8.2 CLI, mobile preset, 4x CPU, simulated throttling, benchmarkIndex 2,200-3,000, median of 3, 30-element reveal page): a CSS transition + IntersectionObserver reveal costs nothing (LCP 751 ms, TBT 0, identical to the bare page); GSAP core+ScrollTrigger (45 KB gz, 266 ms script CPU) pushes simulated LCP from 751 to 1,563 ms when loaded synchronously and still to 1,709 ms with `defer`, because Lighthouse's Lantern model charges every script fetched before LCP to the LCP estimate; loading the same GSAP after `load`+1.5 s or on first user intent gives LCP 751 ms and score 100 with the full animation intact. Lottie (lottie.min.js 76 KB gz + 65 KB JSON autoplaying in the hero) alone drops the page to 95: LCP 2.3 s, TBT 85 ms, 1.4 s of script CPU. The agency's field data agrees and is harsher (entrance `fadeIn` on an `h1` = 7,831 ms Render Delay; gsap+ScrollTrigger+SplitText = 1.78 s bootup; three.js hero = 142 s TBT). Library sizes measured from the current npm releases (gzip -9): GSAP 3.15.0 core 28.3 KB + ScrollTrigger 18.0 KB (all plugins free since 3.13); anime.js 4.5.0 full 40.8 KB, tree-shaken animate+onScroll 18.9 KB; Motion 14.5.0 hybrid 56.9 KB, tree-shaken animate+inView 24.6 KB, `motion/mini` 3.4 KB; Elementor 4.3.5 Interactions = Motion 11.13.5 (42.2 KB) + 7.4 KB handlers, enqueued only on pages with an interaction; lottie-web 76.1 KB (light 46.4, Elementor Pro's copy 63.2); dotLottie 33 KB JS + 496 KB gz WASM; Lenis 5.4 KB. The motion budget that keeps 95-100: 0 animated elements above the fold and none on the LCP element; 0 motion JS requested before LCP; at most 50 KB gz of motion JS and 300 ms of script CPU per page even after LCP; at most 20 animated elements; transform/opacity (plus filter/clip-path) only; reveals that never change layout (CLS from transform is 0 by definition); no autoplay Lottie, canvas, video or smooth-scroll library on phones; every autoplaying loop longer than 5 s has a pause control (WCAG 2.2.2); prefers-reduced-motion honoured everywhere but never relied on to hide cost (Lighthouse reports it false). Scroll-driven CSS animations (`animation-timeline: view()`; Chrome 115, Safari 26, Firefox 159) and Elementor Interactions "Scroll into view" below the fold are the two zero- or near-zero-cost ways to get rich scroll motion; Pro Motion Effects, Lenis/ScrollSmoother, Lottie and cursor effects are desktop-only, loaded by a width- and pointer-gated dynamic import after LCP. Acceptance is proven by a 3-run serial Lighthouse median with benchmarkIndex recorded, an LCP-element assertion (no `elementor-invisible`, Render Delay under 300 ms), a `[data-interactions]`/`.elementor-invisible` count, a Puppeteer scroll+tap probe reading web-vitals attribution INP and long-animation-frames, a layout-shift PerformanceObserver, and a reduced-motion emulation pass.

findings.claim: Any animation library requested before LCP costs 600-950 ms of simulated mobile LCP even with `defer`; loading it after LCP (on `load`+1.5 s or first user intent) restores the bare-page LCP while keeping the animation.
findings.detail: Measured 2026-10-21, Lighthouse 12.8.2 CLI mobile preset (412x823, 4x CPU, simulated 150 ms RTT / 1.6 Mbps), 30 reveal cards, median of 3, benchmarkIndex 2,200-3,000. Bare page: score 100, LCP 751 ms, TBT 0, main thread 170 ms. gsap.min.js + ScrollTrigger.min.js as sync `<script>` at body end: score 99, LCP 1,563 ms (render-blocking-resources lists gsap 901 ms, ScrollTrigger 751 ms), bootup 204 ms, library CPU 266 ms, main thread 495 ms. Same scripts with `defer`: FCP back to 641 ms but LCP 1,709 ms (Render Delay 1,157 ms) because Lantern's pessimistic LCP graph includes every network request that completes before the observed LCP. Same scripts injected by a loader after `load`+1.5 s or on the first scroll/pointerdown/keydown/touchstart: score 100, LCP 751 ms, TBT 26 ms, 126 KB. anime.js 4.5.0 as `<script type=module>`: LCP 1,501 ms, library CPU 230 ms. Motion 11.13.5 (Elementor's copy) sync: LCP 1,501 ms; defer: 1,352 ms. Field confirmation from the agency: platonos pays 1.78 s bootup for gsap+ScrollTrigger+SplitText (levers.md 7.6). Loader (Custom Code, location body end, excluded from Delay-JS so it is not delayed twice): `<script id="motion-loader" data-no-optimize="1" nowprocket>(function(){var d=false;function load(){if(d)return;d=true;if(matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches)return;var s=document.createElement('script');s.src='/wp-content/themes/CHILD/js/motion.bundle.js';s.defer=true;document.body.appendChild(s);} ['scroll','pointerdown','keydown','touchstart'].forEach(function(e){addEventListener(e,load,{once:true,passive:true})}); addEventListener('load',function(){setTimeout(load,1500)});})();</script>`. The bundle must set initial states itself (`gsap.set`/`gsap.from`) so elements are visible until it runs; never pre-hide them in CSS.
findings.breaks_when: The library is referenced by a normal `<script src>` (sync, defer or module) anywhere in the document; the loader is itself caught by Delay-JS (LiteSpeed/WP Rocket/Perfmatters) so initial states are applied only after interaction; CSS pre-hides `.reveal{opacity:0}` and the loader never fires (reduced motion, JS error) leaving blank sections; the first scroll fires before the bundle is parsed on a slow phone, so the first reveal plays late (acceptable) or the LCP element is one of the targets (never).
findings.how_to_apply: Keep every GSAP/anime/Motion/Lenis/Lottie file out of the static HTML; emit the loader above via Elementor Pro Custom Code (location: body end, priority 10) or `wp_add_inline_script` in the child theme; serve the bundle from the theme (one file, long cache); exclude the loader id/token from Delay-JS lists; only target elements that start in the second viewport or lower; add `prefers-reduced-motion` and, for heavy effects, `matchMedia('(min-width:1025px) and (pointer:fine)')` gates inside `load()`.
findings.how_to_verify: Run `lighthouse URL --only-categories=performance --output=json` 3 times serially (mobile default) and compare `audits.largest-contentful-paint.numericValue` and `audits.render-blocking-resources.details.items` before/after: no animation library URL may appear in `network-requests` with `startTime` before `largest-contentful-paint`; LCP phases show Render Delay under 300 ms; `bootup-time` lists the bundle only after load; desktop screenshot still shows the animation. Local reproduction files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/site/gsap-st.html, gsap-st-defer.html, gsap-st-afterlcp.html; results in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/lh2/*.json (summarise with /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/bin/summ.py).

findings.claim: Elementor entrance animations hide the element with `elementor-invisible` (visibility:hidden) until global.js runs, so one above-the-fold entrance animation can cost seconds of LCP Render Delay; a CSS transition + IntersectionObserver reveal below the fold costs 0 ms and 0 score.
findings.detail: Agency data (levers.md 7.6 / rule 13): voreniahorizon `h1` with `_animation: fadeIn` has Render Delay 7,831 ms of an 8.95 s LCP; cretaforums 3,620 ms; pallada keeps 90 animations but an un-animated LCP paragraph and scores 86. Bytes are trivial (animations.min.css 18.5 KB raw / 2.6 KB gz; per-animation stylesheet e.g. fadeIn.min.css 77 B) - the cost is the paint gate. Measured alternative: `.reveal{opacity:0;transform:translateY(24px);transition:opacity .6s,transform .6s}.reveal.in{opacity:1;transform:none}` plus a 300-byte IntersectionObserver (`rootMargin:'0px 0px -15% 0px'`, `unobserve` after first hit) scored 100 with LCP 751 ms, TBT 0, main thread 164 ms - indistinguishable from the bare page across 3 runs. Rule for Elementor controls: every element in the first top-level container and in the header has Advanced > Motion Effects > Entrance Animation = None; Loop Grid `_animation` None; Pro v4 Interactions 'Page load' trigger likewise never above the fold. Budget: more than 20 `elementor-invisible`/`[data-interactions]`/motion-fx elements per page is a finding (rule 13).
findings.breaks_when: The LCP element or anything in the first viewport carries `elementor-invisible` or a Page-load Interaction; Delay-JS defers global.js so the hero stays hidden until interaction (LCP = never on Lighthouse); the hero image is lazy and animated at the same time (both gates stack); the reveal CSS is placed in a stylesheet that loads before JS is guaranteed (if the IO script fails, `.reveal` stays at opacity 0 - add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){.reveal{opacity:1;transform:none}}` and a `<noscript>` or a `.js` class gate).
findings.how_to_apply: Audit: `document.querySelectorAll('.elementor-invisible, [data-interactions]').length` at load must be 0 inside the first viewport (`getBoundingClientRect().top < innerHeight`). Build: for below-fold reveals prefer the CSS class + IO snippet (one Global Class `.reveal` in V4, one Custom Code script) over per-widget Entrance Animations; if designers insist on Elementor's own control, use it only on elements whose container starts below 823 px on a 412 px viewport and keep the count under 20.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse JSON: `audits['largest-contentful-paint-element'].details.items[0]` snippet has no `elementor-invisible` class and no `data-interactions`; items[1] phases Render Delay under 300 ms and under 40% of LCP; filmstrip frame 1 shows the h1. Puppeteer: count `.elementor-invisible` with `top < innerHeight` right after `load` = 0. Reproduction: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/site/css-io.html vs base.html.

findings.claim: Motion budget table: measured bytes and main-thread cost per library (2026-10-21 releases) and the per-page limits that keep 95-100.
findings.detail: Sizes measured from jsdelivr with gzip -9 (raw / gzip): GSAP 3.15.0 core 72.9 / 28.3 KB; ScrollTrigger 44.6 / 18.0; SplitText 7.7 / 3.7; ScrollSmoother 13.4 / 5.5; MorphSVG 21.2 / 9.6; esbuild bundle of core+ScrollTrigger 115.2 / 45.1. anime.js 4.5.0 (MIT) full ESM 118.7 / 40.8; tree-shaken {animate,onScroll,stagger} 51.2 / 18.9. Motion 14.5.0 (MIT) UMD 172.0 / 56.9; tree-shaken {animate,inView} 65.7 / 24.6; `motion/mini` animate 8.4 / 3.4 (docs: mini 3.2 kb, hybrid 22 kb). Elementor 4.3.5 Interactions: lib/motion/motion.min.js (Motion 11.13.5) 128.3 / 42.2 + interactions.min.js 13.3 / 4.4 + interactions-shared-utils.min.js 8.5 / 3.0 = 150 KB raw / 49.5 KB gz. lottie-web 5.13.0 full 305.7 / 76.1; lottie_light 168.4 / 46.4; Elementor Pro 4.3.2 lib/lottie/lottie.min.js 252.6 / 63.2. @lottiefiles/dotlottie-web 0.81.0 JS 165.4 / 32.9 plus dotlottie-player.wasm 1,238 / 496 KB. Lenis 1.3.27 18.8 / 5.4. web-vitals 6.2.3 iife 9.0 / 3.3 (attribution 15.7 / 5.5). For scale: Elementor Swiper v8 143.7 / 39.6; Pro elements-handlers.min.js (incl. motion-fx) 291.6 / 73.0. Lab CPU at 4x on a fast host (library script evaluation per Lighthouse bootup-time, median of 3; expect 2-4x more on a Moto G class phone, benchmarkIndex 125-800): CSS+IO 0 ms; Lenis 160 ms; anime.js 230 ms; GSAP+ScrollTrigger 266 ms; Motion 11 under the 50 ms per-URL reporting threshold (main thread +40 ms); lottie-web + 65 KB JSON autoplaying 1,395 ms (TBT 85 ms, LCP 2.3 s, score 95). Budget per page (mobile): 0 motion bytes and 0 animated elements before/above LCP; motion JS loaded after LCP at most 50 KB gz total (one library, no duplicates: GSAP core+ScrollTrigger OR anime subset OR Motion subset OR Elementor Interactions, never two); library script CPU at most 300 ms in the lab trace and TBT stays under 300 ms (rule 14); at most 20 animated elements; durations 300-700 ms, stagger at most 80 ms per item and at most 8 staggered children; at most one autoplaying loop (marquee or Lottie) and it is paused off-screen; Lottie only below the fold, lazy, at most 1 per page, JSON at most 100 KB, never dotLottie WASM on phones; no smooth-scroll library, canvas, three.js or cursor follower on phones at all (desktop-only dynamic import).
findings.breaks_when: Two libraries ship on one page (e.g. Pro Interactions' Motion 11 plus a theme GSAP, or an add-on pack's own anime/velocity), doubling bytes and bootup; a page bundles the whole GSAP plugin set or full anime.js when 2 functions are used; a Lottie JSON exported with embedded raster images (hundreds of KB) is treated as 'a small vector'; the CPU numbers are read as absolute - they are from a benchmarkIndex ~2,500 host and PSI servers are slower.
findings.how_to_apply: Build step in the child theme: `esbuild src/motion.js --bundle --minify --format=iife --outfile=js/motion.bundle.js` importing only `gsap` + `gsap/ScrollTrigger` (or `{animate,onScroll} from 'animejs'`), served after LCP via the loader in finding 1. Audit step: sum gzip bytes of every request matching `gsap|anime|motion|lottie|lenis|three|swiper|particles|aos|wow` in the Lighthouse network log, flag more than one family, flag any of them before LCP, and read their `bootup-time` totals.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse JSON `audits['network-requests'].details.items` (transferSize, startTime vs LCP) and `audits['bootup-time'].details.items` per URL; compare against this table. Re-measure sizes with `curl -sL <cdn url> | gzip -9 | wc -c` when versions change. Raw files kept in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/libs/.

findings.claim: GSAP 3.13+ is 100% free for commercial use including every former Club plugin (ScrollTrigger, ScrollSmoother, SplitText, MorphSVG, DrawSVG, Flip, Draggable, Inertia, MotionPath, Observer); install from public npm, current release 3.15.0 under GreenSock's Standard 'no charge' license (not MIT).
findings.detail: gsap.com/pricing (2026): 'GSAP is now 100% free for all users, thanks to Webflow's support'; blog 3.13 (April 2025): 'the entire GSAP toolset is FREE, even for commercial use', bonus plugins added to the main GitHub repo and npm package, private registry npm.greensock.com retired (move off by June 1, 2025; 'Ensure that you are using GSAP version 3.13 or later'). package.json 3.15.0: `license: Standard 'no charge' license: https://gsap.com/standard-license` - the license page itself was offline on 2026-10-21 (forums down for a PHP vulnerability), so the exact clause text could not be re-read; treat it as a permissive but non-MIT license and keep the notice. SplitText 3.13 rewrite is 50% smaller (7.7 KB raw / 3.7 KB gz), adds `aria-label`/`aria-hidden` for screen readers, `autoSplit` re-splitting on font load/resize, `mask` option, and can run standalone without the GSAP core. Performance notes from the docs: ScrollTrigger 'scroll events are debounced, updates are synchronized with GSAP and screen refreshes'; start/end are static and recomputed only on `refresh()` (resize) - never animate the trigger element's layout; use `once: true` so finished triggers are killed; `ScrollTrigger.normalizeScroll(true)` 'forces scrolling to be done on the JavaScript thread' - do not enable on mobile; `gsap.matchMedia()` conditions `{isDesktop:'(min-width:1025px) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)', reduceMotion:'(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'}` revert all tweens and triggers when the query stops matching.
findings.breaks_when: A project still points `.npmrc` at npm.greensock.com or uses a pre-3.13 Club build (private, no longer updated); a page loads ScrollSmoother/`normalizeScroll` on phones (JS-thread scrolling, address-bar jitter) or animates `width/height/top/left` through ScrollTrigger (layout each frame, start/end drift); SplitText is applied to the LCP heading (splits before paint when loaded early, and reflows on font swap).
findings.how_to_apply: `npm i gsap@^3.15` in the child theme, `import {gsap} from 'gsap'; import {ScrollTrigger} from 'gsap/ScrollTrigger'; gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger);` wrap setup in `const mm = gsap.matchMedia(); mm.add({isDesktop:'(min-width:1025px) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)', isMobile:'(max-width:1024px) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)', reduceMotion:'(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'}, ctx => { const {isDesktop, reduceMotion} = ctx.conditions; if (reduceMotion) return; ... scrollTrigger:{trigger: el, start:'top 85%', once:true} })`; keep the license note in the bundle header; load via the after-LCP loader (finding 1).
findings.how_to_verify: `npm view gsap version license` prints 3.15.x and the Standard license string; no request to `npm.greensock.com` or `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap-trial`; in DevTools Performance, scroll recording shows ScrollTrigger `onUpdate` work only while scrolling and no `Layout` entries inside tween frames; `ScrollTrigger.getAll().length` drops to 0 for `once:true` triggers after a full scroll.

findings.claim: Elementor 4.3 Interactions (e_interactions, Editor V4) cost 150 KB raw / 49.5 KB gz of JS only on pages that contain an interaction, apply to all devices with no per-breakpoint control, and are rendered without `elementor-invisible` - so the safe pattern is 'Scroll into view' Fade/Slide/Scale on below-fold atomic elements only, never 'Page load' above the fold.
findings.detail: Help article 'Interactions' (updated 2026-06-19): triggers Page load, Scroll into view, While scrolling (start/end points), On hover, On click; effects Fade, Slide, Scale with Type In/Out, Direction arrows, Duration and Delay in ms; 'Interactions apply to all devices, you cannot customize interactions for different screen sizes.' Source (modules/interactions/module.php, main): registers `motion-js` (`lib/motion/motion.min.js`, version 11.13.5), `interactions-shared-utils` and `interactions` handles; levers.md 7.6 verified they are enqueued only when the document has interactions. The 4.3.5 frontend runtime interactions.min.js reads `[data-interactions]` attributes; `isSupportedInteraction()` accepts only triggers `load`, `scrollIn`, `scrollOut` and rejects `effect === 'custom'` - hover/click/while-scrolling triggers from the help article are not executed by this frontend file (medium confidence: they may ship in a later build or another handler). Keyframes are Motion `animate()` on `opacity`/`scale`/`x`/`y` only (compositor-safe); scrollIn/scrollOut use Motion `inView` (IntersectionObserver, `amount: .85` for scrollOut). The element is rendered visible in HTML and the script sets `opacity:0` then animates in, so a Page-load interaction on an above-fold element produces a visible flash (content paints, disappears, fades back) rather than an LCP gate; no `prefers-reduced-motion` check exists in interactions.min.js or shared-utils (Motion 11's own reduced-motion flag is for its React layer). The 'Scroll into view' path costs nothing until the element nears the viewport. Count budget: `[data-interactions]` elements at most 20 per page (rule 13 analogue).
findings.breaks_when: Page-load interactions are placed on hero/header elements (flash, and in Lighthouse's filmstrip the hero blinks; when Delay-JS defers motion.min.js the blink happens on first interaction instead); the same page also loads a theme GSAP/anime bundle (two engines, ~90 KB gz); interactions are used as the only way to hide duplicate mobile/desktop sections (they are display-visible to Lighthouse and to screen readers); reduced-motion users still get full motion because the runtime does not check the media query.
findings.how_to_apply: Build (Novamira `elementor-add-interaction` or editor): trigger = Scroll into view, effect Fade/Slide (Slide distance is the preset `slideDistance`), duration 400-600 ms, delay 0-150 ms, only on atomic elements whose container begins below the first viewport on mobile; never on the first container, header, or any element that can be LCP. Add a site-wide CSS guard in the child theme or a Global Class: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){[data-interactions]{opacity:1 !important;transform:none !important;transition:none !important}}`. Do not combine with legacy Entrance Animations on the same page.
findings.how_to_verify: HTML: `document.querySelectorAll('[data-interactions]')` count at most 20 and none with `getBoundingClientRect().top < 823` at 412 px width; network log shows `lib/motion/motion.min.js` only on pages that have `[data-interactions]`; Lighthouse filmstrip has no frame where hero content disappears; emulate `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and confirm elements are static.

findings.claim: Animate only transform, opacity (and, where needed, filter or clip-path); never width/height/top/left/margin/padding/box-shadow/border-radius/background-position - composited transform animations are excluded from CLS by definition, layout-property reveals are counted and also thrash layout during INP.
findings.detail: web.dev animations-guide: 'Avoid any property that triggers layout or paint unless it's absolutely necessary'; use `transform` for move/rotate/scale and `opacity` for show/hide; `will-change: transform` only on elements that will animate, applied sparingly, because every layer costs GPU memory ('layer explosions' on low-memory phones). web.dev optimize-cls: 'Composited animations using translate can't impact other elements, and so don't count toward CLS'; shifts within 500 ms of a user input are excluded; reserve space for content loaded later ('reserve the expected space within that 500 ms timeframe'). motion.dev performance: layout re-renders 'can easily take upwards of 100ms'; `transform` and `opacity` 'operate directly on a layer' in every browser; Chrome and Firefox composite `filter` (and SVG), Chrome is adding `background-color` and `clip-path`; `box-shadow` and `border-radius` skip layout but need an 'expensive paint' - replace `boxShadow` with `filter: drop-shadow(...)` and `borderRadius` with `clip-path: inset(0 round 50px)`; animating a CSS variable is never hardware accelerated even when the variable feeds `transform`; percentage transforms were not accelerated in older Chrome - prefer px/vw. Typical Elementor CLS offenders: accordion/tab reveals that animate `height`, hover cards that change `margin`/`padding`, headings that animate `letter-spacing`/`font-size`/`font-variation-settings` (layout), sticky headers that change height on scroll, counters that widen text. Pattern for a size-changing reveal without CLS: fix the container's final box (`min-height`, `aspect-ratio`, or `grid-template-rows: 0fr -> 1fr` with `overflow:hidden`) and animate the child with `transform: scaleY()`/`opacity`, or use `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` only where supported; otherwise accept the shift inside the 500 ms input window (user-initiated accordions are fine).
findings.breaks_when: A reveal changes an element's box (`display:none -> block`, `height:0 -> auto`, `max-height` tween, inserting a banner) outside a 500 ms user-input window; a 'parallax' moves backgrounds with `background-position` (paint on every frame); hover effects animate `box-shadow` blur on large cards (blur is the most expensive paint); `will-change` is applied globally (`*{will-change:transform}`) or to hundreds of items.
findings.how_to_apply: Linting rule for Custom CSS / Global Classes / Interactions: `transition` and `@keyframes` may only reference `transform`, `opacity`, `filter`, `clip-path`, `translate`, `scale`, `rotate` (the individual transform properties); flag `height`, `width`, `top`, `left`, `margin*`, `padding*`, `box-shadow`, `border-radius`, `background-position`, `font-*`, `letter-spacing`. Reserve space: every image, embed, slider and dynamic block has width/height or `aspect-ratio`; cookie bar `position:fixed` (rule 8). `will-change: transform` only on the handful of elements that animate, set by class, removed when done.
findings.how_to_verify: CLS observer in the test harness: `new PerformanceObserver(l=>{for(const e of l.getEntries()) if(!e.hadRecentInput) shifts.push({v:e.value, src:e.sources?.map(s=>s.node?.outerHTML.slice(0,80))})}).observe({type:'layout-shift',buffered:true})` after load + scroll-through must total at most 0.05; Chrome DevTools Rendering > Paint flashing and Layout Shift Regions while hovering/scrolling show no flashing outside the animated element; Performance panel frames during an animation contain no `Layout` or `Recalculate Style` of more than 2-3 ms.

findings.claim: CSS scroll-driven animations (`animation-timeline: view()` / `scroll()`) deliver parallax, progress bars and scroll-linked reveals with zero JavaScript and off-main-thread compositing; they are now supported in Chrome 115+, Safari 26+ and Firefox 159+, so use them behind `@supports` instead of ScrollTrigger scrub or Pro Scrolling Effects on mobile.
findings.detail: Chrome docs: 'The classic way ... is to respond to scroll events on the main thread, which leads to ... jank'; scroll-driven animations 'integrate with the existing Web Animations API and CSS Animations API ... including the ability to have scroll-driven animations run off the main thread'. Syntax: `animation: par linear both; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 25% cover 50%;` (`animation-timeline` is not part of the `animation` shorthand and must be declared after it); `view()` tracks the element within its nearest scroller, `scroll(root block)` tracks the page; named timelines via `view-timeline-name: --x` / `animation-timeline: --x`. Browser compat (MDN BCD, 2026-10): Chrome 115, Safari 26, Firefox 159 (MDN page text still says 'Limited availability'; iOS before 26 and Samsung Internet lag, so a `@supports (animation-timeline: view())` guard is mandatory and the no-support state must be the final, fully visible state). Measured: a parallax of 30 cards via SDA scored 100 with LCP 751 ms / main thread 171 ms, identical to the bare page; the classic scroll-listener version that sets `style.top` per card also scored 100 at load (cost is only while scrolling, which Lighthouse does not do - so Lighthouse cannot catch it; see finding on INP probes). Keep animated properties to transform/opacity so the timeline stays on the compositor; Motion's `scroll()` and anime.js `onScroll({sync:true})` fall back to JS where ScrollTimeline is missing (Motion docs: 'will use ScrollTimeline where possible').
findings.breaks_when: The `@supports` guard is omitted and older iOS shows elements stuck at the keyframe's `from` state (opacity 0 = invisible content); `animation-timeline` is written before the `animation` shorthand (shorthand resets it); the animated property is `top`/`height`/`background-position` (falls back to main thread); the first-viewport hero uses it with an `entry` range (the LCP element starts translated/transparent).
findings.how_to_apply: Child theme or V4 Global Class CSS: `@supports (animation-timeline: view()){ .parallax-img{animation:par linear both;animation-timeline:view();animation-range:entry 0% exit 100%} @keyframes par{from{transform:translateY(6%)}to{transform:translateY(-6%)}} .reveal{animation:rev linear both;animation-timeline:view();animation-range:entry 10% entry 60%} @keyframes rev{from{opacity:0;transform:translateY(24px)}} } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){.parallax-img,.reveal{animation:none}}`; apply the class to below-fold images/cards only; put the parallax image inside an `overflow:hidden` wrapper with `aspect-ratio` so movement never changes layout.
findings.how_to_verify: Chrome DevTools Performance recording while scrolling: no `Function Call`/`scroll` handler tasks, animation shows in the Animations track as composited; Puppeteer probe (long-animation-frame count 0 while scrolling at 4x CPU); visual check on an iOS 18 device or `@supports not` emulation shows final static state. Reproduction: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/site/parallax-sda.html vs parallax-scrollhandler.html.

findings.claim: Elementor Pro Motion Effects (Scrolling Effects: Vertical/Horizontal Scroll, Transparency, Blur, Rotate, Scale; Mouse Effects: Mouse Track, 3D Tilt) run as main-thread scroll/rAF handlers inside the 292 KB raw / 73 KB gz elements-handlers bundle; set 'Apply Effects On' to Desktop only, never use Blur, and prefer CSS scroll-driven animations for anything that must move on phones.
findings.detail: Help article 'Motion effects' (updated 2026-06-04): effects list above; 'Apply Effects On: Choose where you want to apply the effects on - Desktop, Tablet or Mobile'; 'Effects Relative To' viewport/entire page; 'Mouse effects will only affect desktop devices'; 'Elementor respects the reduced motion property preference ... motion effects is disabled for that user'; known Safari issue when Mouse Track is combined with entrance animations ('maximum call stack size exceeded', missing carousel arrows) - fix is to remove entrance animations from elements with motion effects. The Pro frontend bundle elements-handlers.min.js (4.3.2) contains the motion-fx handler using `addEventListener('scroll')`, `requestAnimationFrame` and `translate3d`/`.css('transform')` (compositor-safe transforms, but computed per scroll event on the JS thread); the Blur effect animates `filter: blur()` on images, the most expensive paint on large surfaces (web.dev: 'anything that involves a blur ... takes longer to paint'). Scale/Rotate on a hero image at the top of the page also makes the LCP image a transform-animated element (rule 13) and Scale beyond 1 overflows containers (CLS-free but can crop text). The agency's rule set treats more than 20 motion-fx/`elementor-invisible` elements as a finding.
findings.breaks_when: Scrolling Effects are applied on Mobile to many elements (each is a scroll-handler read/write per frame on a mid-tier phone); Blur or Transparency is applied to the hero background (paint cost on the LCP area and an animated LCP element); Mouse Track + Entrance Animation coexist (Safari error hides UI); the effect is used to fake a sticky/parallax header that then jumps when the address bar resizes (ScrollTrigger-style `ignoreMobileResize` has no Pro equivalent).
findings.how_to_apply: Audit: for each element with `data-settings` containing `motion_fx_motion_fx_scrolling`/`motion_fx_motion_fx_mouse`, check `motion_fx_devices` includes 'mobile' and flag; flag any `motion_fx_blur` and any effect inside the first top-level container. Build: Advanced > Motion Effects > Scrolling Effects with Apply Effects On = Desktop; Mouse Effects only for decorative, non-text layers; for mobile parallax use the SDA Global Class (finding 7) instead; keep Entrance Animation = None on any element with a motion effect.
findings.how_to_verify: DevTools Performance while scrolling on a 4x-throttled mobile emulation: no long frames attributed to `elements-handlers.min.js`; `document.querySelectorAll('[data-settings*="motion_fx"]').length` at most 20 and 0 inside the first viewport; Safari (or WebKit) console shows no 'maximum call stack' error on pages with Mouse Track.

findings.claim: Smooth-scroll libraries (Lenis, GSAP ScrollSmoother) are desktop-only by design: both leave touch scrolling native by default, both need a per-frame rAF loop, and Lenis lagged 43% behind real wheel input in the probe; on phones they add bytes and a ticking loop for no visible effect, so ship none on mobile and load them, if at all, from the desktop-only bundle after LCP.
findings.detail: Lenis 1.3.27 (MIT, 18.8 KB raw / 5.4 KB gz): listens to `wheel` and `touch` events, eases toward the target with `lerp` 0.1 (or `duration` 1.2 s); `smoothWheel: true`, `syncTouch: false` by default ('can be unstable on iOS below 16'); needs `lenis.raf(time)` 'every frame' or `autoRaf: true`; `respectReducedMotion` default true (lerp forced to 1); no CSS `scroll-snap` (use lenis/snap); smoothing stops over iframes (booking engines, maps); Safari capped at 60 fps (30 in low power). GSAP integration requires `gsap.ticker.add(t => lenis.raf(t*1000)); gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0); lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)`. ScrollSmoother (free since 3.13, 13.4 KB raw / 5.5 KB gz + ScrollTrigger): 'leverages NATIVE scrolling', moves `#smooth-content` with inline `matrix3d()` transforms to catch up (`smooth: 0.8 s` default), `smoothTouch` 'default is NO smoothing on touch devices', requires the wrapper/content structure with fixed elements outside, `normalizeScroll: true` moves scrolling to the JS thread (do not enable on phones), `ignoreMobileResize` to avoid jumps when the address bar resizes. Measured here: Lenis with `autoRaf` scored 100 at load (LCP 901 vs 751 ms, library CPU 160 ms, main thread +170 ms) but in the 7 s wheel probe at 4x CPU it reached 5,486 px where native scrolling reached 9,600 px - the smoothing is the product, and it is invisible on touch. The agency rule set lists 'Lenis/smooth-scroll before LCP' as a blocker (rule 13).
findings.breaks_when: Lenis or ScrollSmoother is initialised on phones (sticky headers, anchor links to booking forms, `position:fixed` modals and iframes misbehave; address-bar resize triggers `refresh()` jumps); `normalizeScroll`/`syncTouch` is enabled to 'fix' it (now the main thread owns scrolling and INP suffers); the library is loaded before LCP (blocker); `scroll-behavior: smooth` on `html` is combined with a JS smoother (double easing).
findings.how_to_apply: If a design needs it: `if (matchMedia('(min-width:1025px) and (pointer:fine) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)').matches) import('/wp-content/themes/CHILD/js/smooth.js')` from the after-LCP loader; for GSAP sites use ScrollSmoother (same ScrollTrigger instance, no second engine) with `smoothTouch` unset; for in-page anchor easing use CSS `html{scroll-behavior:smooth}` with `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){html{scroll-behavior:auto}}` (Baseline, zero JS).
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse network log has no `lenis`/`ScrollSmoother` URL; on a 412 px emulation `document.documentElement.classList` has no `lenis` class and `#smooth-content` has no inline `transform`; `scrollY` after a programmatic `scrollBy` equals the requested delta immediately; desktop run still shows the eased scroll; Puppeteer probe shows no long-animation-frame attributed to the smoother.

findings.claim: Lottie is the single most expensive 'small' animation: lottie-web is 76 KB gz and an autoplaying 65 KB JSON in the hero cost 1.4 s of script CPU, 85 ms TBT and 1.5 s of LCP (score 95) in the lab; allow at most one Lottie per page, below the fold, lazy-loaded with a viewport trigger, and never the dotLottie WASM player on phones.
findings.detail: Measured: lottie.min.js 5.13.0 (305.7 KB raw / 76.1 KB gz) + `loadAnimation({renderer:'svg', loop:true, autoplay:true, path})` with a 65 KB LottieFiles sample in the hero: score 95 (range 92-95), LCP 2,312 ms (2,252-2,853), TBT 85 ms (43-100), bootup 990 ms, library CPU 1,395 ms, main thread 1,965 ms, 373 KB transferred - the only variant in the test set that lost points. lottie_light (no expressions) is 168.4 / 46.4 KB; Elementor Pro's bundled lib/lottie/lottie.min.js is 252.6 / 63.2 KB. @lottiefiles/dotlottie-web 0.81.0 is 165 KB JS (32.9 gz) plus a 1,238 KB WASM renderer (496 KB gz) - 4x the lottie-web transfer, unsuitable for phones. Elementor Pro Lottie widget help: Source External URL or Media File (JSON; 'make sure the json file is from a trusted source'), Trigger Viewport (percentage slider), On Hover (Hover Area, Hover Out behaviour), Scroll (scrub by viewport), None; Loop with Reverse; Start/End point; 'In order to help the page load faster, toggle Lazy Load on. This means the animation will only load when it becomes visible'; there is no device gate (levers.md 7.1). SVG-renderer Lottie animates hundreds of DOM nodes per frame on the main thread (not compositor) and keeps looping off-screen unless the widget's viewport trigger pauses it. Alternatives that cost 0-5 KB: CSS keyframes on an inline SVG (transform/opacity/stroke-dashoffset), an animated AVIF/WebP, or a muted `<video preload="none" poster>` for complex illustrations.
findings.breaks_when: A Lottie sits in the first viewport (LCP candidate or paints over it; Lazy Load does not help above the fold); the JSON embeds raster images (`"p":"data:image/png;base64..."`), often 500 KB+; two Lottie widgets each load their own player (Pro loads it once, but an add-on pack may add a second runtime); `loop` + `autoplay` on a hidden tab keeps the CPU busy and drains battery; the dotLottie `<dotlottie-player>` web component is used 'because the file is smaller' while the WASM is 1.2 MB.
findings.how_to_apply: Allow: Pro Lottie widget below the fold, Lazy Load on, Trigger = Viewport (or Scroll for scrubbed storytelling), Loop off or capped, JSON at most 100 KB with no embedded bitmaps, one per page. For anything in the hero, replace with an SVG + CSS animation (`@keyframes` on `transform`, `stroke-dashoffset`), or a poster image; export from Figma/After Effects as SVG where possible. Audit rule: `lottie` URL in the network log before LCP is a blocker (rule 13); any `.json` over 100 KB fetched by the Lottie player is a finding.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse network log: `lottie.min.js` must start after `largest-contentful-paint` (or be absent); `bootup-time` for lottie under 300 ms; `getBoundingClientRect().top >= innerHeight` for every `.elementor-widget-lottie` at load; JSON size via `transferSize`; animation stops when `document.hidden` (check `lottie.getRegisteredAnimations()[0].isPaused`). Reproduction: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/site/lottie-hero.html.

findings.claim: Marquees and tickers must be CSS keyframe `translateX` on a duplicated track with a pause control - a 16 ms `setInterval` marquee writing `style.left` added 413 ms of main-thread work in the load trace while TBT stayed 0, so Lighthouse cannot see it but INP, battery and frame rate pay for it; WCAG 2.2.2 (Level A) requires pause/stop/hide for any auto-moving content longer than 5 s shown alongside other content.
findings.detail:
Measured: CSS marquee (`.track{animation:mq 30s linear infinite;will-change:transform}@keyframes mq{to{transform:translateX(-50%)}}` with the content repeated twice) - score 100, main thread 155 ms (same as bare page). `setInterval(fn,16)` moving `style.left` - score 100, TBT 0 (each task is under the 50 ms long-task threshold) but mainthread-work-breakdown 568 ms, i.e. +413 ms of continuous work during load that never shows up in TBT and continues forever. WCAG 2.2 Understanding 'Pause, Stop, Hide': for moving, blinking or scrolling information that '(1) starts automatically, (2) lasts more than five seconds, and (3) is presented in parallel with other content, there is a mechanism for the user to pause, stop, or hide it unless the movement, blinking, or scrolling is part of an activity where it is essential'; 'five seconds was chosen because it is long enough to get a user's attention, but not so long that a user cannot wait out the distraction'. Elementor has no core marquee widget; add-on 'marquee'/'logo ticker' widgets frequently use Swiper autoplay (143.7 KB raw / 39.6 KB gz Swiper 8 + per-slide clones) or JS loops. Pattern: `
A B C A B C
` with `.marquee:hover .track,.marquee.paused .track{animation-play-state:paused}` and `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){.track{animation:none}}`; width the track with `display:inline-flex` so `translateX(-50%)` loops seamlessly; the second copy is `aria-hidden`.
findings.breaks_when: The marquee is an add-on widget driven by `setInterval`/`requestAnimationFrame` writing `left`/`margin-left` (layout every tick, never stops off-screen); autoplay Swiper with `loop:true` is used as a ticker (clones DOM, runs timers, 40 KB); the marquee has no pause control and runs longer than 5 s (WCAG A failure); text inside the moving track is the only place information appears (screen readers read it twice or never).
findings.how_to_apply: Child theme CSS + an HTML widget or a V4 Global Class for `.marquee/.track`; the pause button toggles `.paused` with 3 lines of JS in Custom Code; `animation-play-state: paused` also when `document.hidden` (`visibilitychange`) and via `IntersectionObserver` when off-screen (`.track.offscreen{animation-play-state:paused}`). Dequeue add-on marquee scripts per page (rule 10). Keep 1 marquee per page, below the fold or in the footer; never in the first viewport (it is an animated element above the fold).
findings.how_to_verify: Performance panel on a 4x CPU mobile emulation: idle page shows no periodic JS tasks (only compositor frames); `getComputedStyle(track).animationPlayState === 'paused'` after clicking the control and under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` emulation `animationName === 'none'`; Lighthouse `mainthread-work-breakdown` within 30 ms of the same page without the marquee. Reproduction: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/site/marquee-css.html vs marquee-interval.html.

findings.claim: Cursor followers, magnetic buttons, 3D tilt and hover micro-interactions are free on phones only if they ship zero bytes there: gate the dynamic import on `(pointer: fine) and (hover: hover) and (min-width: 1025px)`, coalesce `pointermove` into one rAF write, and animate transform only.
findings.detail: MDN `pointer` media feature: `none` / `coarse` ('limited accuracy', touch) / `fine` (mouse, trackpad, stylus); `any-pointer`/`any-hover` test every input, `pointer`/`hover` the primary one - Lighthouse's mobile emulation (moto g power, touch) matches `pointer: coarse` and `hover: none`, so a correctly gated effect is never evaluated in the mobile run and costs 0. Elementor's own Mouse Effects are desktop-only by product definition ('Mouse effects will only affect desktop devices'). Implementation cost on desktop: a `pointermove` handler that only stores `x,y` and schedules a single `requestAnimationFrame` which writes `transform: translate3d(x,y,0)` on a `will-change: transform` element is a 2-3 ms frame; writing `left/top`, reading `getBoundingClientRect()` in the handler (layout thrash: web.dev optimize-inp 'update styles ... then read them in the same task'), or running GSAP `quickTo` on 50 elements per move is where frames exceed 16 ms. Hover effects on cards: `transition: transform .25s, opacity .25s` on the card, `filter: drop-shadow()` instead of `box-shadow` for the lift (motion.dev), and `@media (hover: hover)` so touch devices never get stuck in the hover state (tap-to-hover delay on links).
findings.breaks_when: The cursor script is enqueued site-wide (phones download and run it, and `touchmove` is wired to it); the gate uses `wp_is_mobile()`/UA sniffing server-side (breaks with page cache, levers.md 7.1 'Device-vary is the trap'); the custom cursor hides the native cursor (`cursor:none`) without a focus-visible/keyboard fallback; hover styles use `:hover` without `@media (hover: hover)` so iOS requires two taps on links inside cards.
findings.how_to_apply: In the after-LCP loader: `if (matchMedia('(pointer: fine) and (hover: hover) and (min-width: 1025px) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)').matches) import('/wp-content/themes/CHILD/js/cursor.js')`; cursor.js: `let x=0,y=0,q=false; addEventListener('pointermove',e=>{x=e.clientX;y=e.clientY;if(!q){q=true;requestAnimationFrame(()=>{dot.style.transform=`translate3d(${x}px,${y}px,0)`;q=false})}},{passive:true})`; hover CSS wrapped in `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`.
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse network log contains no cursor/tilt script; desktop DevTools Performance while moving the mouse for 5 s shows frames under 16 ms with no `Layout` entries; keyboard-only navigation still shows focus rings; `matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches` emulation (DevTools device mode) leaves `document.querySelector('.cursor')` null.

findings.claim: Image and video 'treatments' - blur, backdrop-filter, mix-blend-mode, large masks, animated filters, autoplay background video - are paint and media costs that belong in the exported asset or on desktop only: bake gradients/duotones/blur into the WebP/AVIF in Figma, keep live filters off the hero, and keep every video off phones (poster `` is the LCP).
findings.detail: web.dev animations-guide: 'anything that involves a blur (like a shadow, for example) takes longer to paint than drawing a red box'; paint cost scales with the painted area (motion.dev: 'the time a browser takes to repaint a layer is proportional to its size'), so a `filter: blur(20px)` or `backdrop-filter` over a full-width hero image re-paints the whole viewport whenever anything inside it changes (text reveal, sticky header). `mix-blend-mode` and `backdrop-filter` each create a stacking context and force the browser to composite the backdrop (MDN); on a fixed glass header that is a small, bounded area (acceptable); on a hero overlay it is the full first viewport (avoid). Static CSS `filter`/`mask-image` on an image are a one-time paint if nothing animates over them; they become per-frame costs when combined with Scrolling Effects, parallax or a sticky header crossing them. Baking the treatment into the asset costs 0 ms at runtime and typically fewer bytes (a pre-blurred/duotone WebP compresses better). Video: levers.md 7.1 measured background video on phones at LCP 16.4 / 9.0 s and Elementor 4.3.5 'Play On Mobile = No' never sets `src` on mobile; web.dev lazy-loading-video: non-autoplay videos use `preload="none"` + `poster`, `loading="lazy"` where supported; when a video is the LCP candidate 'use a poster image ... and preload it with a fetchpriority attribute value of high' (`<link rel="preload" as="image" fetchpriority="high">`); `<source media="(min-width:1025px)">` is evaluated at selection time so phones request 0 bytes. Fonts: 'web font effects' (animating `font-variation-settings`, `letter-spacing`, `font-size`) are layout animations - use SplitText/`clip-path`/transform reveals of static type instead, and never fade text in to hide FOUT (levers 7.6); the LCP heading's font is preloaded, `font-display: swap`, 2 families max (rule 11).
findings.breaks_when: A `backdrop-filter: blur()` glass panel covers the hero on mobile (paints every frame the text animates or the user scrolls under a sticky header); `mix-blend-mode: multiply` overlays are stacked on the LCP image (compositing of the LCP area, and the hero image gets a stacking context that can defeat `fetchpriority` ordering of a later ``); CSS `filter` is animated on a 1,000x1,500 px image with Scrolling Effects Blur; an autoplay `
findings.how_to_apply: Design hand-off rule: every blur/gradient/duotone/grain on a photo is exported as part of the image (Figma export at 1x/2x WebP, hero at most 100 KB for 390-430 px); `backdrop-filter` only on elements under 100 px tall (header/pill) and `@media (min-width:1025px)` for larger glass cards; `mix-blend-mode` only on small decorative layers; hero video via the HTML-widget pattern in levers.md 7.1 (poster `` + `
findings.how_to_verify: DevTools Rendering > Paint flashing while scrolling the first two viewports: no full-viewport green flashes; Layers panel shows the hero as one layer without `backdrop-filter`-induced extra layers; Lighthouse mobile network log has no `.mp4/.webm` and no `.json` before LCP and the LCP element is an `` or text (rule 3); Performance trace `Paint` events during a hero text animation under 4 ms.

findings.claim: `content-visibility: auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size: auto <height>` on below-fold sections cuts initial rendering work roughly 7x (232 ms to 30 ms in Chrome's demo) on long Elementor pages (room lists, forum threads, Loop Grids), with no effect on first-viewport content and no CLS if the placeholder size is right.
findings.detail: web.dev content-visibility: 'applying content-visibility: auto to chunked content areas gives a 7x rendering performance boost on initial load ... rendering times going from 232ms to 30ms'; the element's subtree skips layout and paint until near the viewport; it stays in the accessibility tree and find-in-page (unlike `visibility:hidden`); caveat: landmark elements with `display:none` inside skipped subtrees appear in the a11y tree until rendered, and any DOM API that forces layout on a skipped subtree (`getBoundingClientRect`, `offsetHeight`, `scrollIntoView` targets) cancels the saving - audit scripts (Elementor motion-fx, Swiper, Interactions `inView`) that measure those elements. `contain-intrinsic-size` provides the placeholder box; `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 500px` makes the browser 'remember' the last rendered size so scrollbar jumps and layout shifts disappear after first render (MDN: 'If no size is set, the element risks being zero-sized'). Browser support (MDN BCD): content-visibility Chrome 85, Safari 18, Firefox 125; contain-intrinsic-size Chrome 83, Safari 17, Firefox 107 - Baseline for the agency's audience. Elementor hook points: top-level containers are `.e-con.e-parent:nth-of-type(n)`; Elementor's own 'Lazy Load Background Images' already keys on `:nth-of-type(n+4)` (levers 7.1), so the same selector family works: `.e-con.e-parent:nth-of-type(n+4){content-visibility:auto;contain-intrinsic-size:auto 600px}`. Keep it off the first three top-level containers, the header/footer templates, and any container that holds the LCP element, popups' anchors or `position: sticky` children (containment changes their containing block).
findings.breaks_when: Applied to a container in the first viewport (the LCP element is skipped until layout, delaying LCP) or to a container with `position: sticky` children (layout containment breaks sticky); the intrinsic size is far from the real height (visible jump and CLS when the section renders, scrollbar thumb jumps); a script forces layout on skipped sections at load (no gain, console warning in Chromium); anchor links (`#rooms`) target skipped content on old Safari (17 and below) without `contain-intrinsic-size` (jumps to a zero-height box).
findings.how_to_apply: Child theme CSS: `@supports (content-visibility: auto){ .e-con.e-parent:nth-of-type(n+4):not(.no-cv){content-visibility:auto;contain-intrinsic-size:auto 600px} }`; add class `no-cv` to containers with sticky children or anchors used by the booking widget; measure real section heights on 412 px and set per-section `--cv-h` if they differ wildly (`contain-intrinsic-size: auto var(--cv-h, 600px)`). Only worth it on pages with more than ~1,500 DOM nodes or 8+ sections (rule 15 territory).
findings.how_to_verify: Chrome DevTools Performance: `Layout`/`Pre-Paint` time at load drops versus the control; `document.querySelectorAll('.e-con.e-parent').length` and `getComputedStyle(el).contentVisibility` on the 4th+ containers return `auto`; CLS observer during a slow scroll stays at 0; Lighthouse `dom-size` unchanged but `mainthread-work-breakdown` 'Style & Layout' lower; anchor navigation to a deep section lands correctly on iOS Safari 18.

findings.claim: Scheduling: start non-essential motion after LCP, on first intent, or at idle - using the LCP PerformanceObserver plus a `load`+1.5 s fallback, `requestIdleCallback` only with a `setTimeout` fallback (Safari still has no rIC), and `scheduler.yield()` (Chrome 129, Firefox 142) to chunk any init over 50 ms.
findings.detail: web.dev lcp: `new PerformanceObserver(list => {...}).observe({type:'largest-contentful-paint', buffered:true})` emits candidates; the final one settles only after the next user input or page hide, so a motion loader should fire on the first candidate that is text or the hero `` plus a timeout, not wait for 'final'. Measured in finding 1: the `load`+1.5 s / first-intent loader kept LCP at the bare-page value. web.dev optimize-inp: good INP is 200 ms at p75; interaction = input delay + processing + presentation delay; long tasks during startup (script evaluation) inflate input delay; yield after the UI-updating part of a handler (`requestAnimationFrame(() => setTimeout(nonCritical))`), avoid layout thrashing, keep the DOM small. Chrome blog: `await scheduler.yield()` breaks a long task and prioritises the continuation over other queued tasks (unlike `setTimeout`), shipped in Chrome 129 (BCD; Firefox 142; Safari none - feature-detect: `if ('scheduler' in window && 'yield' in scheduler) await scheduler.yield(); else await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r))`). `requestIdleCallback`: 'A timeout option is strongly recommended for required work'; caniuse 2026-10 shows Safari 27.2 still disabled by default, so always `const idle = window.requestIdleCallback || (cb => setTimeout(() => cb({timeRemaining:()=>50}), 200))`. Long Animation Frames API (Chrome 123+; not Firefox/Safari): `PerformanceObserver` type `long-animation-frame`, 50 ms threshold, `blockingDuration` = sum of task time over 50 ms, `scripts[]` with `invoker` (e.g. 'Window.requestAnimationFrame', 'IMG#id.onload') and `sourceURL` - the attribution the INP probe uses to name the offending library. Patterns: ScrollTrigger `once:true`, IO `unobserve`, Motion `inView` returning a stop function, anime.js `onScroll` with `sync:false` and `repeat:false`; set `engine.pauseOnDocumentHidden` (anime v4) / rely on rAF throttling in hidden tabs; never `setInterval` for animation.
findings.breaks_when: Init waits for the 'final' LCP entry (never arrives without input - animation never starts for a user who does not touch the page); the loader relies on `requestIdleCallback` without a fallback (Safari: never runs); a 400 ms init (splitting 200 headings with SplitText, creating 100 ScrollTriggers) runs in one task during the first tap (input delay, INP over 200 ms); `scheduler.yield` is called without feature detection (TypeError in Safari).
findings.how_to_apply: Loader order: (1) `PerformanceObserver` on `largest-contentful-paint` sets `lcpSeen=true` when the entry's element is the expected hero/h1; (2) `load` event + 1,500 ms timer; (3) `scroll`/`pointerdown`/`keydown`/`touchstart` once, passive; whichever first calls `load()`, which gates on reduced motion/width and `import()`s the bundle; inside the bundle, split setup into chunks of at most 20 elements separated by `await yieldToMain()` where `yieldToMain = () => ('scheduler' in window && 'yield' in scheduler) ? scheduler.yield() : new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))`.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse `long-tasks` audit lists no task over 50 ms attributed to the motion bundle; Puppeteer probe with `long-animation-frame` observer during load + first tap shows `blockingDuration` 0 for the bundle's `sourceURL`; `performance.getEntriesByType('largest-contentful-paint').at(-1).startTime` is unchanged versus the no-motion build; in Safari (WebKit) the bundle still loads (fallback path) - check the network panel.

findings.claim: Honour `prefers-reduced-motion` everywhere (CSS media query, `gsap.matchMedia` reduceMotion condition, Lenis `respectReducedMotion`, Elementor Motion Effects do it natively, Interactions do not) but never count on it to pass Lighthouse: the mobile emulation reports `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, so the full-motion path is what gets scored.
findings.detail: MDN: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` matches when the OS setting is on (iOS Settings > Accessibility > Motion; Android 9+ 'Remove animations'; macOS Accessibility > Motion/Display; Windows 11 Visual Effects > Animation Effects); 'Animations such as scaling or panning large objects can be vestibular motion triggers'. Lighthouse's mobile config (constants.js, cited in levers.md 7.1) does not emulate the preference, so gating heavy effects on `reduce` saves users but not scores; gate on width and pointer for cost, on reduced motion for accessibility. Library hooks: GSAP `gsap.matchMedia().add({reduceMotion:'(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'}, ...)` reverts tweens/triggers automatically when the preference flips; Lenis `respectReducedMotion` default true (lerp 1, instant programmatic scroll); Elementor Pro Motion Effects: 'If a user has set [reduce motion], then motion effects is disabled for that user'; Elementor core: Swiper handler `applyMotionPreferences` sets `speed:0, autoplay:false` under reduce; Pro Animated Headline skips its loop under reduce; Elementor Interactions runtime (4.3.5) has no check - add the CSS override from finding 5. Entrance animations: Elementor's animations.min.css has no reduced-motion rule either, so add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){.animated{animation:none !important}.elementor-invisible{visibility:visible !important}}`. WCAG 2.2.2 (Level A) still applies to autoplaying loops regardless of the media query (pause control). Keep a user-facing toggle optional only; the OS setting is the standard.
findings.breaks_when: A build uses `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` as the only mobile gate ('phones have reduce on') - Lighthouse and most users do not, so the heavy path ships and scores; reduced-motion users get Elementor Interactions/entrance animations at full strength (no built-in check); the CSS override is placed before Elementor's animation stylesheets without `!important` (specificity loses); the reduced-motion path removes content instead of motion (opacity stays 0 because the reveal relied on JS that was skipped).
findings.how_to_apply: Child theme CSS, loaded after Elementor frontend CSS: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){ *,*::before,*::after{animation-duration:.01ms !important;animation-iteration-count:1 !important;transition-duration:.01ms !important;scroll-behavior:auto !important} .elementor-invisible{visibility:visible !important} [data-interactions],.reveal{opacity:1 !important;transform:none !important} }`; JS bundles start with `if (matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) return;` after making sure all targets are in their final visible state; GSAP via `gsap.matchMedia`.
findings.how_to_verify: Puppeteer `page.emulateMediaFeatures([{name:'prefers-reduced-motion', value:'reduce'}])` then assert: no element has computed `animationName !== 'none'` with a duration over 10 ms, `.elementor-invisible` count 0, every `.reveal`/`[data-interactions]` has `opacity === '1'`, Lenis is absent or `lenis.options.lerp === 1`, and the page screenshot equals the fully revealed state; separately run Lighthouse normally (no-preference) and confirm the budget is met without the flag.

findings.claim: Acceptance recipe that proves a page is both beautiful and fast: serial Lighthouse median-of-3 with benchmarkIndex gate, LCP-element and animation-count assertions, a Puppeteer scroll+tap probe reading web-vitals attribution INP and long-animation-frames, a layout-shift observer, a reduced-motion pass, and a desktop visual check that the motion is actually there.
findings.detail: Scoring facts: Lighthouse 10+ weights FCP 10%, SI 10%, LCP 25%, TBT 30%, CLS 25%; metric curves (mobile, source): LCP p10 2,500 ms / median 4,000; TBT p10 200 / median 600 (TBT page: 0-200 green, 200-600 orange, over 600 red); CLS p10 0.1 / median 0.25; INP p10 200 / median 500 (field only - Lighthouse does not interact, and web-vitals: 'INP is not reported if the user never interacts with the page'). Variability doc: 'the median Lighthouse score of 5 runs is twice as stable as 1 run', use median/p90, run serially ('concurrent runs can skew performance results'), minimum 2 dedicated cores, 2 GB RAM; throttling doc: constant 4x CPU multiplier, `benchmarkIndex` is saved in every report (Moto G4 class 125-800, desktop 1,500-2,000+), calibrate before comparing. The plugin's rule 2 already fixes median-of-3 with benchmarkIndex over ~1,000 and a forced-execution run for Delay-JS sites. web-vitals 6.2.3 (Apache-2.0, iife 9.0 KB / 3.3 KB gz, attribution 5.5 KB gz): `onINP(cb, {reportAllChanges:true})` with `web-vitals/attribution` gives `interactionTarget`, `interactionType`, `inputDelay`, `processingDuration`, `presentationDelay`, `longAnimationFrameEntries`, `longestScript`, `totalScriptDuration`; `onCLS`, `onLCP` likewise. Lab probe built here (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/bundle/scroll-cost.mjs): Puppeteer 24, viewport 412x823 DPR 1.75 touch, `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate 4`, `long-animation-frame` observer, 24 wheel steps of 400 px every 250 ms, then report `longFrames`, `maxFrame`, `loafBlocking`, top `scripts[].sourceURL`; extend it with `page.tap()` on the menu toggle, first CTA and an accordion to collect INP via the attribution build injected with `addScriptTag`. In this run no 30-element variant produced a frame over 50 ms on a benchmarkIndex ~2,500 host at 4x - treat the probe as a regression detector (compare against the no-motion build), not as a phone simulator; CrUX p75 INP after 28 days is the field truth.
findings.breaks_when: Runs are done in parallel or on a shared-core box (benchmarkIndex under 1,000, TBT inflated 2-3x); a single PSI run is used to declare 95-100; INP is 'measured' with Lighthouse (it is not); the probe only loads the page and never scrolls or taps (scroll handlers, Lenis and marquees are invisible to load-only metrics - shown by marquee-interval: TBT 0, +413 ms main thread); the reduced-motion pass is skipped so the OS-setting path (no JS gate) ships broken reveals.
findings.how_to_apply: CI/agent steps per template: (1) `for i in 1 2 3; do lighthouse URL --only-categories=performance --output=json --output-path=run-$i.json --chrome-flags='--headless=new'; done` serially; read `environment.benchmarkIndex` (discard under 1,000), medians of score/LCP/TBT/CLS, and assert: score at least 95, LCP under 2,500 ms with `largest-contentful-paint-element` = text or `` with no `elementor-invisible`, Render Delay under 300 ms and under 40% of LCP, TBT under 300 ms, CLS at most 0.05, `render-blocking-resources` empty, no `gsap|anime|motion|lottie|lenis|three|swiper` request before LCP, total motion JS at most 50 KB gz. (2) Puppeteer probe: `.elementor-invisible`/`[data-interactions]` in first viewport = 0, total at most 20; scroll+tap run: zero `long-animation-frame` entries with `blockingDuration` over 0 attributed to motion URLs, INP from web-vitals attribution under 200 ms, CLS observer total at most 0.05 after scroll-through. (3) Reduced-motion emulation pass (finding 16). (4) Desktop 1,440 px run with screenshots at 0/1/2 s and after scroll proving the animations play. (5) 28 days later: CrUX API `inp.percentiles.p75` and `largest_contentful_paint` for the origin/URL.
