findings.how_to_verify: Each assertion maps to a JSON path: `categories.performance.score`, `audits.largest-contentful-paint.numericValue`, `audits['largest-contentful-paint-element'].details.items[1].items[*]` (phases), `audits.total-blocking-time.numericValue`, `audits.cumulative-layout-shift.numericValue`, `audits['render-blocking-resources'].details.items`, `audits['network-requests'].details.items[*].{url,startTime,transferSize}`, `audits['bootup-time'].details.items`, `environment.benchmarkIndex`; probe output JSONL as in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/lh2/scroll-cost.jsonl; summariser /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/bin/summ.py.

title: Local design/motion skills on this machine: what to delegate to, what to write new
summary: Read 30+ SKILL.md files under /root/.claude (skills/synced and plugins/synced) plus the plugin's elementor-build skill, design-to-elementor.md, levers.md 7.1/7.6, sites-in-the-wild rules and breakage-checklist. Verdict: the machine already holds (a) an excellent, stack-neutral motion value system (Emil Kowalski family: animate, review-animations, improve-animations, find-animation-opportunities, emil-design-eng, animation-vocabulary; design-motion-principles with numeric anti-slop heuristics), (b) a strong art-direction engine for marketing pages (tasteskill v2 = taste-skill~g2/skills/taste-skill: draw.mjs directions, house rules, inspect.mjs that runs on a live URL), (c) a UX-psychology layer (perception-first-design), (d) WCAG 2.2 and polish checklists (ECC accessibility, make-interfaces-feel-better, frontend-design-direction), and (e) library references (animejs v4 skill, ui-ux-pro-max GSAP motion.csv). None of them knows WordPress, Elementor JSON, Global Classes/Variables, Interactions, cache-plugin Delay-JS, or the Lighthouse facts that decide the score (reduced-motion is false under Lighthouse; `elementor-invisible` is removed only after Elementor JS; LCP must be text or one ). Several directly contradict the plugin's gate: tasteskill fails a page with fewer than 8 moving elements and animates the hero headline/picture on load, FAILs pages with under 4 photographs and WARNs without video; its scroll scenes load GSAP 3.15 + ScrollTrigger + Lenis from jsdelivr; ui-ux-pro-max GSAP snippets hide content with `gsap.from({opacity:0})`; ECC motion-* and taste-skill-v1 are React/"motion claimed, motion shown" worlds. So the new elementor-design and elementor-motion skills should delegate judgement (direction, copy, critique, motion values, a11y) to the local skills and write new only the translation layer: recipe -> Elementor placement (Interactions / Global Class state variants / Pro Custom Code / child theme), the JSON lint, the conflict register that says which loaded-skill rules the plugin overrides, the live-URL snapshot workflow so file:line review skills can run, and the handover evidence format. Findings below give the which-skill-when map first, then the gaps and conflicts, then one finding per skill family with exact names, values, and what to do with the output in Elementor.
critic_notes: Method: opened every local file cited (paths exist; quoted lines verified by grep), ran tasteskill's draw.mjs/inspect.mjs and ui-ux-pro-max's search.py in this environment, measured bundle sizes from jsdelivr (gsap 3.15.0, animejs 4.5.0) and raw.githubusercontent (Elementor motion.min.js), sparse-cloned elementor/elementor at b4ca769 (2026-10-21) to read the Interactions module, and fetched official pages with curl through the proxy (WebFetch could not resolve most hosts). Main corrections: skill-name collision on `design-taste-frontend`; Interactions mechanics (no CSS hidden state, load/scrollIn/scrollOut only on core frontend, no reduced-motion, breakpoint exclusion, postmeta cache, gated by e_atomic_elements); WCAG 2.2 criterion numbering (2.4.11 is Focus Not Obscured, Focus Appearance is 2.4.13 AAA); anime.js dist bundle is 41 KB gz, not 24.5; Chrome is present and runs with a --no-sandbox shim. Not verified: Elementor Pro's own Interactions handlers (hover/click/scrollOn may work with Pro loaded — test on the dev site), Perfmatters attribute-based exclusions (none documented), Firefox cross-document view-transition status from Mozilla's own notes (search results only), the GSAP standard-license carve-out text (page body did not render), and the plugin reference's 'Elementor 4.3 release' vs main-branch differences for the Interactions module. Skipped: no website or WordPress setting was modified; Novamira tools were not called. Risk for the user: findings that quote Elementor main-branch source may lag or lead the installed 4.3.x by a release.

findings.claim: Which skill when: a routing table that elementor-design and elementor-motion should embed so the builder delegates judgement to the local skills and keeps only the Elementor translation for itself.
findings.detail:
Task -> skill (exact name on this machine) -> what to pass -> what to do with the output in Elementor:
1. Read brief, inventory the subject, write the argument, deal a direction -> `design-taste-frontend` (tasteskill v2, plugin taste-skill~g2, skill folder `skills/taste-skill`) steps 1-5: `node <skill>/scripts/draw.mjs --sector <sector> --brief "..." --sections <roles> [--tone] [--have photography,product-photo] [--keep palette,type] --options 3`, then `--direction <id>`. Pass: brief, real imagery inventory, existing brand. Output: direction sheet (idea, composition, type system, palette, hero and section blueprints). Elementor: palette -> Variables (<= 8 colours) + v3 kit Global Colors; type system -> 2 families, Variables for family, Global Classes for size/weight/line-height; section blueprints -> the section spec of design-to-elementor §7 step 1.
2. Tokens from a live reference -> `extract-design-system <url>` -> `.extract-design-system/normalized.json` -> prune to the §1 budget.
3. Booking/enquiry/checkout UX, conversion, copy structure -> `perception-first-design:solve` (skill `pfd`, Mode 2) with the design problem stated as user experience, not features; output R1-R5 requirements -> page plan constraints (fewer options at decision points, demonstrate price/availability, 2 fonts/3-4 colours).
4. CTA / error / empty-state / confirmation copy in Greek and English -> `design:ux-copy` (plugin afe29730..., skills/ux-copy) with context, user state, tone; output table incl. Localization Notes -> button `text`, Form error messages, Loop Grid "no results" text.
5. Micro-polish of components -> `ecc:make-interfaces-feel-better` -> Global Class CSS (concentric radius, text-wrap balance/pretty, tabular-nums, explicit transition-property, 44 px hit areas).
6. Accessibility design + audit (WCAG 2.2 AA, 24x24 targets, focus appearance) -> `ecc:accessibility`; WCAG 2.1 table format with contrast/keyboard/SR tables -> `design:accessibility-review`.
7. Decide whether something should animate, and the exact curve/duration/spring -> `anthropic-skills:animate` (build sequence: frequency gate, purpose, cheapest tool, transform/opacity, easing, interruption, reduced motion) and `anthropic-skills:emil-design-eng`; output = CSS/WAAPI recipe -> elementor-motion maps it to Interactions, Global Class state variants, or Pro Custom Code.
8. Name an effect the client describes -> `anthropic-skills:animation-vocabulary` -> look the term up in elementor-motion's capability table (allowed / below-fold only / banned).
9. Find where a built page should animate -> `anthropic-skills:find-animation-opportunities` on the page snapshot (HTML + post-N.css + screenshots); output table with exact values + REQUIRED rejected list -> implement only rows that are below the fold.
10. Review motion before publish (Critique phase) -> `anthropic-skills:review-animations` (Block/Approve verdict) and `design-motion-principles` Audit mode with its anti-checklist; input = snapshot of Custom Code CSS/JS + child-theme JS + rendered CSS.
11. Audit a whole site's existing motion and write executable plans -> `anthropic-skills:improve-animations` (plans/NNN-slug.md self-contained for a cheaper executor).
12. Library APIs -> `anthropic-skills:animejs` (v4 API, module sizes) and `ui-ux-pro-max` `search.py "..." --domain gsap` (GSAP snippets by tier) -> code goes to the child theme, enqueued per page, never above the fold.
13. Design critique of screenshots -> `design-taste-frontend` step 8 with `references/critique.md` (14 passes, Awwwards-weighted score) or `design:design-critique`; `impeccable critique` when PRODUCT.md/DESIGN.md exist.
14. Final visual gate on the published URL -> `node <taste-skill>/scripts/inspect.mjs <url> --widths 1440,768,390 [--allow rule,...]` plus Lighthouse 3x median per design-to-elementor §7.
Everything after the arrow "Elementor:" is what no local skill does and the new skills must write.
findings.breaks_when: The builder loads a design skill and follows it literally (its stack, its motion budget, its CDN scripts) instead of using it as an adviser: tasteskill's step 9 or scenes.md would add a GSAP+Lenis bundle and a hero load sequence, dropping LCP render delay from <300 ms to seconds and failing the 95 gate; impeccable/FDD would write React/CSS files nobody enqueues.
findings.how_to_apply: Put this table verbatim in skills/elementor-design/SKILL.md (rows 1-6, 13-14) and skills/elementor-motion/SKILL.md (rows 7-12, 14) with a one-line rule: 'these skills decide what and how it should look/move; this skill decides where it lives in Elementor and whether the gate still passes'. Have the elementor-designer and elementor-motion-designer agents invoke them via the Skill tool by the exact names above.
findings.how_to_verify: Dry run on one brief: each row produces an artefact (direction sheet, R1-R5, copy table, review table) that is then consumed by an Elementor step (Variables/Classes written via `novamira/elementor-create-global-class`, `elementor-set-content`, Custom Code); the page then passes design-to-elementor §7 step 7 (median >= 95, LCP <= 2.0 s, render delay < 40% of LCP, 0 `elementor-invisible` above 800 px at 390 px).
findings.correction: Row 1 must invoke `taste-skill:taste-skill` (never the bare `design-taste-frontend`); sectors: hospitality / restaurant / ecommerce / event / other; row 2 is `anthropic-skills:extract-design-system`; row 12 runs `python3 <plugin>/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/scripts/search.py ... --domain gsap` without `-I`. Add one line to both SKILL.md files: 'the Skill tool has two `design-taste-frontend` entries; only `taste-skill:taste-skill` is allowed'.

findings.claim: The gaps the new skills must fill are one thing: the Elementor translation layer. No local skill outputs Elementor JSON, Global Classes/Variables, Interactions, Pro Custom Code, child-theme enqueues, cache-plugin exclusions, or the Lighthouse facts that decide the score.
findings.detail: What to write new (nothing else; everything else is delegated): (a) Recipe -> placement table for every motion recipe the local skills produce: hover/press/focus -> Global Class `variants[].meta.state` (hover) and CSS `:active` in the class (zero JS, zero bytes beyond the class); entrance/scroll reveal -> V4 Interactions (`interactions[]` on the atomic element; `motion.min.js` 128 KB raw enqueued only on pages that use one; <= 2 per page; never in the first top-level container) or Pro Custom Code CSS + one IntersectionObserver (location body-end, priority high, conditions = only the pages that use it); scroll-linked drift/progress -> CSS `animation-timeline: view()` inside `@supports` in the kit/Custom Code, travel <= 8%, static fallback; timelines/SVG draw/stagger beyond CSS -> anime.js v4 or GSAP as an ES module in the Inglelandi child theme, `wp_enqueue_script` per page, `type=module`, excluded from Delay-JS (`data-no-optimize="1"`, `nowprocket`, LiteSpeed skips non text/javascript types), loaded after LCP; v3 `_animation` entrance -> never (adds `elementor-invisible` = visibility:hidden until Elementor JS). (b) The CSS-first hidden-state pattern adapted from tasteskill's `html.js` gate: hidden states only under `html.js` (one inline `` in the child theme `wp_head`, excluded from delay) AND `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so a failed or delayed script never leaves content at opacity 0. (c) Lighthouse facts the skills do not know: `prefers-reduced-motion` and Save-Data are false under Lighthouse (levers.md 7.6/7.1), so reduced-motion fallbacks never rescue the score; the LCP element is text or the first dimensioned ; `elementor-invisible` above the fold = render delay of 3.6-7.8 s on the agency's sites; third-party <= 150 KB; TBT < 300 ms. (d) Lint on `_elementor_data` before `elementor-set-content` (extends design-to-elementor §5 'Sequence per page'): no non-empty `interactions` and no `_animation`/`motion_fx` in the first top-level container or header; <= 2 interactions per page; <= 20 animated elements; no `
findings.breaks_when: Without (a)-(d) a motion recipe written in good faith lands as a v3 entrance animation on the hero (voreniahorizon pattern: h1 `_animation: fadeIn`, render delay 7,831 ms of an 8.95 s LCP) or as a GSAP bundle on every page (platonos: 1.78 s bootup for gsap + ScrollTrigger + SplitText); without (b) a Delay-JS plugin leaves reveal targets invisible until the first touch.
findings.how_to_apply: Write skills/elementor-motion/SKILL.md around table (a) and pattern (b), with (c) as a 'Lighthouse facts' box; add the lint (d) to a script under skills/elementor-motion/scripts (reads the content array, returns violations by element id); put (e) into skills/elementor-design/SKILL.md referencing design-to-elementor §1; keep the recipe values themselves out of the plugin (point to the local skills) except where the Elementor placement changes them.
findings.how_to_verify: Lint a tree that contains `_animation` in the first container and 3 `interactions` -> 2 violations. Build one page with a below-fold reveal via pattern (b), run Lighthouse mobile 3x: `elementor-invisible` count above 800 px at 390 px = 0, LCP render delay < 40%, `motion.min.js` absent from the network log on pages without an Interaction; then throttle JS off (DevTools 'Disable JavaScript') and confirm the revealed content is visible.
sources: https://github.com/elementor/elementor (sparse clone b4ca769: modules/interactions/assets/js/interactions.js, interactions-utils.js, interactions-shared-utils.js, interactions-frontend-handler.php, validators/trigger-value.php, cache/interactions-postmeta.php, modules/atomic-widgets/module.php)
findings.correction: Rewrite the Interactions row: 'V4 Interactions = JS-only entrance (load/scrollIn/scrollOut, fade/slide/scale, duration/delay, breakpoints.excluded); element is visible until motion.min.js (42 KB gz) runs, then flashes to its start state — so above the fold it costs a flash and JS, below the fold it is fine; hover/click/while-scrolling are not executed by core frontend JS, keep hover in Global Class variants; no reduced-motion handling, so add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) [data-interaction-id]{transition:none}` is NOT possible (inline styles) — accept or avoid.' Lint (d) must also read `[data-interaction-id]` in rendered HTML and check `breakpoints.excluded` for mobile when the owner wants desktop-only reveals. After `elementor-set-content`, delete postmeta `elementor-interactions-cache` for that post (or re-save through the document) and re-check `#elementor-interactions-data` on the frontend. Replace `e_interactions` with `e_atomic_elements` in the pre-conditions.

findings.claim: Conflict register: several installed skills contain hard rules that contradict the plugin's gate; the new SKILL.md files must name them and state that the gate wins, or the agent will obey the loaded skill.
findings.detail:
1. tasteskill v2 `references/motion.md` §1: "the inspector ... fails it under eight elements (warns under sixteen)" and the 'Load sequence in 1.2 seconds' recipe animates the hero headline lines (`transform: translateY(105%)`, 800 ms), the hero picture (`clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0)`, 1000 ms) and the CTA on load. Plugin rule 13 / levers 7.6: no animation above the fold or on the LCP element. Resolution: keep the budget idea (choreographed, not uniform) but count only below-fold elements; the 'signature move' moves to the first section after the hero or becomes the 'Receding hero' (CSS `animation-timeline: --hero; animation-range: exit 0% exit 100%`, zero JS) pending measurement (open question).
2. tasteskill `scripts/lib/rules.mjs`: FAIL `few-pictures` when < 4 raster pictures, WARN `no-footage` when no <video>. Plugin: page <= 1 MB, <= 50 requests, no autoplay video on mobile hero, every <video> poster + preload=none. Resolution: run inspect.mjs with `--allow few-pictures,no-footage` (or defend each) and cap pictures by the §4 image budget (hero <= 100 KB, no image > 300 KB).
3. tasteskill `references/scenes.md` + `assets/scenes/stage.js`: loads `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.15.0/dist/gsap.min.js`, `ScrollTrigger.min.js`, optional `SplitText.min.js`, `lenis@1.3.26`, and `Stage.smooth()` (Lenis lerp 0.12). Plugin: third-party <= 150 KB, no CDN scripts, 'Lenis/smooth-scroll before LCP' is a blocker, no scroll hijack. Resolution: scenes only self-hosted, below the fold, loaded on interaction/visibility, never Lenis; or not at all on mobile (stage.js already falls back to the finished composition for `(pointer: coarse)` and reduced motion, which is the right default).
4. `design-taste-frontend` (skills/synced, 87 KB v2-experimental text) §5 "Motion claimed, motion shown: entry transitions on hero, scroll-reveal on key sections, hover physics on CTAs" when MOTION_INTENSITY > 4, GSAP sticky-stack/horizontal-pan skeletons, Motion `whileInView`, 'Perpetual Micro-Interactions'. Plugin forbids all of it above the fold; its CWV targets (LCP < 2.5 s, CLS < 0.1) are looser than the plugin's (2.0 s, 0.05). Resolution: do not load this file for Elementor work; use the taste-skill~g2 v2 instead.
5. `taste-skill-v1` (MOTION_INTENSITY 6 default, §9 'Motion-Engine Bento Paradigm, perpetual motion'): never load.
6. ui-ux-pro-max `data/motion.csv` rows 4-8: `gsap.from(el, { opacity: 0, y: 12 ... scrollTrigger })` sets the hidden state from JS at runtime (content flashes then hides; with Delay-JS it stays hidden until interaction) and row 6 pins sections (`pin: true, scrub: 1`). Resolution: take only durations/eases/Do-Don't, write hidden state in CSS under `html.js`.
7. ECC `motion-foundations` rule 3 'reduced motion disables all transforms' and `isLowEnd()` via `navigator.hardwareConcurrency <= 4`: React-only; Lighthouse reports the host's cores, so neither changes the lab score.
8. `design-motion-principles/references/accessibility.md` global `* { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important }` under reduced motion: harmless to the score (reduced motion is false under Lighthouse) but it would snap every Interaction; prefer Emil's 'gentler, not zero'.
9. `impeccable` 'Persuade' mode: 'Ship real imagery when the brief needs it' and 500-800 ms authored focal entrances: fine below the fold; the hero stays static.
findings.breaks_when: An agent with tasteskill loaded reaches step 9 or runs inspect.mjs, sees `FAIL few-pictures` / 'under eight moving elements', and 'fixes' the page by adding photographs and hero animation: page weight > 1 MB, LCP render delay in seconds, score drops 10-30 points (cretaforums 76 animations = 74; voreniahorizon 160 animations + video = 50).
findings.how_to_apply: Add a 'Rules from other skills that do not apply here' section to both new SKILL.md files listing items 1-9 with the replacement; have the elementor-ux-reviewer agent treat any of the nine as a finding; pass `--allow few-pictures,no-footage` by default when running inspect.mjs on Elementor pages.
findings.how_to_verify: Grep the final SKILL.md files for 'eight', 'Lenis', 'gsap@', 'MOTION_INTENSITY', 'whileInView' and confirm each appears only inside the override section; run inspect.mjs on a passing page and confirm the only FAILs left are ones the register explicitly allows.

findings.claim: tasteskill v2 (`design-taste-frontend`, folder taste-skill~g2/skills/taste-skill) is the strongest design-direction source on the machine and its inspector runs on a live URL; delegate steps 1-8 and the house rules to it, override step 9 (motion) and the imagery floor.
findings.detail: What it provides: `scripts/draw.mjs` deals 3 of 20 researched directions (library distilled from 247 One Page Love / Awwwards sites) then a full sheet (idea, composition, type system, palette, hero, section blueprints, one signature move, scroll scenes when the library has them); `references/copy.md` (claims-with-proof argument, two-line headline arithmetic), `type.md`, `colour.md`, `layout.md`, `imagery.md` (incl. §7 real interface fragments with `data-ui`), `critique.md` (14 passes, Awwwards-weighted score, caps), `tells.md`, `research.md`; `scripts/assets.mjs` finds openly licensed pictures of the subject's world (needs network, no keys); `scripts/lint.mjs` (Node 18+) scans source for banned patterns; `scripts/inspect.mjs <url | file> [--widths 1440,768,390] [--allow rule,...] [--app] [--json]` measures a real page in Chrome and screenshots it. House rules worth adopting as Global Class defaults: headlines <= 2 lines at every width; one h1 on the first screen, a heading per section; equal outer margins; no eyebrows/pill badges; no monospace labels; no index numbering; no hairlines/1 px outlined boxes; no gradients (one neutral scrim exception); no shadows at rest; no cream+terracotta or violet palette; no tiny tracked caps; no icon-topped card rows; no glass; no styled accent word; two typefaces max. Laws: display tracking -0.02 to -0.05 em, leading 0.85-1.05; text 16-20 px, leading 1.45-1.6, 45-75 ch; five sizes ceiling; section gap 120-240 px; one ground/one ink/one accent; buttons flat, square or fully round. Inspector rule ids (rules.mjs): headline-lines, statement-length, hero-words, eyebrow, mono, numbering, micro-label, emoji, gradient, gradient-text, shadow, text-shadow, button-fx, hairline, outlined-box, dashed, glass, icon-cards, card-rows, pill-nav, palette-claude/terracotta/cream/purple, contrast, font-count, font-fallback, size-count, body-size, grey-body, first-action, few-pictures, no-real-pictures, no-footage, no-poster, side-scroll, blend-text, measure, small-text, all-centred, ui-wrapper, overflow, broken-image, no-hero, focal-point, off-centre. Stack assumption: HTML/CSS/React/etc. output in a project folder (`.taste-skill/`), Node 22 + Chrome; it knows nothing of Elementor markup. Environment check: Node v22.22.0 present; `CHROME_PATH` empty and lighthouse not installed in this session, so inspect.mjs needs a Chrome install or the chrome-devtools MCP as a fallback for screenshots.
findings.breaks_when: Step 9 or scenes.md is followed (see conflict register); or inspect.mjs is pointed at an Elementor page that Elementor itself styles with hairline dividers (`e-divider`), 1 px form borders outside form fields, or `.elementor-widget-container` outlines and its FAILs are 'fixed' by adding ornament elsewhere; or `assets.mjs` downloads 6-12 pictures that blow the 1 MB page budget.
findings.how_to_apply: In elementor-design: run steps 1-5 before any Elementor write; map the sheet to Variables/Classes; adopt the house rules as the Global Class defaults (h1-h6, p, a, button, div padding 0); run `inspect.mjs <published-url> --widths 1440,768,390 --allow few-pictures,no-footage` as a gate alongside Lighthouse; use `critique.md` for the look loop at 390/768/1440; cap pictures by design-to-elementor §4. Record `--allow` reasons in the handover. Skip step 9; route motion to elementor-motion.
findings.how_to_verify: `node <skill>/scripts/draw.mjs --list sectors` prints sectors (hotel/restaurant/shop map to one each); `node <skill>/scripts/inspect.mjs https://<dev-site>/ --json` returns 0 FAIL other than allowed ids on a passing page; screenshots land in `.taste-skill/inspect/`; the page still meets the Lighthouse gate afterwards.
findings.correction: Document in the plugin README: `CHROME_PATH=/path/to/chrome-nosandbox.sh node <taste-skill>/scripts/inspect.mjs <url> --widths 1440,768,390 --allow few-pictures,no-footage,still-page,scene-not-started,reduced-hidden --json`; the shim is `#!/bin/sh\nexec /root/.cache/puppeteer/chrome/linux-148.0.7778.97/chrome-linux64/chrome --no-sandbox "$@"`. Use sector `hospitality` for hotels/villas, `restaurant`, `ecommerce` for the water-park shop, `other` for the forum.

findings.claim: The Emil Kowalski motion family (animate, review-animations, improve-animations, find-animation-opportunities, emil-design-eng) is the right source of motion values and the right Critique gate; it is stack-neutral CSS/WAAPI but assumes code files and Base UI, so elementor-motion must supply the Elementor placement and the above-the-fold rule.
findings.detail: Shared value system (identical across the five files, copy exactly): tokens `--ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`, `--ease-in-out: cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)`, `--ease-drawer: cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)`; durations press 100-160 ms, tooltips 125-200, dropdowns 150-250, modals/drawers 200-500, UI < 300 ms, marketing may be longer; frequency gate (100+/day or keyboard = never animate; rare = delight budget); purpose must be feedback / spatial consistency / state indication / preventing a jarring change / explanation / delight; transform+opacity only (clip-path sanctioned, height only for accordions); never `scale(0)` (use 0.9-0.97 + opacity); `transform-origin` at the trigger except modals; transitions not keyframes for anything re-triggered; `@starting-style` for entry; springs `{ type: "spring", duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.2 }`, bounce 0.1-0.3; stagger 30-80 ms; exit the way it entered; asymmetric hold-to-confirm (2 s linear press, 200 ms release); `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` gentler not zero; `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` for hover; WAAPI `element.animate([...], { duration, fill: 'forwards', easing })` for programmatic motion without a library; blur <= 20 px to mask crossfades; never drive child transforms from a parent CSS variable. `review-animations` outputs a Before/After/Why table + Block/Approve; escalation triggers include `transition: all`, ease-in on UI, > 300 ms UI, keyframes on toasts, layout props, missing reduced motion, ungated hover. `find-animation-opportunities` caps at 5-7 suggestions and REQUIRES a rejected list. `improve-animations` writes plans/NNN-slug.md with exact file:line, target CSS, boundaries, mechanical + feel verification. Stack assumptions: `file:line` evidence in a repo, `var(--transform-origin)` from Base UI, React `useReducedMotion`, Motion library for springs/gestures. Gaps for Elementor: no notion of LCP, above-the-fold, Lighthouse, `elementor-invisible`, Interactions, Delay-JS; the 'cheapest tool' ladder (CSS transition -> @starting-style -> CSS animation -> WAAPI -> Motion) must gain the Elementor rungs (Global Class state variant -> Interaction -> Custom Code CSS -> child-theme module) and the rule that the first rung that is zero-JS wins.
findings.breaks_when: The reviewer is pointed at the live page instead of files (it needs file:line and will decline), or `animate` is asked to animate the hero and obeys the request's frequency tier ('rare, once per visit') and writes a hero entrance that the plugin's gate forbids.
findings.how_to_apply: elementor-motion: cite the tokens above as the house tokens written once into the kit Custom CSS (`:root { --ease-out: ... }`), prepend one gate before `animate`'s step 1 ('is it above the fold or on the LCP element? then no'), and extend step 3's ladder with the Elementor rungs. Critique phase: snapshot Custom Code CSS/JS and child-theme JS to a local folder, run `review-animations` (Block = do not publish), `find-animation-opportunities` for the below-fold candidates, `improve-animations` for a site-wide motion audit of an existing site (its plans become the debloater's work list).
findings.how_to_verify: Feed `review-animations` a snapshot containing `transition: all 400ms ease-in` on a button class: expect a Block with the Before/After row. Feed `find-animation-opportunities` a page with an instant accordion and a hero: expect the accordion in the table and the hero in the rejected list (frequency/first-screen).

findings.claim: design-motion-principles adds two things the Emil family lacks: a project-type weighting (hotels/restaurants are 'Marketing/landing: Jakub primary, Jhey secondary, Emil for forms/nav'; the water-park shop is 'E-commerce: Jakub, Emil, Jhey for product showcase') and a numeric anti-slop checklist that works as a lint over rendered CSS.
findings.detail: Modes: Create (`workflows/create.md`, always loads `references/motion-cookbook.md` + `creation-gotchas.md`) and Audit (`workflows/audit.md`, loads `audit-checklist.md` + `anti-checklist.md`, emits a branded HTML report by default, terminal mode by flag). Anti-checklist heuristics to reuse verbatim as elementor-motion lint thresholds: pulsing indicators = flag ANY instance (`@keyframes *pulse|glow|breathe|throb*`, `animation: ... infinite` on small elements, Tailwind `animate-pulse`); blur-everywhere = >= 3 components sharing the same `filter: blur()` enter; hover-scale-on-everything = >= 3 components with the same `scale(1.0X)` on :hover; stagger-spam = >= 2 lists per view with stagger; bouncy springs on utility actions = any bounce > 0 on dropdown/menu/toggle/modal; uniform fade-in = >= 4 components with identical opacity+translateY+duration+easing; motion-on-mount for static content = any entrance on h1/h2/p/nav whose only purpose is the entrance (this one is the plugin's rule 13 in design language). Duration table is context-dependent (Emil < 300 ms / 180 ideal; Jakub 200-500; Jhey whatever serves) and the skill says 'do not universally cap'. Cookbook items usable in Elementor Custom CSS without JS: `@property --x { syntax: '<percentage>'; initial-value: 0%; inherits: false }` typed variables for curved paths; `linear()` easing; clip-path reveals; scroll-driven `animation-timeline` with the 'duration control' pattern (scroll-driven trigger toggles a custom property, a Style Query starts a fixed-duration animation) and the fallback `if (!CSS.supports('animation-timeline', 'scroll()'))` -> IntersectionObserver. Performance.md: will-change on 0-3 elements fine, 4-10 careful, 10+ reconsider; cheap gradient animation = background-position/size only. Stack assumption: React/Framer Motion/CSS/HTML; no WordPress.
findings.breaks_when: Audit mode is run on a 10-page site with HTML output (slow, writes report files) instead of the terminal flag; or the Jhey lens is weighted for a booking page and playful overshoot lands on the date picker.
findings.how_to_apply: Use the context table to set the default lens per site type in elementor-design's brief read (hotel/villa/restaurant = Jakub+Jhey below the fold, Emil for header/nav/forms/booking; forum = Emil); encode the seven anti-slop thresholds in the elementor-ux-reviewer agent's checklist and run them over the page's post-N.css + Custom Code CSS; borrow the scroll-driven 'duration control' pattern for below-fold reveals that must not play at scroll speed.
findings.how_to_verify: Run Audit (terminal mode) on a page with `hover:scale-105` on 6 cards and one pulsing 'live' dot: expect two findings (hover-scale >= 3, pulse any). Run it on a plugin-compliant page: expect zero AI-slop findings.

findings.claim: tasteskill's `references/motion.md` is the best local library of marketing-page motion recipes that are CSS-first and JS-optional, with a measured study behind the numbers; elementor-motion should import its tokens and the below-fold recipes and reject its hero load sequence and scenes.
findings.detail: Tokens (study of 99 Awwwards SOTD, Jul-Oct 2026): `--ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` (< 600 ms), `--ease-expo: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` (reveals >= 800 ms), `--ease-in-out: cubic-bezier(0.76, 0, 0.24, 1)` (wipes), `--ease-soft: cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1)` (slow photo drift), `--ease-exit: cubic-bezier(0.55, 0.055, 0.675, 0.19)` (leaving for good, 60-70% of entrance), `--t-press: 140ms; --t-hover: 180ms; --t-ui: 240ms; --t-reveal: 800ms; --t-open: 1200ms; --stagger-line: 90ms; --stagger-item: 70ms`. Study facts: median running transition 420 ms; reveals fire at 80-95% of viewport, once; 14 of 18 scrubbing sites lock to the scrollbar (linear); parallax travel < 8%; 60 of 99 sites use a preloader and half were unreadable 2.5 s after load (house: none; readable first frame; load sequence over by 1.2 s); 35 of 99 have any reduced-motion rule. Recipes safe for Elementor below the fold (all keep content visible without JS, hidden state only under `.js` + `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`): 'Reveal on scroll (once)' (`opacity:0; translateY(24px)`, 700/900 ms, IntersectionObserver `rootMargin: '0px 0px -12% 0px'`, `unobserve` after fire); 'Image shutter' (`clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0)` 1100 ms + img `scale(1.12)` 1500 ms); 'Press and hover' (scale .97 at 140 ms, underline-colour hover behind `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`); 'Scroll-linked progress without JavaScript' (`@supports (animation-timeline: view())`, drift -4% to 4%, `animation-range: entry 0% exit 100%`); 'Pinned story' (position: sticky, no hijack); 'Lines that rise on scroll' (JS line split after `document.fonts.ready`, restores plain text on `transitionend`); 'Receding hero' (exit-range scroll timeline on the hero picture/copy, zero JS, static fallback; needs a Lighthouse check before use because it touches the LCP element); 'Rolling figures' (replaces the Counter widget's 7.5 KB + jquery-numerator: CSS strips, `tabular-nums`, sr-only real number); 'Accordion' via `grid-template-rows: 0fr -> 1fr` 320 ms; 'Menu or dialog' from the trigger, `scale(0.97) translateY(-6px)`; 'Page to page' with `@view-transition { navigation: auto }` (cross-document, 480 ms max, off under reduced motion); 'Ink fill' one statement starting at 45% ink; 'Sideways gallery' native scroll-snap row first, pinned only on wide screens with keyboard support. Rules 1-14 (§10) are a ready motion policy except rule 1 (load sequence) and rule 7 (scroll scenes). Important caveat in §6: `animation-timeline: view()` takes the nearest scroll container and `overflow: hidden` creates one, so use `overflow: clip` on frames (Elementor containers often set overflow hidden).
findings.breaks_when: The load-sequence or masked-headline recipe is applied to the hero (h1 at `translateY(105%)` until the animation runs = LCP render delay); `overflow: hidden` on an Elementor container silently kills every view() timeline inside it; the Rolling-figures/line-split scripts run before fonts load and leave split spans.
findings.how_to_apply: Copy the token block into elementor-motion as the kit `:root` CSS (one place, Custom Code location head or kit Custom CSS); list the recipes above with their Elementor placement (CSS-only ones in Custom Code with page conditions; IO/line-split JS in the child theme as one deferred module); add 'use overflow: clip, never hidden, on any container that holds a view() timeline' to the lint; reserve 'Receding hero' as owner-OK pending measurement.
findings.how_to_verify: Build one below-fold section with 'Reveal on scroll' and one with the view() drift inside an `e-div-block`; Lighthouse 3x unchanged within spread; scroll in DevTools with JS disabled: content visible; set the container to overflow hidden and confirm the drift stops (then clip and confirm it resumes).

findings.claim: The `animejs` skill is v4 and its API map is usable as-is (animate, createTimeline, stagger, onScroll, createDrawable, splitText, createScope, createLayout new), with per-module gzip sizes that fit the budget; its install guidance (npm, esm.sh, unpinned jsdelivr UMD, React) is not usable on WordPress and must be replaced by a child-theme enqueue.
findings.detail: API names in the skill: `animate(targets, {to, from, delay, duration, ease, composition, modifier, keyframes, loop, alternate, autoplay})`, `createTimeline({defaults})` with `.add(target, params, '<' | '-=200' | label)`, `stagger(100, { from: 'center', grid })`, `onScroll({ container, target, axis, debug, repeat, enter: 'bottom right', leave, sync: true, onEnter, onEnterForward, onEnterBackward, onLeave, onUpdate, onSyncComplete })` passed as `autoplay`, `createDraggable`, `createAnimatable`, `createScope({ root, defaults, mediaQueries })`, `createLayout` (enterFrom/leaveTo/swapAt), SVG `morphTo()`, `createDrawable('path')` with `draw: ['0 0', '0 1']`, `createMotionPath`, `splitText(target, { lines, words, chars, accessible })`, `createSpring({ stiffness, damping, mass, velocity })`, WAAPI adapter `waapi.convertEase()`, engine `{ timeUnit, fps, precision, pauseOnDocumentHidden }`. Sizes stated in the skill (minified+gzipped; not re-verified by me): full bundle ~24.5 KB; timer ~5.6 KB; animation +5.2; timeline +0.55; draggable +6.4; scroll +4.3; scope +0.22; SVG ~0.35; stagger +0.48; spring ~0.52; WAAPI ~3.5. Standalone imports `animejs/animation`, `animejs/timeline`, `animejs/timer` for tree-shaking. CDN example in the skill is `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/animejs/dist/bundles/anime.umd.min.js` (unpinned; violates the plugin's pinning and no-CDN rule). Elementor translation: copy the ESM bundle into `wp-content/themes/inglelandi-child/js/vendor/anime.esm.min.js`, enqueue only on pages that use it (`is_page()` or a page-settings flag) with `wp_enqueue_script_module` or `wp_enqueue_script(..., ['strategy' => 'defer'])`, exclude from Delay-JS, initialise after `requestIdleCallback`/first scroll, use `onScroll({ target, enter: 'bottom-=10% top' })`-style thresholds instead of a scroll listener, `pauseOnDocumentHidden` default on. Budget: a reveal module (timer+animation+scroll+stagger ~15.5 KB gz per the skill's table) is small, but every page that loads it adds a request; prefer CSS-first recipes and reserve anime.js for timelines, SVG draw, text split, draggable.
findings.breaks_when: The UMD CDN URL from the skill is pasted into an HTML widget (third-party host, unpinned, blocked by the plugin's no-script-in-HTML-widget rule and Delay-JS leaves it dead); `splitText` is run on the h1 (LCP text replaced by spans before paint); `onScroll({ sync: true })` scrubs a large image on mobile (INP/TBT).
findings.how_to_apply: In elementor-motion: reference `anthropic-skills:animejs` for API and the `references/api-reference.md` + `references/examples.md` files; add the WordPress enqueue recipe above and a rule 'anime.js only below the fold, one module file per site, versions pinned and self-hosted, never in the first viewport, never on text that is the LCP'. Mark the sizes 'from the skill, verify against animejs.com before quoting to a client'.
findings.how_to_verify: After enqueue: page without the module shows no `anime` request in the Lighthouse network log; page with it shows one same-origin request, `bootup-time` for it < 50 ms, TBT delta < 30 ms over 3 runs; `coverage` in DevTools shows the module executes only after LCP.
findings.correction: Quote 'anime.js v4.5.0, MIT; whole dist bundle 41 KB gz; tree-shaken reveal module (timer+animation+scroll+stagger) about 15.5 KB gz per animejs.com'. Pin `animejs@4.5.0`; build one tree-shaken ESM file (esbuild/rollup) rather than copying `dist/bundles/anime.esm.min.js`, or accept 41 KB and count it in the budget. Keep the rule: never in the first viewport, never splitText on the LCP heading.

findings.claim: ui-ux-pro-max gives a searchable, tiered GSAP snippet table and a token generator; use `search.py --domain gsap` for GSAP syntax and Do/Don't, and `--design-system --variance --motion --density` for a first token draft, but translate its JS-hidden initial states to CSS and ignore its React/npm framing.
findings.detail: Files: `skills/ui-ux-pro-max/data/motion.csv` (17 rows; columns Category, Intensity Tier Subtle/Standard/Complex, Trigger, Duration, Easing, GSAP Snippet, Framework Notes, Do, Don't, Performance Notes), `scripts/search.py "<query>" --domain gsap|ux|style|color|typography|landing|product|icons|google-fonts`, `--design-system [--variance 1-10] [--motion 1-10] [--density 1-10] -p "<project>"` (writes a MASTER.md token sheet; `--motion` attaches the matching GSAP tier). Useful rows: Hover Subtle `gsap.to(el, { y: -1, opacity: 0.9, duration: 0.15, ease: 'power1.out' })`, displacement < 2 px; Scroll Reveal Subtle `gsap.from(el, { opacity: 0, y: 12, duration: 0.35, ease: 'power1.out', scrollTrigger: { trigger: el, start: 'top 90%', toggleActions: 'play none none reverse' } })`; Standard stagger `stagger: 0.08`, do not stagger > ~8 children; Complex pin `scrollTrigger: { start: 'top top', end: '+=150%', scrub: 1, pin: true }`, pin <= 1-2 sections per page, call `ScrollTrigger.refresh()` after images/fonts; every row says to use `gsap.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` and render the final state; `gsap.quickTo` for many hover targets. §7 Animation rules worth quoting: `excessive-motion` 'Animate 1-2 key elements per view max', `exit-faster-than-enter` ~60-70%, `stagger-sequence` 30-50 ms, `layout-shift-avoid`, `cancellable-state-transitions`, `no-blocking-animation`. Also `data/google-fonts.csv` + `google-font-licenses.json` for picking a family (check Greek subset separately; Poppins has none). Gaps: GSAP assumed via npm and `useGSAP` from `@gsap/react`; no sizes, no licence note, no WordPress; `gsap.from({opacity:0})` means the element is visible then hidden by JS (flash) and stays visible if JS is delayed, which is safe for the score but visually wrong; with Delay-JS the reveal fires on first interaction. Python 3 is available on this machine; the skill's `--design-system` output is HTML/Tailwind-flavoured and needs mapping to Variables/Classes.
findings.breaks_when: A Complex-tier pin/scrub row is used on mobile (forced layout reflow on mid-tier phones, INP) or a `gsap.from` reveal targets the hero (`start: 'top 90%'` fires at load and animates the LCP element); the MASTER.md palette over-produces (> 8 colours) and lands in Variables unpruned.
findings.how_to_apply: elementor-motion: 'for GSAP syntax run `python3 <plugin>/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/scripts/search.py "scroll reveal stagger" --domain gsap`'; translate every `gsap.from` hidden state into CSS under `html.js` and use `gsap.to`/`fromTo` with `immediateRender: false`; allow Complex tier only on `(min-width: 1025px)` via `gsap.matchMedia` and never on the hero. elementor-design: use `--design-system --density 3-4 -p <site>` as a draft, prune to the §1 budget before creating Variables.
findings.how_to_verify: `python3 .../search.py "scroll reveal" --domain gsap` returns rows 4-6; a page using the translated Subtle reveal shows no opacity flash on load (DevTools filmstrip), Lighthouse unchanged; with JS disabled all content visible.

findings.claim: impeccable 4.7.0 is the best stack-neutral design-director skill for critique/polish/typeset/layout and its `animate` reference already encodes the plugin's safety rule ('keep content visible in the default state so failed scripts do not hide the page'); use its modes and commands, not its file-writing or launcher-dependent workflow.
findings.detail: Modes to copy into elementor-design's brief read: Persuade (hotel/villa/restaurant landing, pricing: design is the product), Operate (booking flow, checkout, My Account, forum: scanability and native patterns outrank expression), Read (blog, policies), Experience (gallery). Commands (each a reference file under `skills/impeccable/reference/`): `shape` (plan UX before code), `critique` (heuristic scoring), `audit` (a11y/perf/responsive), `polish`, `bolder`, `quieter`, `distill`, `harden` (errors, i18n, edge cases: Greek/English), `onboard` (empty states), `animate`, `colorize`, `typeset`, `layout`, `delight`, `clarify` (UX copy), `adapt` (devices), `optimize` (perf: images srcset/sizes, font-display swap, subset, preload). `animate.md` values: 100-150 ms immediate feedback, 150-300 routine state, 300-500 layout/overlay/view transition, 500-800 one authored focal entrance; `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` for confident arrivals; exit faster than entrance; no bounce/elastic by reflex; one focal moment that comes from this product, 'a generic fade-and-rise, hover lift, parallax layer, or scroll reveal is not a thesis'; scroll-driven only when the scroll relationship carries meaning, with fallback; `will-change` only during animation; loops stop offscreen/hidden; reduced motion = fewer and gentler. Setup requires `"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/impeccable" context` which downloads a self-contained binary on first run (may be blocked by the proxy; the skill documents the fallback: read PRODUCT.md/DESIGN.md directly) and expects PRODUCT.md/DESIGN.md in the project. Stack assumption: writes production code in the repo; a 'design detector hook' runs after UI file edits. Gap: nothing maps to Elementor; PRODUCT.md/DESIGN.md should be generated from the plugin's token sheet and kept under the site's build folder so `critique`/`polish` have context.
findings.breaks_when: `impeccable context` cannot download its binary and the agent stalls instead of taking the documented fallback; `bolder`/`overdrive`/`delight` are run on an Operate surface (booking) and add decoration to a transactional flow; `optimize.md`'s `` example is copied onto the hero.
findings.how_to_apply: elementor-design: write PRODUCT.md (client, audience, languages, booking engine, constraints incl. the 95 gate) and DESIGN.md (the §1 token sheet) per site; invoke `impeccable critique`/`polish`/`typeset`/`layout` on screenshots + rendered CSS; set the mode per template (home = Persuade, booking/checkout/account = Operate, blog = Read, gallery = Experience). elementor-motion: cite `animate.md` timing table as the second reference beside Emil's.
findings.how_to_verify: `impeccable critique` on a built page returns heuristic scores with concrete fixes that are expressible as Global Class changes; after applying, inspect.mjs FAIL count does not rise and Lighthouse is within spread.

findings.claim: perception-first-design (`pfd`) is the only installed skill that reasons about conversion and cognition; use Mode 2 (solve) to derive the booking/enquiry/shop flows and Mode 1 (evaluate) on the published URL; its layer rules reinforce the plugin's font/colour budget.
findings.detail: Three modes with auto-detection: Mode 1 Evaluation (URL/screenshot/HTML -> walk L0-L4, score; corpus-backed via `corpus/core/tier2-prompt-template.md` + `corpus/heuristics/universal/{foundation,l1..l4}-rules.yaml`), Mode 2 Derivation (`/perception-first-design:solve`: Rule Zero no solution until R1-R5 requirements are derived bottom-up, each with citations), Mode 3 Analysis (`:analyze`, 'what happens if' cascades). Layer content directly relevant: L0 cognitive load (3-5 chunks; delete fields, progressive disclosure, 'clean background noise users never notice: inconsistent spacing, off-system colors'); L1 first impression (50 ms; hero = thesis; audit uncanny AI photos and 'uncanny animation timing'); L2 processing fluency ('2 fonts max. 3-4 colors. Consistent spacing', 'Lighthouse score and lived fluency are correlated but not identical'); L3 perception bias (design for analytics not surveys; fix visual coherence before copy when trust is low); L4 decision architecture (demonstrate don't describe: interactive availability/price preview beats a paragraph; 'near-term actions get concrete language: buy now'; fewer options at decision points, not in browse/reference contexts). Side effect: the skill mandates appending to `references/insights-log.md` inside its own plugin folder after every analysis (harmless, but it writes files). Corpus has `design-systems/web-frameworks` only (no WordPress/Elementor profile seen). Stack assumption: none (artefact-agnostic), which is why it fits.
findings.breaks_when: Mode 2 is skipped and the booking flow is copied from a competitor (the skill's 'competitive copying' anti-pattern), producing a 7-field enquiry form above the fold on mobile; or Mode 1 is run with the corpus on every page (slow) instead of a quick 5-layer scan.
findings.how_to_apply: elementor-design: for every transactional template (room/villa booking, water-park tickets, restaurant reservation, forum sign-up) run `/perception-first-design:solve` with the problem stated as user experience; convert R1-R5 into the section spec (field count, option count at decision points, demonstrate-price component, CTA register in Greek and English); run `:evaluate` on the published home and booking URLs in the Critique phase and keep the L-layer flags in the handover.
findings.how_to_verify: Derivation output lists R1-R5 with citations and a solution that satisfies all five; the built booking page has <= 3-5 simultaneous choices at the decision point, one primary CTA, price/availability visible without a paragraph; evaluate run flags nothing at L1/L2 (fonts <= 2, palette <= 8).
findings.correction: Reference the corpus as `<pfd plugin root>/corpus/...` (b70132db-.../corpus), not `skills/pfd/corpus`.

findings.claim: Accessibility: prefer ECC `accessibility` (WCAG 2.2: SC 2.5.8 target 24x24, 2.4.11 focus appearance, 3.3.7 redundant entry, 400% reflow) over the Anthropic design plugin's `accessibility-review` (WCAG 2.1 AA, 44x44 from 2.5.5); use `ux-copy` for bilingual CTA/error/empty-state copy; neither knows Elementor's widgets, so the new skills must name the Elementor controls that satisfy each criterion.
findings.detail: ECC `accessibility`: POUR steps; contrast 4.5:1 / 3:1; alt text; reflow to 400% zoom; 24x24 CSS px minimum target (2.5.8); keyboard reachability + visible focus (2.4.11); single-pointer alternatives for drag; descriptive errors with suggestions (3.3.3); redundant entry (3.3.7); Name/Role/Value; `aria-live` for dynamic status; anti-patterns: div-buttons, colour-only meaning, modals that do not trap and release focus (2.1.2), 'Image of' alt text. `design:accessibility-review` adds the audit output tables (Findings by principle, Color Contrast table, Keyboard Navigation table, Screen Reader table) and a testing approach (automated ~30%, keyboard-only, VoiceOver/NVDA, zoom 200%). `design:ux-copy`: CTAs start with a verb and are specific ('Create account' not 'Submit'); errors = what happened + why + how to fix; empty states = what this is + why empty + how to start; confirmations name the action ('Delete 3 files?' / 'Delete files' / 'Keep files'); output includes Localization Notes (character expansion: Greek strings run longer, so button widths and two-line headline rule must be checked in both languages). Elementor mapping to write: Pro Form field labels visible (not placeholder-only), error messages per field, honeypot not reCAPTCHA on load; Off-Canvas/Popup focus trap and Escape (Elementor popups: check `Prevent Closing on ESC` is off); Nav Menu keyboard focus styles via Global Class `:focus-visible`; icon-only buttons need `aria-label` (atomic `e-button` 'attributes' setting); Loop Grid empty state text; `e-image` alt from Media Library; touch targets via class padding (>= 44 px for primary CTA, >= 24 px minimum).
findings.breaks_when: The 2.1-only checklist is used and the site ships 20 px icon buttons and no focus appearance; placeholder-only labels in Pro Form; Greek CTA copy wraps to two lines in a fixed-width button and clips.
findings.how_to_apply: elementor-design: adopt ECC accessibility's checklist as the a11y gate and the design plugin's table format for the handover report; run `ux-copy` per template with the two languages and apply the Localization Notes to button width/headline checks at 390 px; add the Elementor control mapping above as a table.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse accessibility category >= 95 on home and booking; manual Tab pass reaches every control with a visible ring; Polylang-switched Greek page passes inspect.mjs `headline-lines` and no button text clips at 390 px.
findings.correction: In the new skill's a11y gate cite criteria from w3.org/TR/WCAG22, not from ECC's text: AA gate = 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (sticky header must not cover the focused control), 2.4.7 Focus Visible (A) for the ring, 2.5.8 Target Size 24x24 (keep the 44 px CTA as a house rule), 2.5.7 Dragging (slider/gallery needs a non-drag alternative), 3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A), 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (forum login). Mention 2.4.13 Focus Appearance only as AAA/optional.

findings.claim: `make-interfaces-feel-better` and `frontend-design-direction` (ECC) hold the small polish rules and the content-state contract that translate one-to-one into Global Class CSS and Loop/Form states; their evidence checker is a reusable handover gate format.
findings.detail: make-interfaces-feel-better: concentric radius `outer = inner + padding`; optical alignment of icons; borders for separation, layered transparent shadows only for things that float; `text-wrap: balance` on headings/short titles, `text-wrap: pretty` on body/captions, neither on long prose; `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for prices/counters; image inset outline `outline: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.1); outline-offset: -1px` (neutral, never brand-tinted); motion: transitions for state changes, keyframes only for one-shot entrances; enter = opacity + small translateY (+ optional blur), exit shorter (~150 ms), press `scale(0.96)`, icon swaps cross-fade; never `transition: all` or `will-change: all`, use `transition-property: transform, background-color, box-shadow; transition-duration: 150ms; transition-timing-function: ease-out`; hit areas >= 40x40, ideally 44x44, expanded with a pseudo-element without overlapping. frontend-design-direction: choose purpose/audience/tone/one memorable detail/constraints before building; content-state table with trigger, feedback and safe next action for Loading, Empty, Error, Partial, Success, Permission ('unavailable test access is an untested state, not N/A'); anti-patterns: purple gradients, blobs, cards inside cards, oversized hero copy, a dependency for a flourish; rendered finish gate at target viewports with keyboard, focus, contrast, reduced motion, touch targets, long content; `scripts/check-evidence.js <report.json>` validates a record with `contract`, `targetViewports` (e.g. `["390x844","1440x900"]`, each needing a matching `renderedEvidence[].viewport` + `artifact` file + `observation`), `accessibility`/`responsive` `{status:"pass", evidence}`, `contentStates` for all six. Stack assumption: component code (tokens in CSS variables, Tailwind); nothing WordPress-specific, which is fine because every rule is plain CSS.
findings.breaks_when: Rules are applied per widget instead of in Global Classes (per-widget CSS is the thing the plugin bans); `text-wrap: balance` is set on long Greek paragraphs (reflow cost); the handover claims states that were never exercised (booking with no availability, empty cart, form error).
findings.how_to_apply: elementor-design: put the polish rules into the base Global Classes (`btn-primary`, `card`, `heading-display`, `price`) and the Defaults; adopt the six content states as required rows in the page spec for Loop Grid (empty), Pro Form (error/success), booking widget (loading/partial/permission); emit the evidence JSON per page with screenshots at 390x844 and 1440x900 and run `node <ecc>/skills/frontend-design-direction/scripts/check-evidence.js report.json` as part of handover.
findings.how_to_verify: `check-evidence.js` exits 0 on the handover record and non-zero when a viewport artefact is missing; computed styles of `.price` show `tabular-nums`; no `transition: all` in post-N.css or Custom Code (grep).

findings.claim: `animation-vocabulary` is the shared naming layer between client brief and build; elementor-motion should pair each glossary term with its Elementor capability and budget verdict so 'the thing where numbers count up' is answered with a decision, not a widget.
findings.detail: The skill is a reverse-lookup glossary (Emil Kowalski) returning the exact term with a one-line definition, e.g. Fade in, Slide in, Scale in, Pop in, Reveal (clip-path/mask), Stagger, Orchestration, Crossfade, Morph, Shared element transition, Layout animation, Accordion/Collapse, Scroll reveal, Scroll-driven animation, Parallax, Page transition, View transition, Hover effect, Press/Tap feedback, Hold to confirm, Drag, Rubber-banding, Shake, Ripple, Marquee, Loop, Pulse, Float, Idle animation, Blur, Clip-path, Before/after slider, Line drawing, Text morph, Skeleton/Shimmer, Number ticker, Tabular numbers, Typewriter, plus performance terms (Compositing, will-change, Layout thrashing) and principles (Frequency of use, Reduced motion). Capability map to write in elementor-motion (term -> where -> verdict): Scroll reveal -> below fold, Interaction or CSS+IO, once, <= 2 Interactions per page -> allowed; Stagger -> CSS `animation-delay` per child 50-90 ms, <= 8 children -> allowed below fold; Hover effect / Press feedback -> Global Class state variant, `(hover:hover)` gated, scale .96-.97 -> allowed everywhere incl. header; Accordion -> atomic Accordion or `grid-template-rows 0fr->1fr` -> allowed; Parallax -> CSS `view()` drift <= 8%, never on the hero image on mobile -> below fold only; Scroll-driven animation (scrub/pin) -> desktop only via matchMedia, <= 1-2 sections, self-hosted GSAP -> owner OK; Marquee -> one per page, CSS linear loop, pause on hover/reduced motion, never `setInterval` -> allowed below fold; Number ticker -> never the Counter widget (7.5 KB + jquery-numerator); CSS 'Rolling figures' with tabular-nums -> allowed below fold; Typewriter / Text morph -> never as hero heading (Animated Headline is a blocker) -> banned above fold; Pulse / Float / Idle loops -> banned (anti-slop 'flag any instance'); Page transition / View transition -> `@view-transition { navigation: auto }` cross-document, 480 ms, off under reduced motion -> allowed (verify cache-plugin HTML rewriting does not break it); Shared element -> same mechanism with `view-transition-name` on the card image and the hero image -> allowed; Skeleton/Shimmer -> only for genuinely async content (booking calendar) -> allowed; Hold to confirm -> destructive actions in My Account -> allowed; Drag/Rubber-banding -> native `scroll-snap` row first, anime.js `createDraggable` only below fold -> owner OK; Lottie/3D/video hero -> blockers per rules 3-4/13.
findings.breaks_when: A client asks for 'the counting numbers like on the other hotel's site' and the builder drops the Pro Counter widget into the stats band (jquery-numerator + 7.5 KB chunk) or an Animated Headline into the hero (LCP span, blocker).
findings.how_to_apply: elementor-motion: include the term -> capability -> verdict table; when a brief or Figma prototype names or shows an effect, invoke `anthropic-skills:animation-vocabulary` to fix the term, then read the verdict row; offer the owner the 'below the fold' or 'desktop only' version when the verdict is owner OK.
findings.how_to_verify: Every effect in a brief maps to a row; the built page's network log has no `jquery-numerator`, `swiper`, `lottie`, `three`, `gsap` before LCP; at most one marquee; zero infinite `@keyframes` on indicators (grep post-N.css and Custom Code).

findings.claim: ECC motion-foundations / motion-patterns / motion-advanced are React + motion/react only ("use client", AnimatePresence, useScroll, Reorder); do not delegate to them, only harvest their token numbers and three behavioural rules.
findings.detail: Hard rules in the files: 'Use motion/react only', '"use client" is required', 'initial must match server output' (hydration), 'All token values come from motionTokens'; patterns are JSX (`<motion.div whileInView ... viewport={{ once: true }}>`, `AnimatePresence mode="wait"`, `layoutId`, `useMotionValue`/`useTransform`, `useAnimate`, `Reorder.Group`). Numbers worth keeping as a cross-check against Emil/tasteskill: durations instant 0.08 s, fast 0.18, normal 0.35, slow 0.6, crawl 1.0; easings smooth `[0.22, 1, 0.36, 1]` (same curve as tasteskill `--ease-out`), sharp `[0.4, 0, 0.2, 1]` (the framework default tasteskill rejects), bounce `[0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1]` (overshoot: banned on UI); distances 4/8/16/24/48 px; scale subtle .98 / press .95 / pop 1.04; springs snappy {300,30}, gentle {120,14}, bouncy {400,10}, instant {600,35}, release {200,20}; stagger 0.05-0.10 s; exit always defined with enter; scroll reveals `once: true`; infinite animations must pause on `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'`; swipe = offset AND velocity (offset > 120 px or velocity > 500); `isLowEnd()` = `navigator.hardwareConcurrency <= 4` (do not use as a gate: Lighthouse reports the host machine's cores, and the moto g emulation is CPU-throttled, not core-limited). Nothing here is enqueueable in WordPress without a React build; the equivalent for Elementor is CSS variables in the kit and the Global Class states.
findings.breaks_when: An agent follows 'motion-foundations: load this skill before any animation work' and tries to install motion/react into the Inglelandi child theme, adding a framework bundle (Motion is not tiny; design-taste-frontend itself says so) to every page.
findings.how_to_apply: In elementor-motion's 'Do not load' list: `ecc:motion-foundations`, `ecc:motion-patterns`, `ecc:motion-advanced` (React). Keep three rules in the house policy: define exit with enter, reveal once, pause loops when hidden/offscreen.
findings.how_to_verify: Grep the child theme and Custom Code for `motion/react`, `framer-motion`, `AnimatePresence`: none. The plugin's SKILL.md names the three skills under 'not for this stack'.

findings.claim: Delegation mechanics: the review skills need files and file:line, Elementor has a database and a URL; the new skills must define a 'page snapshot' workspace per page so review-animations, improve-animations, find-animation-opportunities, design-motion-principles audit and inspect.mjs can run, and must state the tool availability caveats of this machine.
findings.detail: Snapshot recipe to write into elementor-motion/elementor-design (read-only against the site): `curl -A '<mobile Chrome UA>' https://<site>/<page>/ -o snapshot/<page>/index.html` (detect WAF/challenge pages per sites-in-the-wild rule 1); fetch every same-origin stylesheet (`post-N.css`, kit CSS, `frontend.min.css`) and script URL listed in the HTML into `snapshot/<page>/css|js/`; export Pro Custom Code snippets via `novamira/elementor-get-content` or the Custom Code list and the child theme files via the read side of `write-file` into `snapshot/site/custom-code/` and `snapshot/site/theme/`; `_elementor_data` JSON via `elementor-get-content` into `snapshot/<page>/tree.json` for the lint; screenshots at 390/768/1440 via `node <taste-skill>/scripts/inspect.mjs <url>` (needs Chrome; `CHROME_PATH` is empty here and lighthouse is not installed in this session, so install Chromium or use the chrome-devtools MCP `take_screenshot` + `lighthouse_audit`). Then run the review skills on `snapshot/` and map each `file:line` back to its Elementor location (Custom Code snippet id, Global Class name, element id = `data-id`). Node v22.22.0 and python3 are present (tasteskill scripts need Node 22+, ui-ux-pro-max needs python3). `extract-design-system <url>` needs `npx playwright install chromium` (network, large download) and `web-design-guidelines` fetches its rules live from `raw.githubusercontent.com` on every run; both are optional. `assets.mjs` needs network, no keys.
findings.breaks_when: The reviewer is given a live URL (it declines or guesses), or snapshots are taken through a WAF challenge page (7 of 32 profiled sites served one) and the review runs on the wrong HTML; screenshots are skipped because Chrome is missing and the look loop silently degrades to reading CSS.
findings.how_to_apply: Add a `scripts/snapshot.sh <url> <out_dir>` to elementor-motion (curl with mobile UA, 403/challenge detection, asset fetch, HTML-to-asset list) and document the Chrome/Playwright requirements in the plugin README 'Requirements' next to the existing Lighthouse note; have the Critique agents refuse to review without a snapshot.
findings.how_to_verify: `snapshot.sh` on a dev site produces index.html with `elementorFrontendConfig`, >= 1 post-N.css, tree.json with top-level ids matching `data-id`s in the HTML; `review-animations` then cites `snapshot/.../custom-code/<id>.css:<line>`.
findings.correction: README 'Requirements': Chrome via `CHROME_PATH=<shim --no-sandbox>` (path above) or chrome-devtools MCP; Lighthouse via `npx -y lighthouse@13` or MCP `lighthouse_audit`; snapshot.sh also saves the `#elementor-interactions-data` JSON and every `[data-interaction-id]` as `snapshot/<page>/interactions.json`.

findings.claim: Do-not-route list: four installed skill families have names that invite misuse for Elementor design work and must be excluded explicitly: liquid-glass-design (iOS 26 SwiftUI/UIKit only), ECC taste / taste-application / taste-distillation (music-video grading and cutting), taste-skill-v1 and the 87 KB skills/synced `design-taste-frontend` v2-experimental (dial-driven, Tailwind/Motion/GSAP, 'motion claimed, motion shown'), and ui-ux-pro-max `design` (Gemini logo/CIP/banner generation needing GEMINI_API_KEY).
findings.detail: liquid-glass-design: `.glassEffect()`, `GlassEffectContainer`, `UIGlassEffect`, WidgetKit; zero web content. Any web 'glass' request is answered by tasteskill's house rule (no backdrop blur panels, no floating pill nav; `glass` WARN when > 1 blurred surface) and, if the brand insists, by v2-exp §5's recipe (1 px inner border, inset highlight, `prefers-reduced-transparency` solid fallback) limited to one sticky header; `backdrop-filter` is a per-frame GPU cost on phones. ECC taste*: 'angelcore / cloud-trance / hyperpop' video direction, LUTs, cut rhythm; name collision only. taste-skill-v1: DESIGN_VARIANCE 8, MOTION_INTENSITY 6 by default, 'Motion-Engine Bento Paradigm (Perpetual Motion)'. skills/synced design-taste-frontend (v2-exp): three dials, GSAP sticky-stack/horizontal-pan skeletons, Motion whileInView, Three.js allowed, CWV targets looser than the plugin's. ui-ux-pro-max `design`: logo/CIP/icon/social-photo generation via Gemini scripts (external API, credits) and slides; its `ui-styling` is shadcn/Tailwind. The useful parts of ui-ux-pro-max are `search.py` domains and `design-system` tokens (finding 9), not `design`.
findings.breaks_when: The Skill tool is invoked by a partial name match ('taste', 'design', 'glass') and the agent spends the Research budget on SwiftUI or video grading, or applies v1's perpetual-motion bento to a hotel home page (every card an infinite loop).
findings.how_to_apply: List these exact skill names under 'Not for Elementor sites' in both new SKILL.md files, with the one-line reason and the replacement skill; in the agents' instructions name the allowed skills explicitly rather than by topic.
findings.how_to_verify: Grep the plugin for each excluded name: present only in the exclusion section; a test brief mentioning 'glass header' routes to tasteskill house rule + one-sticky-bar recipe, not to liquid-glass-design.

findings.claim: The ECC `design-system` skill and the Anthropic `design:design-system` / `design-handoff` skills offer audit formats (10-dimension visual score incl. 'Animation: purposeful or gratuitous', AI-slop detection list; component spec tables with states and a11y; dev handoff spec) that fit the Critique and Handover phases; the plugin's existing Design System ZIP export is the Elementor-native equivalent of their token files.
findings.detail: ECC design-system: Mode 2 Visual Audit scores 0-10 on colour consistency, typography hierarchy, spacing rhythm, component consistency, responsive, dark mode, animation, accessibility, density, polish, each with file:line fixes; Mode 3 slop list ('gratuitous gradients', 'purple-to-blue defaults', 'glass morphism cards with no purpose', 'excessive animations on scroll', 'generic hero with centered text over stock gradient', 'sans-serif stack with no personality'); Mode 1 generates DESIGN.md + design-tokens.json + design-preview.html (and 'researches 3 competitor sites via browser MCP'). design:design-system: token categories incl. Motion (durations, easings) and component docs with Variants/States (default, hover, active, disabled, loading, error)/Accessibility/Do-Don't; design-handoff: layout, tokens, props, interaction states, breakpoints, edge cases, animation details from a Figma URL or description. Stack assumption: codebase tokens (CSS/Tailwind/styled-components). Elementor mapping: design-tokens.json -> Variables (colour/font/size) and the v3 kit; component docs -> one Global Class per component with its hover state variant; the 'Motion' token category -> the kit `:root` eases/durations; the preview HTML -> replaced by the Elementor 'styleguide' page built from the classes (also what Element Manager and the Design System export need). The 10-dimension score is a good shape for the elementor-ux-reviewer agent's report alongside the Lighthouse table.
findings.breaks_when: Mode 1 is run as the token source (it researches competitors and proposes its own palette, over-producing tokens the §1 budget must then prune) instead of tasteskill's dealt direction + pruning; the preview HTML is mistaken for a deliverable.
findings.how_to_apply: elementor-design: use design:design-system 'document' format for each Global Class (variants, states, a11y, do/don't) and the ECC 10-dimension score as the review rubric; export tokens as the Design System ZIP and, for the client, a design-tokens.json derived from `GET /wp-json/elementor/v1/global-classes` plus Variables; attach design-handoff's spec sections to the client package in design-to-elementor §7 Handover step 5.
findings.how_to_verify: Every Global Class in `_elementor_global_classes` has a documented row (variant, states, a11y); the review report shows 10 scores with file/element references; the Design System ZIP re-imports on a fresh site and the styleguide page renders identically (screenshot diff).

findings.claim: GSAP is 100% free for commercial use including every former Club plugin (SplitText, MorphSVG, ScrollSmoother, DrawSVG, ScrollTrigger) since 3.13 (public npm), so tasteskill's `gsap@3.15.0` pins are licence-clean; the only cost is bytes and bootup, and the real numbers are gsap 28.3 KB gz + ScrollTrigger 18.0 KB gz + SplitText 3.7 KB gz
findings.detail: gsap.com/pricing: 'GSAP is now 100% free for all users, thanks to Webflow's support'; gsap.com/blog/3-13: 'GSAP is now 100% FREE including ALL of the bonus plugins like SplitText, MorphSVG, and all the others that were exclusively available to Club GSAP members ... even for commercial use' and 'install GSAP and all the bonus plugins directly from the public NPM repository'. jsdelivr `latest` = 3.15.0 (3.14.2, 3.14.1 before it). Measured from cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.15.0/dist/: gsap.min.js 72,927 raw / 28,268 gz; ScrollTrigger.min.js 44,575 / 17,998 gz; SplitText.min.js 7,732 / 3,658 gz. Lenis latest 1.3.27. The standard-license page body did not render in the fetched HTML, so any Webflow-competitor carve-out could not be read here; irrelevant for hotel/restaurant sites but say 'verify at gsap.com/standard-license' rather than quoting it.
findings.breaks_when: GSAP core + ScrollTrigger (46 KB gz) is enqueued on every page or before LCP: platonos already pays 1.78 s bootup for gsap + ScrollTrigger + SplitText (levers 7.6); 46 KB is a third of the 150 KB third-party budget before any site scripts.
findings.how_to_apply: elementor-motion: 'GSAP 3.15.x: free incl. all plugins (verified 2026-10-22); self-host `gsap.min.js` + only the plugins used in the child theme (`js/vendor/gsap/`), pin the version in the filename, enqueue per page with `strategy => defer` (or as a module), load after LCP, never Lenis/ScrollSmoother on mobile; count 46 KB gz against the budget'. Remove any 'Club-only' or 'licence pending' language.
findings.how_to_verify: `curl -sI https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.15.0/dist/SplitText.min.js` is 200 (public); the child-theme files' headers read 'GSAP 3.15.0 ... Subject to the terms at https://gsap.com/standard-license'; Lighthouse network log on a page using them shows one same-origin request each, none before LCP, bootup-time entry for them under 300 ms total.

findings.claim: Cache-plugin exclusion attributes are not interchangeable; the recipe->placement table must give the per-plugin truth: LiteSpeed honours `data-no-optimize`, `data-no-defer`, `data-cfasync="false"` and any `type` other than `text/javascript` (so `type="module"` is never deferred or delayed); WP Rocket honours `nowprocket`; Perfmatters documents only URL/string exclusion lists (optional 15 s timeout, off by default); FlyingPress matches any keyword against the whole `<script>` tag (src, id, inline)
findings.detail: LiteSpeed source src/optimize.cls.php (master): in the JS parser `if (!empty($attrs['data-no-optimize'])) continue;`, `if (!empty($attrs['data-cfasync']) && $attrs['data-cfasync'] === 'false') continue;`, `if (!empty($attrs['type']) && $attrs['type'] != 'text/javascript') continue;`, `nomodule` skipped; in `_js_defer`: `data-no-defer` bypass, native `defer` kept in Deferred mode but still queued in Delayed mode ('a native defer would run before its delayed inline data'); Delayed mode rewrites to `type="litespeed/javascript" data-src=`. Docs: 'JS Delayed Includes deprecated as of v7.9.2 ... use JS Deferred/Delayed Excludes to list any scripts that must run early'. WP Rocket docs: 'Programmatically by adding the nowprocket attribute to inline scripts or scripts in external files'. Perfmatters docs: exclusions by 'source URL (example.js), or ... a unique string from that script', 'timeout that will automatically load scripts after 15 seconds ... optional and off by default', plus `perfmatters_delay_js_exclusions` filter; no attribute documented. FlyingPress docs: 'FlyingPress checks the full <script> tag — src, id, and inline content. You can exclude a script by entering any partial keyword'; 'Load after interaction ... not suitable if your site has sliders, animations, menus ... in the above-the-fold area'. WordPress: `wp_enqueue_script_module()` since 6.5, `$args` added 6.9 with only `in_footer` and `fetchpriority` ('auto'|'low'|'high') — no way to add `nowprocket`/`data-no-optimize` through it; `wp_enqueue_script(..., ['strategy' => 'defer'])` plus a `script_loader_tag` filter is the route when an attribute is required.
findings.breaks_when: The reveal module is printed as `type="module"` and the site runs Perfmatters or FlyingPress 'delay all': both can delay it (FlyingPress only skips by keyword, Perfmatters by URL/string), so `.js [data-reveal]{opacity:0}` content stays invisible until the first tap unless the filename is in the exclusion list; conversely the inline `<script>document.documentElement.classList.add('js')</script>` gate gets delayed too, which is actually the safe failure (content stays visible).
findings.how_to_apply: In elementor-motion's placement table add a column 'exclusion per cache plugin': LiteSpeed = `type="module"` or `data-no-optimize="1"`; WP Rocket = `nowprocket`; Perfmatters = add the file name (`reveal.js`) and the inline string (`classList.add('js')`) to Delay exclusions, do not rely on attributes; FlyingPress = add the keyword `inglelandi-child/js` (or the handle id) to Exclude. The `html.js` gate script must be excluded everywhere OR the hidden state must also be gated on a class the module itself adds after load (`html.js.motion-ready`), so delay never hides content.
findings.how_to_verify: View source after cache warm: the reveal module tag still has `type="module"` and its original `src` (not `data-src`/`litespeed/javascript`, not `type="rocketlazyloadscript"`, not `data-perfmatters-type`/`pmdelayedscript`); with JS disabled every below-fold section is visible; on a cold load without touching, the reveal still plays within 3 s.

findings.claim: LCP candidacy facts settle two open questions: Chrome never counts an element with opacity 0 as an LCP candidate and never re-evaluates size/position changes, so (a) any CSS hidden state (`elementor-invisible`, `.js [data-reveal]{opacity:0}`, `translateY(105%)` inside overflow clip) on the hero pushes LCP to the moment it becomes visible, while (b) a JS-applied entrance (Interaction `load`, `gsap.from`) on an already-painted hero does not move LCP but produces a visible flash, and (c) the 'Receding hero' exit-range scroll timeline (identity transform at progress 0) does not change the candidate
findings.detail: web.dev/articles/lcp: elements not considered include 'Elements with an opacity of 0, that are invisible to the user' and 'An element with a background image loaded using the url() function'; 'changes to an element's size or position don't generate new LCP candidates. Only the element's initial size and position in the viewport is considered'; `` is. Lighthouse constants.js: mobile = 412x823, DPR 1.75, moto g power UA, `throttling.mobileSlow4G`, `throttlingMethod: 'simulate'`, no reduced-motion or Save-Data emulation. Consequence for the plugin's lint: the dangerous pattern is any rule that makes the LCP node start at opacity 0 / visibility hidden / fully clipped before JS, whichever tool writes it; a transform-only, opacity-1 start state is LCP-neutral (still banned above the fold by rule 13 for UX, but it is not a score bug).
findings.breaks_when: A reviewer approves a hero Interaction because 'Lighthouse LCP did not move' and ships the flash; or rejects the Receding hero on score grounds it does not have (the right objection is INP/TBT on phones and the rule-13 UX policy, not LCP).
findings.how_to_apply: elementor-motion 'Lighthouse facts' box: 'opacity-0 at first paint = LCP waits; transform-only start = LCP unchanged but flash; scroll-driven exit timelines on the hero are LCP-neutral — measure TBT/INP, not LCP'. The lint flags for the first container and header: any `opacity:0`, `visibility:hidden`, `clip-path: inset(... 100% ...)` or `translate*(>=100%)` reaching the LCP node from kit CSS, Custom Code, Global Class or inline style; and separately any `[data-interaction-id]`/`_animation`/`gsap.from` there as a UX finding.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse 3x on a dev page with (1) a `.js .hero{opacity:0}` rule: LCP render delay jumps by the script delay; (2) a `load` Interaction on the h1: LCP unchanged within spread, filmstrip shows h1 visible, then gone, then fading; (3) the Receding hero timeline: LCP and CLS unchanged within spread.

findings.claim: Default `--allow` list for tasteskill's inspector on Elementor pages must also cover the inspector's motion-expectation rules, or every plugin-compliant page fails for being static: `still-page`, `scene-not-started`, `scene-not-live`, `many-scenes`, `scene-heavy`, `reduced-hidden` (desktop widths) in addition to `few-pictures` and `no-footage`
findings.detail: rules.mjs RULE_IDS includes 'still-page', 'scene-not-started', 'scene-not-live', 'many-scenes', 'scene-heavy', 'reduced-hidden', 'no-poster', 'long-pin', 'side-scroll'; inspect.mjs:239 runs the `reduced-hidden` check whenever a width >= 1100 is requested unless allowed; motion.md:22 says the inspector 'fails it under eight elements'.
