The inspector's `motion` block in report.json counts `elements`, `css`, `transitions`, `scripted`, `videos` (seen in the test run: all 0 on a static page). Keep the layout/typography/colour rules live: `headline-lines`, `font-count`, `size-count`, `contrast`, `hairline`, `outlined-box`, `gradient`, `shadow`, `all-centred`, `overflow`, `small-text`, `measure` are exactly the house rules the plugin wants as Global Class defaults. Expect `hairline`/`outlined-box` noise from Pro Form borders and `e-divider` (open question stands) and record each `--allow` reason in the handover.
findings.breaks_when: The agent runs inspect.mjs without the allow list, reads 'still-page' / 'scene-not-started' FAILs and adds hero motion or scenes to satisfy them, which is the exact failure mode of finding 3.
findings.how_to_apply: elementor-design gate command: `node <taste-skill>/scripts/inspect.mjs <url> --widths 1440,768,390 --allow few-pictures,no-footage,still-page,scene-not-started,scene-not-live,many-scenes,scene-heavy,reduced-hidden --json`; treat any remaining FAIL as a design finding, never as a reason to add motion or pictures beyond the §4 image budget.
findings.how_to_verify: On a plugin-compliant static-hero page the JSON `judge` output has zero FAIL ids outside the allow list; removing `still-page` from the list reproduces the FAIL.

findings.claim: Cross-document View Transitions ('Page to page' and 'Shared element' rows) are a safe progressive enhancement: same-origin only, both documents must carry `@view-transition { navigation: auto }`, supported in Chrome/Edge 126+ and Safari 18.2+, not in Firefox; unsupported browsers just navigate; Polylang per-language domains break it (cross-origin)
findings.detail: MDN: '@view-transition ... opt in the current and destination documents ... For a cross-document view transition to work, the current and destination documents of the navigation need to be on the same origin'; 'provided the navigation is same-origin, without cross-origin redirects, and its navigationType is traverse, push, or replace'; examples use 0.4 s animations. Chrome docs (via search, case study): Chrome 126+, Firefox not supported; one 2026 guide lists Safari 18.2. Zero JS, zero bytes beyond a few CSS lines; nothing loads before LCP; the plugin's CSS exclusions (keep `@view-transition` and `view-transition-name` out of RUCSS/UCSS removal — they are not 'used' by any element in the static page scan) are the only cache interaction, beside the open question on HTML rewriting.
findings.breaks_when: LiteSpeed UCSS strips the `@view-transition` rule or `::view-transition-*` pseudo-elements as unused; a Polylang setup with one domain per language makes the language switch cross-origin (no transition, no harm); a 480 ms root crossfade on a slow phone feels like latency — keep <= 300 ms and only the shared image.
findings.how_to_apply: elementor-motion row 'Page to page': kit Custom CSS `@view-transition { navigation: auto } ::view-transition-old(root), ::view-transition-new(root) { animation-duration: 240ms } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { @view-transition { navigation: none } }`; shared element via `view-transition-name` on the card image (Global Class) and the hero image; add `@view-transition`, `::view-transition` to the UCSS/RUCSS safelist; test in Chrome and Safari, document Firefox as plain navigation.
findings.how_to_verify: Chrome 126+: navigate card -> detail, DevTools Animations panel shows `::view-transition-group(...)`; view-source of the cached page still contains `@view-transition`; Firefox navigates without transition and without console errors; Lighthouse unchanged.
tools: Pro Custom Code / kit Custom CSS

findings.claim: After a programmatic `elementor-set-content`, Elementor's Interactions postmeta cache can be stale: the frontend reads `elementor-interactions-cache` postmeta first and rebuilds it only through `elementor/document/after_save`, so an element whose `interactions[]` was added or removed by the MCP write may keep the old behaviour until the document is re-saved
findings.detail: interactions-frontend-handler.php `collect_document_interactions()`: `$cached_rows = $interactions_postmeta->load_content($post_id); if (empty($cached_rows)) { $cached_rows = ...process_content(...) }` — the cache is only rebuilt when empty; module.php hooks `elementor/document/save/data` -> `handle_interactions` and `elementor/document/after_save` -> `handle_interactions_cache`; cache/interactions-postmeta.php `META_KEY = 'elementor-interactions-cache'`, `delete_post_meta` when the new set is empty else `update_post_meta`. Whether Novamira's `elementor-set-content` goes through Document::save (and fires `after_save`) is unknown; `elementor-clear-document-cache` purges CSS, not this meta.
findings.breaks_when: The lint removes an Interaction from the first container via `elementor-set-content`, the review sees a clean `_elementor_data`, but the live page still prints the old `#elementor-interactions-data` JSON and animates the hero.
findings.how_to_apply: In design-to-elementor §5 'Sequence per page' add after `elementor-set-content`: `wp post meta delete <id> elementor-interactions-cache` (or a Novamira meta ability if present, read-only check first with `wp post meta get`), then `elementor-clear-document-cache`, then fetch the page and compare `#elementor-interactions-data` element ids with the tree's `interactions` owners.
findings.how_to_verify: Set an Interaction on a test element, save via editor, confirm meta exists; remove it via `elementor-set-content`; if the frontend JSON still lists the element id, the stale-cache path is real and the meta delete step is required.
